en.name: Sultaniye Fortress
description:
Following the conquest of Istanbul, Sultan Mehmed II ordered the construction of two fortresses on the narrowest point in order to control the Dardanelles; these fortresses face each other, one on the Anatolian side, and the other on the Thracian side. Located today in Çanakkale’s city centre, the fortress on the Anatolian side, Sultaniye Fortress, was built in 1463 under the supervision of Yakup Bey, one of Sultan Mehmed II’s generals. The fortress has been restored recently and its surrounding area has been reorganised and turned into a museum.  
Past the ticket office on the right is the Nusrat ship used for laying mines during the Battle of Çanakkale in 1915. The main entrance under a tower in the middle of the north side opens into the court. The Sultaniye Fortress, also known as Çimenlik Fortress, is composed of an outer fort, 110 x 160 m., and a three-storey inner castle of 30 x 42 m. and 20 m. high, along with two *masjid*s and a circular armoury. The outer wall is fortified with several towers and bastions and supports battlements. On entering the court one faces the inner fort straight ahead, and the round armoury to the left in the distance. The first *masjid* adjoins the tower, under which is the entrance today, and the upper part of its short minaret is in ruins. In the court between the outer fort and the inner castle is an open-air display of cannons and artillery from the First World War. The second *masjid* stands by the southwest corner of the inner castle and according to the inscription, it was built during the reign of Sultan Abdülaziz (1861-1876). The redoubts in the west part of the outer fort were built in the same period. On the landing in front of the main door of the inner castle there is a broken marble seat, on which, according to legend, Sultan Mehmed II sat. This inner castle is a very secure building with walls more than 7 m. thick; according to the writings of researchers, a 38’ cannon ball left only a small mark on its wall during the Battle of Çanakkale (1915); today it is used as an exhibition hall housing a display of weapons.  
Grelot, a 17th-century traveller, describes Sultaniye Fortress in detail and records that there were 28 large cannons that could shoot cannon balls to the opposite shore, and that Çanakkale was a large village behind the castle, with a population of 3000.

es.name: Fortaleza Sultaniye (Çimenlik)
description:
Después de conquistar Estambul, Mehmet II hizo levantar, en el punto donde las dos orillas del estrecho de los Daradanelos están más próximas, dos fortalezas, una en la costa de Tracia y la otra en la de Anatolia. Situada hoy en el centro de la ciudad de Çanakkale, la fortaleza Sultaniye, que está en la orilla de Anatolia, fue construida en 1463 bajo la supervisión de uno de los generales del sultán Mehmet II, Yakub Bey. La construcción ha sido restaurada recientemente, y sus alrededores, reformados, han sido convertidos en museo.  
Pasada la taquilla, a la derecha se ve el barco Nusrat, que se usó para colocar minas en la batalla de Çanakkale de 1915. Por la entrada principal, que se encuentra bajo una torre en medio del lado norte, se entra al patio. La fortaleza Sultaniye, también llamada fortaleza de Çimenlik, está compuesta por un recinto fortificado exterior (110 x 160 m), un castillo interior de tres pisos (30 x 42 m y 20 m de altura), dos *masyid*s y una armería circular. La muralla exterior, almenada, está fortificada con numerosas torres y baluartes. Al entrar en el patio, se ve de frente el castillo interior; a lo lejos, a la izquierda, queda la armería redonda. El primer *masyid* se encuentra junto a la torre de entrada, y la parte superior del corto alminar está completamente derruida. En la explanada entre la muralla exterior y el castillo están expuestos cañones y artillería de la I Guerra Mundial. El otro *masyid* se levanta junto al ángulo suroeste del castillo y, según reza su inscripción, fue construida durante el mandato del sultán Abdülaziz (r. 1861-1876). Los reductos de la parte occidental de la muralla exterior se hicieron también en la misma época. En el rellano de la puerta principal del castillo hay un asiento roto de mármol en el que, según la leyenda, se sentaba Mehmet II. El castillo es un edificio bien defendido, con muros de 7 m de grosor; según los escritos de algunos investigadores, la bala de un cañón del 38 dejó solo una pequeña marca en el muro durante la batalla de Çanakkale (1915). Hoy, el castillo es una sala de exposiciones donde se muestran armas.  
Un viajero del siglo XVII, Grelot, nos describe la fortaleza Sultaniye con todo detalle. Cuenta que en ella había 28 grandes cañones que podían disparar proyectiles a la orilla opuesta y que Çanakkale era un gran pueblo de 3.000 habitantes situado detrás del castillo.

ar.name: صهاريج الأغالبة.
description:
يضم الموقع صهريجين شيدا بطريقة البناء نفسها، من الحجر غير المهذب المغطى بطلاء كتيم. وقد دعمت السطوح الداخلية بدعامات ساندة داخلية وخارجية متناوبة لمقاومة ضغط الماء، وهي دعامات شبه أسطوانية تعلوها أنصاف كريات، مما يمزج الناحية الجمالية بالبراعة التقنية.  
يتألف النظام من ثلاثة أجهزة أساسية:  
الحوض الصغير وقطره 17 متراً، وهو مدعوم بسبعة عشر دعامة داخلية وستة وعشرين دعامة خارجية. وتصل طاقته الاستيعابية إلى أربعة آلالاف متر مربع. يلعب هذا الحوض دور حوض للتصفية يصله الماء أولا ليتخلص من الردميات التي يجرفها قبل أن ينسكب في الحوض الكبير.  
الحوض الكبير دائري، ويصل قطره إلى 128 متراً وعمقه إلى 4.8 أمتار، وقد تصل طاقته الاستيعابية إلى 57000 متر مربع؛ مما تطلب على الأقل 182 دعامة (118 سارية دعم خارجية و64 سارية دعم داخلية) ليتحمل الضغط ويضمن صلاحية المنشأة المخصصة لتخزين المياه الضرورية لحياة المدينة. ترتفع في منتصف الحوض ركيزة ضخمة متعددة الفصوص، كانت تعلوها في الماضي قبة استخدمت كجناح للاسترخاء.  
ينتهي المسار الطويل للمياه في خزانات الاغتراف المكونة من خزانين متوازيين مستندين بشكل متعامد على الأحواض. و قد تمت تغطيتهما بقبوة نصف اسطوانية ذات أقواس مزدوجة مدعومة بركائز. وتمكن ستة فوهات موجودة في قمم القبب من ضخ المياه.

إنها المنجزات المائية الأكثر شهرة في العالم الإسلامي؛ وهي صهاريج كانت تنتمي إلى مجموعة من الأحواض التي يصل عددها إلى 15 حوض كانت تتواجد خارج الأسوار، وكانت تزود مدينة القيروان. وقد جعلت الضخامة المدهشة لهذه الإنشاءات مدينةَ القيروان تستحق تسمية "مدينة الخزانات". يتعلق الأمر بحوضين ذي شكل نصف دائري؛ كانا يُزوَّدان، عن طريق جهاز مبتكر لتصريف وجلب مياه الأمطار وروافد وادي مرقليل التي تسقط في المنخفض المجاور.
history: إن عدد الصهاريج الأغلبية اليوم اثنان، وهي تشكل جزءا من مجموعة تضم 15 حوضا،ً كانت تتواجد خارج أسوار المدينة، بنيت لتزود الساكنة بالمياه. وتعد هذه الصهاريج من بين المنشآت المائية الأكثر ضخامة في تاريخ العالم الإسلامي، مما جعل المدينة تستحق اسم "مدينة الخزانات" وتنتزع إعجاب المسافرين. وقد جرت تغذيتها عبر نظام بارع لتصريف مياه الأمطار ومياه روافد وادي مرقليل التي تنصب في الحوض المجاور. وكانت المياه تحبس بواسطة سدود صغيرة وقناة لجر المياه لتوصلهم بالحوض الصغير. وفي عام 350 هجري/961 ميلادي، شيد الخليفة الفاطمي المعز قناة مياه لتجميع منابع نهر الشريشيرة الواقع على بعد 40 كلم من القيروان.

en.name: Aghlabid Reservoirs.
description:
These two reservoirs were built using the same method. They are constructed of rubble and surfaced with a waterproof coating. The walls are consolidated by internal and external buttresses which alternate, thus providing maximum resistance against the water pressure. These buttresses are semi-cylindrical in shaped and topped with semi-spheres, combining aesthetics with technical performance.  
They are composed of three main sections:  
– The small reservoir measures 17 m in diameter and is reinforced by 17 internal and 26 external buttresses. Its holding capacity is 4,000 cubic metres. It is a filtering basin which receives the untreated water and rids it of most of the debris that it carries before decanting it into the large reservoir.  
– The large reservoir is circular in shape, measures 128 m in diameter and is 4.8 m deep. Its holding capacity is 57,000 cubic metres. No less than 182 buttresses were needed (118 external and 64 internal) to contain the pressure and guarantee the viability of the project, which was to store enough water for the needs of daily life in the town. A squat poly-foil pillar rises up from its centre. Formerly surmounted by a dome, it was used as a leisure pavilion.  
The water travels from here into two parallel dispensing water-tanks set perpendicular to the reservoirs. They are covered with barrel vaults held up by arch-beams that rest on pillars. Six openings at the top of the vaults allow the water to be drawn.

These hydraulic structures are the most famous in the Muslim world. They were among 15 pools outside the city walls that provided water to Kairouan. The imposing majesty of these installations earned Kairouan the epithet ‘city of water tanks’ in the Middle Ages. There are two semi-cylindrical pools supplied by an ingenious system for draining rainwater and the water from a nearby depression filled by tributaries of the *wadi* Merguelli.
history: The Aghlabid reservoirs, of which only two survive, were part of a group of about 15 reservoirs, located outside the city walls, which supplied the town with water. They are considered to be among the most important hydraulic works of the Muslim world. They provoked the admiration of travellers and led to the town being given the name 'city of the cisterns'. They were filled by draining rainwater as well as water from the tributaries of the *wadi* Merguelli, which flow in the surrounding lowlands. Its waters were harnessed by small dams and a conveyance canal which transported it to the small pool. In 350 (961), the Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz built an aqueduct that brought water from the Shreshira springs, located 40 km to the west of Kairouan.
keywords: Aghlabid; Umayyad; reservoirs; buttresses; filtering pools; aqueducts; hydraulic works; cisterns; leisure pavilion

es.name: Estanques de los Aglabíes.
description:
Se trata de dos estanques circulares, construidos siguiendo un mismo modelo. Son de morrillo recubierto con un enlucido impermeable. Las paredes están reforzadas por contrafuertes interiores y exteriores, que se alternan para resistir mejor la presión del agua. Son de forma semicilíndrica, rematada por una media esfera, lo que conjuga la estética con las cualidades técnicas.  
El sistema se compone de tres partes esenciales:  
–El estanque pequeño, de 17 m de diámetro, está reforzado por 17 contrafuertes interiores y 26 exteriores. Su capacidad es de 4.000 m3. Es un estanque de decantación, que recibe el agua en primer lugar y donde se depura de los residuos que acarrea antes de verterse en el estanque grande.  
–El estanque grande mide 128 m de diámetro y 4,8 m de profundidad: su capacidad puede alcanzar los 57.000 m3. Se necesitaron no menos de 182 contrafuertes (118 exteriores y 64 interiores) para resistir la presión del agua y garantizar la viabilidad de la obra, destinada al almacenamiento del agua necesaria para la vida de la ciudad. En medio del estanque se eleva un grueso pilar polilobulado, antaño rematado con una cúpula, que servía de pabellón de recreo.  
–El largo recorrido del agua termina en las cisternas de extracción, constituidas por dos depósitos paralelos adosados perpendicularmente a los estanques. Estas cisternas, cubiertas por bóvedas de cañón con arcos fajones sostenidos por pilares, disponen de seis aberturas, situadas en las cimas de las bóvedas para permitir la extracción del agua.

Estos estanques son la obra hidráulica más célebre del mundo musulmán. Integraban un conjunto de quince estanques situados extramuros y que abastecían la ciudad de Kairuán. Por su majestuosidad, estas instalaciones hicieron que Kairuán fuera conocida como la “ciudad de las cisternas”. Estos dos estanques circulares eran abastecidos por un ingenioso sistema de drenaje de las aguas de lluvia y de los afluentes del río Merguellil, que se vierten en la depresión cercana.
history: Los Estanques de los Aglabíes, actualmente dos, formaban parte de una quincena de estanques situados extramuros que abastecían de agua la ciudad. Se encuentran entre las obras hidráulicas más importantes de la historia del mundo musulmán. Han dado a la población el nombre de “ciudad de las cisternas” y han provocando la admiración de los viajeros. Estaban abastecidos por un ingenioso sistema de drenaje de las aguas de lluvia y de los afluentes del río *(wadi)* Merguellil, que se vertían en la depresión de los alrededores. Las aguas eran captadas por pequeños embalses y un canal de derivación que las conducía hasta el estanque pequeño. En 350 / 961, el califa fatimí al-Muizz edificó un acueducto para canalizar las aguas de los manantiales de Chréchira, a 40 km al oeste de Kairuán, hasta los aljibes de la ciudad.
keywords: aglabí; omeya; estanques; contrafuertes; estanque de decantación; acueducto; obra hidráulica; cisterna; pabellón de recreo
partner: Ministry of Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Bassins des Aghlabides.
description:
Il s'agit de deux bassins édifiés sur le même mode constructif. Ils sont en moellons, recouverts d'un enduit étanche. Les parois sont consolidées par des contreforts intérieurs et extérieurs qui s'alternent pour mieux résister à la pression de l'eau. Ceux-ci sont de forme semi-cylindrique et coiffés d'une demi-sphère, ce qui allie l'esthétique aux performances techniques.  
  
Le système se compose de trois organes essentiels :  
  
Le petit bassin, de 17 m de diamètre, est renforcé par 17 contreforts intérieurs et 26 extérieurs. Sa contenance est de 4 000 m3. C'est un bassin de décantation qui reçoit l'eau en premier. Là, elle est débarrassée des débris qu'elle charrie avant de se déverser dans le grand bassin.  
  
Le grand bassin, de forme circulaire, mesure 128 m de diamètre et 4,8 m de profondeur ; sa contenance peut atteindre 57 000 m3. Il a fallu pas moins de 182 contreforts (118 extérieurs et 64 intérieurs) pour contenir la pression et garantir la viabilité de l'ouvrage destiné au stockage des eaux nécessaires à la vie de la ville. Au milieu du bassin s'élève un gros pilier polylobé, jadis surmonté d'une coupole et qui servait de pavillon de loisir.  
  
Le long parcours des eaux se termine dans les citernes de puisage, constituées de deux réservoirs parallèles adossés perpendiculairement aux bassins. Elles sont couvertes de voûtes en berceau à arcs doubleaux soutenues par des piliers. Six ouvertures placées aux sommets des voûtes permettaient le puisage de l'eau.

Ce sont les ouvrages hydrauliques les plus célèbres du monde musulman. Ils faisaient partie d'une quinzaine de bassins qui se trouvaient extra-muros et qui approvisionnaient la ville de Kairouan. La majesté impressionnante de ces installations a valu à Kairouan au Moyen âge le nom de “ville des citernes”. Il s'agit de deux bassins de forme semi-cylindrique. Ils étaient alimentés par un astucieux système de drainage des eaux de pluies et des affluents de l'oued Merguellil qui se déversent dans la dépression environnante.
history: Les bassins aghlabides, aujourd'hui au nombre de deux, faisaient partie d'une quinzaine de bassins extra-muros qui alimentaient la ville en eau. Ils comptent parmi les ouvrages hydrauliques les plus importants de l'histoire du monde musulman. Ils ont valu à la ville son nom de “ville des citernes” et ont forcé l'admiration des voyageurs. Ils étaient alimentés par un astucieux système de drainage des eaux de pluie et des affluents de l'oued Merguellil qui se déversent dans la dépression environnante. Les eaux étaient captées par de petits barrages et un canal d'adduction qui les conduisait jusqu'au petit bassin. En 350 H / 961 J.-C., le calife fatimide al-Mouiz édifia un aqueduc pour capter les sources de Chréchira, à 40 km de Kairouan.
keywords: Aghlabide; omeyyade; bassins; contreforts; bassin de décantation; aqueduc; ouvrage hydraulique; citerne; pavillon de loisir.

en.name: Pottery Kilns in the North Theatre (Archaeological Site of Jerash)
description:
The **Pottery Kilns in the North Theatre** were identical in the construction of oval chambers and in some remains of misfired pottery vessels were found; together with the typical “Jerash Lamp” with its zoomorphic -type handle and oval-slipper shape, already known from the Byzantine kilns of the 6th century at the Hippodrome and elsewhere at Jerash. The history of Umayyad pottery production in Jerash, as illustrated by the Artemis kiln complex, is interesting from various points of view. It highlights the continuation of Jerash as a major centre of ceramic manufacture, Wares from here have been found over much of northern Jordan, in heavy competition with centres in other Decapolis cities especially during the late Byzantine period (see Umm Qays/Gadara and Tabaqat Fihl/Pella to name other known pottery markets on the east side of the Jordan while at Beisan/Scythopolis massive Umayyad kiln deposits have been excavated).  
It is only the Artemis Kiln Complex, which has been preserved as a representative of a lively trade, which did not lose its impetus until after the Abbasid period in the 4th/10th century. Then Jerash experienced a general decline in commercial activities and probably also in population, both being interrelated. Much of this permanent recession had to do with the  
shifting of the main trading routes between greater Syria and Iraq. Being bypassed, Jerash continued an existence of modest means due to reduction of trade and relied on smallholdings in  
agriculture and manufacturer catering to local needs.  
A few accounts show evidence of deliberate destruction. Also mentioned in records is that this occurred, it seems, during the  
Crusades when the long abandoned ruins of the Artemis and the Zeus Temples provided shelter for the Ayyubids and lastly, in the post-Crusader period, by the Mamluks. This state of an  
almost forgotten slumbering country town remained intact until the Ottoman rulers installed the Circassian population there in the 13th/19th century and Jerash, thought of even then as a  
town of ancient ruins, became once more a thriving place, as it is today.  
Still, a final word needs be said. The historical picture gleaned to date from the excavations (from the late 1920’s  
to the present) is distorted or at least unbalanced because the excavations have concentrated on monumental remains and public spaces rather than on ordinary dwellings and a general town  
plan.

es.name: Hornos de cerámica del Teatro Norte (Yacimiento arqueológico de Jerash)
description:
Los **Hornos de cerámica del Teatro Norte** eran idénticos en cuanto a la construcción de cámaras ovales. En algunos de ellos se han hallado restos de vasijas de alfarería mal cocidas, así como de la típica lámpara de Jerash, con su asa zoomórfica y su forma de babucha ovalada, que ya había surgido en el siglo VI de los hornos bizantinos del Hipódromo y de otros hornos de Jerash. La historia de la producción alfarera omeya de Jerash, tal como la ilustra el conjunto de hornos de Artemisa, es interesante desde varios puntos de vista. Por una parte, pone de manifiesto la pervivencia de Jerash como gran centro de fabricación de cerámica cuyos productos se difundían por la mayor parte de la Jordania norte, en fuerte competencia con los centros surgidos en otras ciudades de la *Decápolis* y especialmente durante el periodo bizantino (por ejemplo, Umm Qays/Gadara y Tabaqat Fihl/Pella, por nombrar otros mercados alfareros de prestigio de la orilla oriental del Jordán, aunque también se han excavado grandes depósitos asociados a hornos omeyas en Beisan/Escitópolis).  
Sin embargo, solamente el conjunto de hornos de Artemisa se ha conservado como ejemplo representativo de este comercio dinámico que no perdió impulso sino hasta después del periodo abbasí, en el siglo IV/X, cuando Jerash en su conjunto experimentó un declive generalizado en cuanto a sus actividades comerciales y probablemente también en cuanto a su población, dada la vinculación entre ambas. Gran parte de esta recesión permanente tuvo que ver con el desvío de las principales rutas comerciales entre la gran Siria e Iraq. Al encontrarse en situación tangencial respecto a las nuevas rutas, sometida a una fuerte reducción del comercio, Jerash se vio obligada a mantenerse a través de medios más modestos, recurriendo a pequeñas explotaciones agrícolas y a actividades productivas de carácter meramente local.  
Unas pocas huellas, junto con alguna mención escrita, revelan que se produjo una destrucción deliberada, al parecer durante las Cruzadas, cuando las ruinas de los templos de Artemisa y Zeus, abandonadas desde hacía tiempo, ofrecieron refugio a los ayyubíes y más adelante, en el periodo posterior a las Cruzadas, a los mamelucos. Esta condición de ciudad rural sumida en el letargo y casi olvidada permaneció inalterada hasta que los dirigentes otomanos instalaron allí a la población circasiana en el siglo XIII/XIX, y Jerash, considerada incluso entonces una antigua ciudad en ruinas, revivió para convertirse una vez más en un lugar floreciente, tal como lo es hoy en día.  
De todas formas, es preciso añadir una apostilla: la imagen histórica que se deduce hasta ahora de las excavaciones (llevadas a cabo desde finales de la década de 1920 hasta la actualidad) está probablemente distorsionada o, al menos, desequilibrada, ya que dichas excavaciones se han concentrado y siguen concentrándose en los restos monumentales y en los espacios públicos, más que en las viviendas ordinarias y en el tejido urbano general.

fr.name: Les fours à poteries du théâtre nord
description:
Les **fours à poteries du théâtre nord** étaient construits selon le même principe. Dans les chambres de cuisson pansues, on a retrouvé des poteries défectueuses et des lampes à huile, ces fameuses “lampes de Jérach”, avec leur poignée zoomorphe et leur forme ovale de babouche, qui étaient déjà produites au VIe siècle dans les fours byzantins de Jérach, tant sur l’hippodrome que sur d’autres sites.  
La contribution apportée par les fouilles des fours d’Artémis nous permet de retracer l’histoire de la production des céramiques omeyyades à Jérach. Il en ressort que la ville a su tenir avec constance une place importante dans la production de poteries, que ses produits se sont répandus largement dans la Jordanie du nord, malgré la concurrence des autres villes de la Décapole, une concurrence qui sera de plus en plus vive à la fin de la période byzantine (cf. “Oum Qays (Gadara)” et “Tabaqat Fihl (Pella)”, pour nommer d’autres marchés de poteries réputés de la rive est du Jourdain, bien que les fouilles des fours omeyyades de Beisan/Scythopolis ont aussi mis au jour d’importants dépôts de poteries).  
Mais c’est surtout grâce aux informations recueillies au cours des fouilles des fours d’Artémis que nous sommes en mesure de nous représenter cette activité commerciale, qui sera soutenue et florissante jusqu’à la fin de la période abbasside, au IVe/ Xe siècle, quand Jérach va pâtir du déclin général de l’activité commerciale et voir sa population diminuer, les deux phénomènes étant d’ailleurs étroitement liés. Les causes de cette récession de longue durée se trouvent en grande partie dans le basculement du commerce sur le nouvel axe de la grande Syrie à l’Irak. Ainsi, Jérach, marginalisée, sera réduite à une relative autarcie: la baisse des activités commerciales n’est compensée que par la production agricole des petites propriétés et par l’artisanat répondant aux besoins locaux.  
Il semble qu’il faille attribuer les rares traces de destructions délibérées à l’occupation des ruines des temples d’Artémis et de Zeus par les Ayyubides qui vont s’y réfugier pendant les croisades, et enfin aux Mamelouks, après les croisades cette fois. Mis à part une seule mention de Jérach dans les documents de cette époque, la ville restera confinée dans sa vie de provinciale endormie et sera presque oubliée, jusqu’à ce que l’occupant ottoman y installe une population circassienne au XIIIe/XIXe siècle. Jérach, qui commence d’ailleurs à bénéficier de son image de site antique, va alors retrouver sa prospérité perdue et sa vitalité actuelle.  
Il reste à faire une dernière réserve sur ce panorama historique général. Elle repose sur les résultats des fouilles entreprises depuis la fin des années 20 jusqu’à nos jours: quel degré de distorsion, quel déséquilibre affectent des recherches fondées sur des fouilles qui se sont limitées aux vestiges monumentaux et officiels en négligeant, aujourd’hui encore, l’étude des quartiers modestes et le plan d’ensemble de la ville ?

en.name: Ceramic floor
description:
The Palatine Chapel, founded by King Dinis (1261‒1325, crowned 1279) in the early 14th century, contains one of the oldest ceramic floors in Portugal. This rare floor of the main altar probably dates from the 15th century, contemporary with the reign of King Afonso V (1432‒81, crowned 1438).  
The Chapel, a Christian religious space dedicated to the Holy Spirit, is characterised by the Mudéjar style, Hispano-Muslim ceiling decoration in *alfarge* carved wood and by the *alicatado* floor, formed from ceramic pieces of many colours and shapes. Both the mosaic floor and the wooden ceiling are among the oldest examples of Mudéjar craftsmanship in Portugal.  
The configuration and decorative composition used in the ceramic floor remind one of the Mudéjar-style carpets, decorated with a network of interlacement motifs containing geometric patterns, commissioned to embellish palaces and churches.  
Up until the second half of the 15th century, the term “*alicatado*” (Spanish for cut-tiles, derived from the Arabic verb qata’a, “to cut”) was given to the ceramic mosaics made in this technique. It requires piecing together monochromatic enamelled *tesserae* (small glazed ceramic pieces of various geometric shapes and colours that had been glazed and cut beforehand) to create decorative compositions with geometric patterns, a delicate, painstaking and expensive task, used mostly for paving floors, but also for wall surfaces.  
This ceramic floor might date from the same period as that of the room where King Afonso VI was imprisoned, one of the Royal Palace’s oldest rooms.
keywords: ceramic; mosaic; tiles; *alicatado*; Royal Palace; Mudéjar; Portugal; Hispano-Muslim; 15th century; Afonso V
materials: Glazed clay; *alicatado* composition of monochrome enamelled *tesserae* (green, white, brown and black)
tags: alicatado composition of monochrome enamelled tesserae (green, white, brown and black)

en.name: Moroccan House in Linderhof  Palace Park
short_description: The king had considerable alterations made to both the outside and the inside of the house in keeping with his own lavish tastes. Jean Perron, a sculptor in Paris who had organised the purchase for Ludwig II, also acquired the rich furnishings appropriate for an ornamental setting such as tables, chandeliers, tabourets, mirrors and vessels, none of which have been preserved. Numerous skilled workers and artists were involved in the dismantling, rebuilding and altering of the house.The entire colour scheme was changed with an abundant use of gold, and individual rooms were furnished with costly materials. Coloured glazing “in the Moorish style” and a tessellated floor were introduced to add to the oriental character of the house.
type: Pavillion; Park building in Linderhof Palace Park
history:
When the rebuilding of the “Moorish Kiosk” in the Linderhof park undertaken by order of Ludwig II was completed at the beginning of 1878, it evidently reawakened the king’s interest in buildings in the Islamic architectural style.  
The pavilion, acquired at the World Exhibition in Paris in 1878, was remodelled inside at Ludwig II's request and originally built on the Stockalpe near the Austrian border. The "Moroccan House" had already also been shown at the International Exhibition in Vienna in 1873 and had been built for this purpose in Morocco. The wooden building, acquired by a private individual after the king's death, was bought back by the state in 1980 and was reconstructed in the palace park in 1998.
keywords: King Ludwig II; Linderhof Palace; Ettal; Moorish style; Romanticism; gardens

ar.name: كأس ذات طلاء معدني.
description:
القطعة عبارةكأس عميقة ذات ساق حلقيّة الشكل وسطح دائري. تتألف الزخرفة من غصنيّة على شكل أغصان ملتفّة تنحدر منها سعيفات مختزلة خيطيّة الشكل. تتطوّر اللفائف وتتداخل، وتشكل زخرفة نباتية غزيرة تلتف حول عنقود العنب. من جهة ثانية، تقسم دوائرٌ الفراغَ إلى مناطق منضّدة وواضحة بشكلٍ كافٍ. بَيد أنّ الوحدة والحركة تنبعثان من المجموع، مما يوفّر توازنا ًمنسجماً بين الأشكال البنيّة المذهّبة والسطح السكري اللون، والفراغ مُحاك دون أن يكون مُشبعا.  
ولصناعة الخزف المذهّب والتي كانت وصفتها مشروحةً، ولكن دون الكثير من الدقّة، منذ القرن 6 الهجري/ 13 الميلادي، يتمّ استعمال مزيج من النحاس والفضّة بنسبٍ شديدة الدقّة، ويضاف إلى هذا المزيج مُغرة حمراء (أكسيد الحديد المعروف ب "المزرّون")، ثمّ يتمّ حلّ الكل في الخلّ. لقد كان الخزف المذهّب الذي انتشر في الأندلس اعتباراً من القرنين 7 و 8 الهجريين/ 13 و 14 الميلاديين، رائجا في مصر في الفترة ذاتها؛ وكانت الزخرفة النباتيّة تحاذي الأشكال الحيوانيّة. ويشهد اكتشاف هذه الكأس ذات الأصل الأندلسي في تونس على أهمّية العلاقات التجاريّة التي تطوّرت بين إفريقية وإسبانيا الإسلاميّة، وعلى الأخصّ اعتباراً من القرن 7 الهجري/ 13 الميلادي.

إنه المثال الأنموذج للفخار المذهب الذي انتشر في الأندلس وفي مصر ابتداءا من القرن 7 للهجرة (القرن 13 للميلاد). يجمع هذا النوع من الفخار بين الزخرف الزهري والشكل الحيواني؛ ويبرهن اكتشاف هذا الصحن ذي الأصل الأندلسي في تونس على أهمية الروابط التجارية بين إفريقية (تونس) وإسبانيا المسلمة.
place: عثر على القطعة خلال  تنقيبات أجيت بالقصبة (تونس).
keywords: خزف مصقول بالمعدن؛ زخرفة زهرية ؛ طلاء معدني؛ خزف مذهب.

en.name: Bowl with golden-brown metallic glaze.
description:
This deep bowl with round base and curved sides is decorated with scrolls of foliage and stems with palm leaves. They interweave exuberantly, revealing a bunch of grapes. Clearly defined rings divide the decoration into concentric areas, but the overall effect is one of unity and uninterrupted movement, enhanced by the harmony of the golden-brown motifs against the cream background. The space is well-covered but not overloaded.  
The formula for producing ceramics with a golden glaze has been roughly described since the AH 6th / AD 12th century. Red ochre (iron oxide or *almazzaron*) is added to a precisely measured mixture of copper and silver. This mixture is then diluted with vinegar. The golden-glazed ceramics which spread throughout al-Andalus from the AH 7th–8th / AD 13th–14th centuries were in vogue in Egypt at the same time. Both floral and animal decorations were used. The discovery of this bowl of al-Andalus origin in Tunis has highlighted the importance of the trade established from the AH 7th / AD 13th century between Ifriqiya and Muslim Spain.

This is a typical example of the golden-glazed ceramics that spread through al-Andalus and Egypt from the AH 7th / AD 13th century, combining floral and zoomorphic motifs. The discovery of this dish of Andalusian origin in Tunis underlines the importance of trade between Ifriqiya and Muslim Spain.
keywords: Glazed ceramic; floral decoration

es.name: Cuenco de reflejo metálico dorado.
description:
Cuenco profundo de base anular y pared redondeada. La decoración se compone de follajes ornamentales desde donde dimanan palmetas estilizadas filiformes. Los roleos se extienden y entrecruzan. En el interior de la frondosa flora se puede observar la presencia de racimos de uva. Varios círculos dividen el espacio en netas zonas superpuestas. Sin embargo, el conjunto proyecta una imagen de unidad y movimiento gracias a un armonioso equilibrio entre los motivos marrón dorado sobre un fondo color crema. La superficie está decorada sin llegar a estar recargada.  
La fórmula para la fabricación de la cerámica dorada era conocida, aunque sin gran detalle, desde el siglo VI / XIII. Se procedía en primer lugar mezclando cobre y plata, respetando unas proporciones exactas; luego se añadía ocre rojo (óxido de hierro denominado almazarrón); por último, el líquido se diluía en vinagre. La cerámica dorada, que se propagó por al-Andalus a partir de los siglos VII-VIII / XIII-XIV, estaba en boga en el Egipto de la misma época. El diseño floral alterna con motivos zoomórficos. El descubrimiento en Túnez de este cuenco procedente de al-Andalus evidencia la importancia de los vínculos comerciales que se desarrollaron entre Ifriqiya y la España musulmana, especialmente a partir del siglo VII / XIII.

Ejemplo típico de la cerámica dorada que se extendió por al-Andalus y Egipto a partir del siglo VII / XIII. El diseño floral alterna con motivos zoomórficos. El descubrimiento en Túnez de este cuenco procedente de al-Andalus evidencia la importancia de los vínculos comerciales entre Ifriqiya y la España musulmana.
dates: Siglos VII-VIII de la Hégira / XIII-XIV d. C.
keywords: Cerámica dorada; decoración floral

fr.name: Coupe à lustre métallique.
description: Profonde coupe à base annulaire et paroi arrondie. Le décor est composé de rinceaux d'où émanent des palmettes stylisées filiformes. Les enroulements se développent et s'interfèrent. La flore, à l'intérieur de laquelle on constate la présence de la grappe de raisin, est exubérante. Des cercles divisent l'espace en zones superposées assez claires. Néanmoins, unité et mouvement se dégagent de l'ensemble, qui offre un équilibre harmonieux entre les motifs brun doré et la plate-forme crème. L'espace est tapissé sans être saturé. Pour la fabrication de la céramique dorée, dont la formule était décrite, mais sans grande précision, depuis le VIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.), on fait intervenir un mélange de cuivre et d'argent selon des proportions bien précises, auquel on ajoute de l'ocre rouge (oxyde de fer appelé almazarrón), puis on dilue le tout dans le vinaigre. La céramique dorée qui s'est répandue en Andalousie à partir du VIIe-VIIIe siècle H (XIIIe-XIVe siècle J.-C.), était en vogue en égypte à la même époque ; le décor floral côtoie des motifs zoomorphes. La découverte à Tunis de cette coupe d'origine andalouse témoigne de l'importance des liens commerciaux qui se sont développés, surtout à partir du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.), entre l'Ifriqiya et l'Espagne musulmane.

C'est l'exemple type de la céramique dorée qui s'est répandue en al-Andalus et en égypte à partir du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.). Elle associe le décor floral au motif zoomorphe. La découverte de cette coupe d'origine andalouse à Tunis témoigne de l'importance des liens commerciaux entre l'Ifriqiya et l'Espagne musulmane.
dates: VIIe-VIIIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIIe-XIVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Céramique lustrée, décoration florale

ar.name: رداء قداس (لباس كبير لرجل دين كاثوليكي ) مصنوع من مخمل مزين وحياكة حريرية
description: إن رداء القداس للكاهن هو تكوين  ملفوف pasticcio مكون من مخمل مزين إيطالي أقدم ورداء قداس عرضاني من الحرير العثماني والحرير الأخير له فتحات بيضوية مملوءة بالتوليب والقرنفل         و اللفات المزهرة وهو تزيين نوعي لحياكة الحرير العثماني في ذلك الوقت. وهذا التشكيل من الأقمشة لرداء قداس الكاهن يظهر أنه لم يكن هناك تحفظات حول استخدام القماش من المناطق الإسلامية للملابس الكنسية المسيحية من حيث مظهرها الجميل.

de.name: Kasel (Messgewand für den katholischen Ritus) aus Dekorsamt und Seidengewebe
description: Die Kasel ist ein *Pasticcio* bestehend aus einem älterem italienischen Dekorsamt und einem Kaselkreuz aus osmanischer Seide. Letztere Seide hat ein Muster aus großen Spitzovalen, gefüllt mit Tulpen, Nelken und Blütenranken, dem für die osmanische Seidenweberei der Zeit typischen Dekor. Die Zusammenstellung der Gewebe für eine Kasel macht deutlich, dass man ein aus islamischen Regionen stammendes Gewebe wegen seiner eindrucksvollen Wirkung vorbehaltlos für den christlichen Ritus verwendete.
holder: MAK – Österreichisches Museum für angewandte Kunst / Gegenwartskunst

en.name: Chasuble (Mass vestment for the Catholic liturgy) made of decorative velvet and silk weave
description: The chasuble is a *pasticcio* consisting of an older Italian decorative velvet and a chasuble cross of Ottoman silk. The latter silk has a pattern of large lancet ovals filled with tulips, pinks and floral scrolls, a decoration typical of Ottoman silk weaving of the time. This combination of textiles for a chasuble demonstrates that there were no reservations about using a textile from Islamic regions for the Christian liturgy on account of its impressive appearance.

de.name: Dießener Heiligenhimmel
description: Im Kuppelfresko gruppieren sich die unzähligen Heiligen und Seligen aus den verschiedenen Zweigen der gräflichen Stifterfamilie Dießen-Andechs um Christus und sind zugleich Exempla für die an den Pendentifs dargestellten Kardinaltugenden. Bilderzählerisch wie perspektivisch kalkuliert fallen beim Betreten der Kirche zuerst die ältesten und lokal verehrten Familienmitglieder ins Auge: Rasso, Rathard und Mechtildis.

en.name: The Saints in Heaven (so-called Heaven of Dießen)
description:
In this dome fresco, innumerable saints and beatified persons from the various branches of the founding noble family, the Counts of Dießen-Andechs, form a group amassed around Christ. As being such, they exemplify the cardinal virtues which are depicted in the pendentives.  
Having been carefully calculated both narrationally and perspectively, the oldest locally revered members of the Dießen-Andechs family (Rasso, Rathard and Mechtildis) are the first to catch the eye of those entering the church.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Les foggaras
description:
An ingenious system of drawing and distributing water simultaneously in an extremely dry area, foggaras consist of a row of wells on a gentle and uninterrupted slope that allows surface water to flow to gardens.  
  
The well shafts are made by drilling a tunnel at the base of a mountainous area and following an aquifer, with the goal of bringing water to the surface for irrigation of agricultural land. The tunnels are horizontal and dug with extreme precision on a regular slope to allow the water to flow steadily.  
  
The tapped foggara water table is deeper than the water table under the dunes, but closer to the surface in the nearby plateau of Tadmaït (to the east), which makes it accessible by digging horizontally. The size of this network of wells is estimated at thousands of kilometres between the Gourara and the Touat; seven kilometres for just the Mghayer, the foggara of Timimoun. The punishing work of digging could not have been accomplished without the exploitation of many slaves. For this reason maintaining foggaras that collapse or become silted is problematic.  
  
The term foggara refers not only to this system of pumping from the water table, but also to the pooling of water to irrigate the palm groves. The oases of Gourara and Touat have comb-like structures (*kesria*) that direct the water flowing between the “teeth” (*kiel el-Ma*). The water is distributed according to the requirements of the private gardens, and routed through channels (*seguias*) that drain into ponds (*majens*) from which farmers draw water to the extent allowed. This system, specific to Saharan regions, is evidence of its early use, and of the people’s deep desire to live in harmony by sharing with each other the meagre resources of the Sahara in a strict but fair manner.

en.name: Ewer
description: The achievements of old Samarqand (Afrasiab) pottery workmanship are exemplified by a separate type of unglazed and stamped tableware, mainly jugs and ewers, manufactured in moulds from an ash-grey clay. There were vast deposits of this clay near the town of Penjikent (60km to the east of Samarqand). Elegantly shaped thin-walled vessels with a polished surface and a delicate stamped ornamental pattern on shoulders and neck were probably designed to imitate valuable silver tableware. Historians suggest that the main function of these ewers was storing water that while steadily evaporating through the pores of the ceramic body remained fresh and cold for a long time.
keywords: Earthenware; unglazed; Samanid
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

en.name: *Huqqa* base
description: This spherical *huqqa* base is carved from white nephrite.The gemstones have been finely carved with the veins of the leaves and petals. This particular *huqqa* once belonged to the Qing Dynasty Emperor Qianlong (r. AH 1148-1210 / AD 1736-1795), as his seal is inscribed on its base. The popularity of this object among the elites gave way to a proliferation of smoking devices.

de.name: Kath. Pfarr- und Wallfahrtskirche St. Notburga
description: Die Wallfahrtskirche ist die Hauptverehrungsstätte der hl. Notburga von Rattenberg, die der Legende nach hier 1313 begraben worden sein soll (Stelle des ersten Halts des Ochsenkarrens mit ihrem Leichnam). Unter Einbeziehung des spätgotischen Chors wurde wohl durch Jakob Singer das Langhaus errichtet, eine einfache Saalkirche mit einer Abfolge von kuppeligen Gewölben, daran der eingezogene, polygonal schließende Chor. Die kräftigen Pilasterpeiler geben die barocke Gliederung des Raums vor, und die reiche Stuckausstattung in frühen Rokokoformen überdeckt die gotischen Bauelemente völlig. Überaus prächtig der Hochaltar, der gleich einem monumentalen Reliquiar die aufrecht stehenden Gebeine der Heiligen in einem Glasschrein birgt.

Die Wallfahrtskirche in Eben bildet den Mittelpunkt der Verehrung der bäuerlichen Schutzheiligen Notburga und ist ein besonders anmutiges Beispiel für die Verbindung von ländlicher Volksfrömmigkeit und hochrangiger künstlerischer Qualität im österreichischen Spätbarock. So werden die Fresken mit bäuerlichen Szenen in volkskunstartigem Stil von feinstem Wessobrunner Stuck umrahmt. Der trotz der einfachen baulichen Anlage prächtige Raumeindruck ist wesentlich der reichen Ausstattung zu verdanken.
artist:
Architektur: Jakob Singer (1685-1760, Zuschreibung)  
Deckenfresken: Johann Georg Höttinger (um 1690 – nach 1645, Zuschreibung)
history: Eine erste Kapelle, dem heiligen Rupert geweiht, bestand in Eben schon zu und vor Lebzeiten der hl. Notburga (um 1265-1313). 1434 erfolgte der Patronatswechsel zugunsten Notburgas, die immer mehr als Schutzheilige verehrt wurde; 1474 zur Kaplanei erhoben. Der Vorgängerbau wurde 1510-15 spätgotisch erneuert, davon sind Chor und Ostturm in den 1736-38 errichteten Barockbau einbezogen worden. 1891 Erhebung zur Pfarre. Eine gründliche Innen- und Außenrenovierung ist 1988-92 durchgeführt worden.
keywords: Wallfahrtskirche; Reliquienverehrung; hl. Notburga; Wessobrunner Stuck; Deckenfresken

en.name: Catholic Parish and Pilgrimage Church of St. Notburga
description: The pilgrimage church is the main site for the veneration of St. Notburga of Rattenberg, who according to legend was buried here in 1313. The nave was built, with the integration of the Late Gothic choir, by Jakob Singer; a simple hall church with cupola-like vaults and the adjoining retracted, polygonal choir. Powerful pilaster piers establish the Baroque configuration. Rich stuccowork in the style of the Early Rococo completely covers the Gothic architectural features. The magnificent high altar, like a monumental reliquary, contains the upright bones of the saint in a glass shrine.

The pilgrimage church in Eben, the centre of the veneration of St. Notburga, the patron saint of peasants, is an especially charming example of the combination of popular rural piety and great artistic quality within Austrian Late Baroque. The frescos depicting peasant scenes in the style of folk art are framed by the finest stucco of the Wessobrun school. The magnificent spatial impression, despite the simple architectural structure, is largely due to the rich interior work.
artist: Architecture, attributed to: Jakob Singer (1685–1760); ceiling frescos, attributed to: Johann Georg Höttinger (c. 1690–after 1645) or Christoph Anton Mayr (c. 1720–1771); stuccowork, attibuted to: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr (1698–1763); sculpture, attributed to: Franz Xaver Nißl (1731–1804)
history: A chapel, dedicated to St Rupert, stood in Eben before and during the lifetime of St. Notburga (c. 1265–1313). In 1434 the patron was changed in favour of Notburga who was increasingly venerated as a patron saint; elevated to the status of a chaplaincy in 1474. The predecessor building was renewed in the Late Gothic style in 1510–15, of which the choir and east tower were integrated into the Baroque building erected in 1736–38. Elevation to the status of a parish in 1891. A thorough renovation of both the interior and exterior was carried out between 1988 and 1992.
keywords: Pilgrimage church; veneration of relics; St. Notburga; Wessobrunn stucco; ceiling frescos

en.name: Perforated baton with incised wild horses
description: 15,000 years ago, towards the end of the last Ice Age, human beings found an ideal campsite under a rock spur in Canton Schaffhausen. Here they ate, drank, worked flint stones, and did sewing work. The campsite was discovered in Herblingen, a district in the town of Schaffhausen, in the nineteenth century. Among the finds was a perforated baton made from reindeer antlers, featuring two incised wild horses. It is one of the oldest figurative representations ever found in Switzerland. It would be interesting to know what the baton was used for in the late Stone Age. Archaeologists assume that it served ritual purposes in connection with hunting. Drawing was considered a thaumaturgic act through which humans hoped to gain control over wild game and thus enhance their hunting luck.
keywords: archaeology; Paleolithic; perforated baton

ar.name: بقايا مبنى إسلامي في كنسية القديس جوفاني ديلي إريميتي.
description:
استفيد في بناء القسم الجنوبي للكنيسة النورمندية (كنيسة القديس جوفاني ديلي إريميتي) من جدار كان موجوداً، وهو الجدار الشمالي للقاعة العربية الإسلامية؛ وهي عبارة عن قاعة مستطيلة الشكل كان لها أهمية كبيرة، وتم قطع احد ضلعي العرض لتوسيع الكنيسة.  
كان المبنى الإسلامي مؤلفاً من ثلاثة أقسام : القاعة المتسطيلة (القاعة العربية) والرواق والسور المحيط . وقد بقي منها ( القاعة العربية) أجزاء من هيكل الحائط الجنوبي للكنيسة. أما مقاييسها فهي ( 17،76م X 5،62م)، وتتجه نحو الجنوب، القبلة (مكة). وكانت مقسمة طولانياً إلى رواقين تقسمهما خمسة أعمدة وتشكل مقاطع مربعة الشكل، حيث يرتكز عليها اثنا عشر قوساً، موزعة على الأجزاء المربعة )ستة من كل طرف)، وكان يحتوي كل مقطع مربع على نافذة ذات قوس، يدخل منها النور. صارت هذه القاعة العربية مغطاة اليوم بثلاثة أقواس كبيرة متقاطعة، وقد شيدت عام 905/ 1500.

يستغل الجانب الجنوبي للكنيسة النورمندية للقديس جيوفاني ديجلي إيريميتي الحائط المتواجد سلفا (الجانب الشمالي) والذي كان يُحيطُ ببناية إسلامية مكونة من ثلاث وحدات معمارية: قاعة كبيرة مستطيلة الشكل (تسمى القاعة العربية)، ورواق وسياج. كانت "القاعة العربية" ذات المحور الرئيسي الموجه صوب الشمال الجنوبي في اتجاه مكة مقسمة طوليا إلى بلاطتين بواسطة خمسة أعمدة ذات مقطع مربع.
keywords: منشأة دينية.
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

en.name: Remains of an Islamic building in the complex of the church of San Giovanni degli Eremiti.
description:
The south wall of the Norman church of San Giovanni degli Eremiti was erected using the north wall of the enclosure of an Islamic building containing the ‘Arab Hall’, a rectangular hall that was also used in construction during the Norman era, interrupted on its shorter side by the transept of the church.  
The Islamic building would have consisted of three architectural units: the rectangular room (the Arab Hall), the portico and an enclosure. The Arab Hall (17.76 m by 5.62 m), with its main north–south axis oriented towards Mecca, was divided lengthways into two naves by five square-section pillars. These pillars supported the vaults of the 12 square bays (six on each side), of which some of the structure remains in the south wall of the transept. Each bay was illuminated by a small splayed, pointed window. The Arabic Hall is now covered by three large 16th-century cross vaults.

The south wall of the Norman church of San Giovanni degli Eremiti incorporates the existing north outer wall of an Islamic building consisting of three architectural units: a rectangular room (known as the Arab Hall), a portico and an outer wall. The Arab Hall, oriented north–south in the direction of Mecca, was divided longitudinally into two naves by five square pillars.
keywords: religious architecture
partner: Regione Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

es.name: Restos de edificio islámico en la iglesia de San Juan de los Eremitas.
description:
La pared sur de la iglesia normanda de San Juan de los Eremitas se erigió aprovechando el muro septentrional del recinto de un edificio islámico que incluía la llamada “sala árabe”, una estancia rectangular incorporada asimismo a la construcción de época normanda aunque cortada en su lado menor por el crucero de la iglesia.  
El edificio islámico debía de constar de tres unidades arquitectónicas –la sala rectangular, el pórtico y un recinto–. La “sala árabe” (17,76 por 5,62 m), con el eje principal orientado de norte a sur en dirección a La Meca, estaba dividida longitudinalmente en dos naves por cinco pilares de sección cuadrada. Sobre ellas descargaban las bóvedas de las doce crujías (seis por lado), de las cuales queda un tramo de la estructura del muro meridional del transepto. Cada crujía estaba iluminada por un ventanuco ojival con esviaje. La sala está cubierta hoy por tres grandes bóvedas de crucería del siglo X / XVI.

La pared sur de la iglesia normanda de San Juan de los Eremitas está constituida por el muro septentrional del recinto de un edificio islámico precedente que estuvo formado por tres unidades arquitectónicas: una sala rectangular (la llamada “sala árabe”), un pórtico y un recinto. La “sala árabe”, con el eje principal orientado de norte a sur en dirección a La Meca, estaba dividida longitudinalmente en dos naves por cinco pilares de sección cuadrada.
keywords: arquitectura religiosa
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

fr.name: Vestiges d’un édifice islamique dans le complexe de l’église de San Giovanni degli Eremiti.
description:
La paroi sud de l'église normande de San Giovanni degli Eremiti exploite le mur préexistant (côté nord) qui ceignait un édifice islamique comprenant ce que l'on appelait la “salle arabe” : il s'agit d'une salle rectangulaire, elle aussi affectée par la construction d'époque normande, interrompue sur le petit côté par l'extension du transept de l'église.  
  
L'édifice islamique devait comporter trois unités architecturales : la salle rectangulaire (“salle arabe”), le portique et une enceinte. La “salle arabe” (17,76 m x 5,62 m), dont l'axe principal est orienté nord-sud en direction de La Mecque, était divisée longitudinalement en deux nefs par cinq piliers à section carrée. Les voûtes des douze travées carrées (six par côté) s'appuyaient sur ces piliers ; il n'en subsiste qu'un fragment de structure, dans le mur sud du transept. Chaque travée était éclairée par une petite fenêtre ogivale ébrasée. La “salle arabe” est aujourd'hui couverte par trois grandes voûtes d'arêtes, du XVe siècle.

La paroi sud de l'église normande de San Giovanni degli Eremiti exploite le mur préexistant (côté nord) qui ceignait un édifice islamique constitué de trois unités architecturales : une grande salle rectangulaire (dite salle arabe), un portique et un enclos. La “salle arabe”, dont l'axe majeur est orienté nord-sud en direction de La Mecque, était divisée longitudinalement en deux nefs par cinq pilastres à section carrée.
keywords: architecture religieuse
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

it.name: Resti di un edificio islamico nel complesso della chiesa di San Giovanni degli Eremiti.
description: La parete meridionale della chiesa normanna di San Giovanni degli Eremiti sfrutta il preesistente muro settentrionale del recinto di un edificio islamico comprendente la cosiddetta “sala araba”: si tratta di un'aula rettangolare, anch'essa interessata dalla costruzione d'età normanna, interrotta nel lato minore dall'estensione del transetto della chiesa. L'edificio islamico doveva essere costituito da tre unità architettoniche: l'aula rettangolare (la “sala araba”), il portico e un recinto. La “sala araba” (m. 17.76 x 5.62), con l'asse maggiore orientato da nord a sud in direzione della Mecca, era divisa longitudinalmente in due navate da cinque pilastri a sezione quadrata. Su di essi scaricavano le volte delle dodici campate quadrate (sei per lato), delle quali rimane un brano della struttura nel muro meridionale del transetto. Ogni campata era illuminata da una finestrella ogivale strombata. La sala araba è oggi coperta da tre grandi volte a crociera di età cinquecentesca.

La parete meridionale della chiesa normanna di San Giovanni degli Eremiti sfrutta il preesistente muro settentrionale del recinto di un edificio islamico costituito da tre unità architettoniche: un'aula rettangolare (la cosiddetta sala araba), un portico e un recinto. La “sala araba”, con l'asse maggiore orientato da nord a sud in direzione della Mecca, era divisa longitudinalmente in due navate da cinque pilastri a sezione quadrata.

en.name: Carillons
description: A Flanders-made ensemble of two carillons with 92 bells commissioned by King D. João V, representing the world’s largest historical set. The north tower carillon has 45 bells and the south tower carillon 47 bells. The bells are made of bronze and their total weight is 217 tons. According to tradition, when the king was told the astronomic price of only one carillon, he answered "I didn't expect it to be that cheap, I'll have two."
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Carrilhões
description: Conjunto de dois carrilhões com noventa e dois sinos em bronze, encomendados pelo rei, na Flandres, formando o maior conjunto histórico do mundo, com um peso total de 217 toneladas. A torre norte tem quarenta e cinco sinos e a torre sul tem quarenta e sete. Segundo a tradição, ao ser informado do elevado custo deste instrumento, o Rei terá dito “*Não sabia que era tão barato, quero dois.*”

en.name: Trophy

it.name: Trofeo
description: Quattro magnifici trofei in stucco decorano gli angoli della sala da ballo. Rappresentano una testa di unicorno circondata da armi e bandiere, a creare un'elegante composizione.

ar.name: ثوب عرس من الطراز الأندلسي
description: ثوب العرس هذا المفصل كان يشاهد في فسيفساء من العصر الروماني. و لكن الطبيعة الخاصة لهذا الزي الرائع لا تكمن فقط في قصته التي هي قياسية من أجل كل ملابس الأعراس في تونس و لكن في في تزيينه المعقد والذي يعكس التأثير الأندلسي. والشيء النمطي في هذا الثوب المصنوغ في راف راف على الساحل الشمالي لتونس هو الشريط المركزي الشامل المطرز بالذهب والفضة و مزين بترترة. واليد المدافعة تعمل كرمز حماية.

en.name: Wedding tunic in Andalusian style
description: Simply tailored wedding tunics have been seen in mosaics from the Roman period. The special character of this splendid costume, however, lies less in its cut, which is standard for all wedding attire in Tunisia, but in its sophisticated decoration, which reveals Andalusian influence. Typical for this tunic, made in Raf Raf on the north coast of Tunisia, is the extensive central stripe embroidered in gold and silver and decorated with sequins. A defensive hand serves as protective symbol.
materials: Silk, cotton, gold and silver threads, sequins
tags: Silk, cotton, gold and silver threads, sequins

en.name: "Alexander Fights a Sea Battle"
names: Folio from a Khamsa (Quintet) of Amir Khusrau Dihlavi
description: In the episode illustrated, Alexander the Great has ordered the construction of a tall tower surmounted by a revolving mirror in order to battle the pirates menacing the Mediterranean Sea. The protagonists appear as contemporary Indians wearing turbans and tunics, rather than ancient Greeks, and one of the fighters uses a gun, an invention from nearly two millennia after Alexander’s time.
materials: Main support: Ink, opaque watercolour, gold on paper Margins: Gold on dyed paper

en.name: School of North African girls directed by Mme Luce. Studying.
names: Taken from *L'Algerie Phtographiée*, vol. 2, Province d'Alger
short_description: French colonisation of Algeria deprived the Algerian schooling system of its traditional funding and brought it into disorder, as very few "indigenous Muslim" students were accepted into the new European schools. A few private initiatives emerged, such as this establishment for young Muslim women, founded by Madame Luce Allix in 1846.
keywords: Teaching; French colonies; Algeria

fr.name: Ecole de jeunes filles mauresques dirigées par Mme Luce. L'étude

short_description: La colonisation de l’Algérie par la France entraîne une désorganisation des écoles algériennes, privées de leurs ressources économiques traditionnelles. en.name: *Sitara* for the *rawda* of the Prophet’s mosque in Medina
description:
That this curtain was intended for the *rawda* is suggested by the text in the large medallion at the top. It consists of a *hadith* of the Prophet, *ma bayna qabri wa minbari rawda min riyad al-janna* (‘Between my tomb and my minbar is one of the gardens of Paradise’). The same text appears above the *mihrab* in the *rawda*.  
Sultan Mahmud II is known to have practised the art of calligraphy and a number of *sitara*s commissioned by him for the Prophet’s mosque bear his pear-shaped signature cartouche which reads, *katabahu al-‘abd Mahmud bin ‘Abdulhamid khan* (‘written by the servant \[of God\] Mahmud, the son of ‘Abdulhamid Khan’).

en.name: Museum of Islamic Art
description:
The Museum of Islamic Art (MIA) is a pioneering project spotlighting the cultural vision of the State of Qatar, both in the region and across the world. Under the guiding vision of His Excellency, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the project is the cornerstone for the State of Qatar in its establishment as a global capital of culture.  
  
The 35,500 sq. m museum was designed by I.M. Pei, taking inspiration from the 13th-century sabil (ablutions fountain) of the 9th-century Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun in Cairo. The museum comprises a five-level main building and a two-storey Education Wing, connected across a fountain courtyard. The main building’s angular planes form ascending pinnacles, rising around an atrium. Inside, a dome is revealed, concealed from outside view by the walls of a central tower. A window on the building’s north side rises to a height of 54 m., providing dramatic views from all five floors. The ground floor is home to a temporary gallery space for touring international exhibitions and the café, giftshop and Information Services. The museum’s permanent exhibition is installed on two floors of galleries designed by the French firm Jean-Michel Wilmotte & Associés. The fourth floor contains temporary galleries showcasing the research topics of museum staff, using items either not seen in the permanent galleries or with new information to see them in a new way.  
  
Overview of the collections  
The MIA houses artefacts highlighting the creative achievements of the Islamic world's richest cultures and spanning nearly a thousand years. The collection represents the full scope of Islamic art in all media, from manuscripts to ceramics, metalwork, glass, stone, ivory, textiles, wood, precious stones and jewellery.  
  
The permanent exhibition of c. 850 artefacts offers an insight into the diverse art of the Islamic world. Two floors are dedicated to the exploration of historical eras and interpretation of the themes of Islamic art and material culture, from the 8th century to the cusp of the 19th century.  
  
The MIA also holds thousands more objects, some destined to be seen in future displays and others providing a resource for education and research.  
  
Highlights of the collection include: a distinguished group of carpets and textiles, a range of Ayyubid and Mamluk metalwork and enamelled glass, an outstanding strength in early ceramics, a comprehensive collection of astrolabes and scientific instruments, masterpieces of Mughal jewellery and rare manuscripts and miniatures.  
  
The Department of Education and Information  
The department’s main goal is to create materials, programmes and workshops that will engage the public, allowing them to explore the world through Islamic art, promoting a culture of learning within an atmosphere of knowledge and entertainment.  
  
The Curatorial Department  
The department of internationally trained curators is committed to studying, documenting and publicising the MIA’s collection and establishing the MIA as a world-class centre of scholarly research.  
  
The Conservation Department  
Set to become a leading regional service centre for museums, the department is committed to restoring, preserving and caring for the collection through the application of innovative scientific methods.  
  
International partnerships  
The MIA is committed to building a network of partnerships around the world and offering institutes and museums collective access to information, research and images. It has strong ties with many world-class museums and collections, including the Louvre, France, the British Museum, UK, the Victoria & Albert Museum, UK, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, USA, the Museum für Islamische Kunst, Germany, the Al-Sabah Collection, Kuwait, the Gulbenkian, Portugal, and the National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art, Algeria.

en.name: Photo of al-Busiri Mosque
short_description: The al-Busiri Mosque was named after the great Imam, famous for writing Sufi poetry about the love of God and in praise of his Prophet Muhammad. The fame of his poem “al-Burda” surpasses that of its writer. The mosque is located in Alexandria, in the Anfushi area in the Gomrok (al-Jumruk) district overlooking the Eastern Harbour, on the *Midan Al-Masajid* (The Square of Mosques). The Square of Mosques is so-named because the area is comprised of a large number of shrines to *Awliya’ Allah* (good people of God), who came to Alexandria during the Ayyubid and Mamluk times. The mosque consists of two separate squares: the mosque courtyard with a water fountain in the middle, surrounded by corridors from all directions; and the second square with the *qibla* wall or *iwan al-qibla*, which leads to the tomb of Imam al-Busiri. Above the tomb is a metal dome and the minaret which takes the shape of an obelisk. The dome and the minaret are in the 19th-century Turkish style.
keywords: Imam al-Busiri Mosque; Alexandria; Anfushi District

en.name: Ersari, so-called *Beshir*
description: Measuring 4 metres long and 1.70 metres wide, this piece is representative of the large-format carpets from the middle Amu-Darya region, probably made in oasis cities. In older literature, it is also referred to as Beshir or Ersari-Beshir. The pattern and ornamental repertoire of such carpets are predominantly of non-Turkmen origin and often go back to Ikat motifs. Furthermore, variants of the Minah Khani pattern, boteh forms, or large rhombus patterns are characteristic. This piece shows a rhombus cross pattern, which can already be found on a colour plate of the first monograph of Turkmen carpets, published in 1908/1909 in St. Petersburg. The pattern's design concept in the publication of the Russian general A. A. Bogolyuvov also corresponds to that of the Dresden carpet. Despite some sections with a more pronounced pile, this knotting is characterized by its lustrous wool and a wonderful play of colours. The field and border ornaments seem to hover over the base, alternately designed in shades of blue and green. The rich reddish-brown colour, combined with the accentuated use of yellow, appears somewhat restrained, which further enhances the composition's overall effect.
holder: Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum Dresden), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Amu-Darja; Central Asia
materials: Wool, goat hair; pile weave, asymmetrical knot open left

en.name: Incense Burner
description:
This hollow cast incense burner in the shape of a bird is hinged and consists of two parts, which allows the object to be fully opened to insert the incense.  
The whole surface is engraved. Perforated decoration can be found on the chest, wings, back and tail. The eyes are highlighted by studs and engraved feathers cover the neck. An angular inscription runs chain-like around the neck and reaches the middle of the chest. A pierced, interwoven motif is placed in between. The wings contain a medallion with an elevated centre and spiralling tendrils and knots. The wingtips are ribbed and framed by an interlaced band which widens below them. The area between hinge and tail tip contains an ornament band with interwoven patterns. The legs are covered in engraved feathers and the claws are shaped in a detailed manner.  
The hinged body is different to most other bird-shaped incense burners, which either have a square drawer or an opening for the incense.
holder: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection
keywords: Incense burner; Bronze; metalwork; Inlaid metalwork; Iran; Iranian world; Afghanistan; Persian world; Inscription; Bird; Animal
partner: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection

DeSoto Custom
description:
This DeSoto belonged to Sheikh Ali Bin Abdullah Al Thani, who reigned as Qatar’s fourth ruler between 1948 and 1960. The vehicle would escort His Highness to attend special occasions in the country such as inaugurations and official site visits during oil explorations.  
  
The navy-blue car features an all-steel body structure, chrome trims, and hydraulic brakes. Its rustproof body protects the interior structure complete with its V6 engine.  
  
In Qatar, tailor-made exterior handles turned the ordinary car into a state limousine for Sheikh Ali. The royal guards would grasp on to the handles during parades and ceremonies.

en.name: Cup and cover
description:
This cup and cover is a virtuosic example of Venetian glass-making in the 15th century. The applied 'prunts', or small blobs of glass fused to a glass body, in this case in bright colours, are intended to simulate a vessel encrusted with jewels. Paired with the moulded ribs on the foot that are giled, a feature that appears in similar forms on contemporary gold and silver work, the bowl and cover gives an impression of a highly prized object displaying vast technical skill.  
  
The bowl and cover was formerly in the collection of Alessandro Castellani (1823-1883), a member of the famous family of antique dealers and goldsmiths. The fact it was owned by Castellani emphasises the jewel-like appearance and its status as a luxury object in the 15th century.
materials: Footed, covered cup in colourless glass with applied red, blue and green glass prunts, enamelled and gilt

en.name: Church of San Cataldo
description:
This small church represents a complete masterpiece and deserves particular attention as a typical example of the workers from the Fatimid culture in the service of Christian clients. Its present position dominates Piazza Bellini below, like an acropolis and is due to the lowering in the late 19th century of the old level of San Cataldo, undertaken in order to regulate the altimetry of the surrounding urban area. Usually ascribed to the reign of Guglielmo I (1154-1166), the church must have been part of a group of buildings which have now disappeared, a luxurious property of Maione da Bari, Admiral and later the King’s Grand Chancellor. Some formal analogies with examples of Romanesque architecture from Puglia are evident, in particular with the ancient Cathedral of Molfetta. This has led some scholars to recognise in Maione, who commissioned the church at the same time as he held the office of Grand Admiral (1154-1160), that he was possibly moved by a feeling of emulation in relation to his predecessor Giorgio d’Antiochia, who had erected the Church of Santa Maria d’Ammiraglio nearby.  
Externally, the building stands as a square volume with walls that are coloured with prominent blind arcades that frame the three windows, open on each side. A blind arch of lesser dimension indicates, on both lateral sides, the passage between the naves and the *santuario*. The crowning of the church, made of small ashlars of well-squared cut stone, is formed by a crenellation, which has been restored in many places. Above the crowning, the red hemispherical volumes of three small cupolas covering the central nave stand out, placed on a low continuous tambour onto which small windows open. In the interior, the three cupolas of the central nave mark the three bays of the central nave flanked by two short lateral naves with cross-vaulted bays. The arches on columns that longitudinally identify the naves are pointed arches; some capitals come from more ancient buildings. Angular joints with indented niches mark the transition between the square bays and the round imposts of the cupolas. The structure terminates with three apses; the two lesser ones are made from the thickness of the wall, and the semi-cylindrical wall of the central and larger apse appears on the outside, the only derogation from the purity of the parallelepiped volume.  
The simplicity of the bare walls contrasts with the richness of the original pavement of marble and porphyry marquetry with a mosaic underlining the principal structural lines of the edifice. The walls are articulated with a system of pointed-arch windows, along the whole perimeter, in correspondence with the bays, the three apses and the entrance portal. Only the altar and a slab of white marble, decorated with a Greek cross with the symbols of the evangelists, remain from the internal decoration.  
Works of restoration were launched in 1877, conducted by Giuseppe Patricolo in the years 1882-85, and spared the edifice from the added volume, reforming the exterior according to the criteria of stylistic restoration. The church now belongs to the Equestrian Order of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem.

es.name: Iglesia de San Cataldo
description:
Entre los ejemplos de arquitecturas surgidas durante el reino normando, la pequeña iglesia representa una acabada obra maestra y merece especial atención como típico producto de los maestros de cultura fatimí al servicio de clientes cristianos. Su actual ubicación, dominando como desde una acrópolis Piazza Bellini, se debe al rebajamiento de finales del siglo XIX del antiguo nivel de San Cataldo para regularizar las alturas del área urbana circundante. Atribuida habitualmente al reinado de Guglielmo I (1154-1166), la iglesia formaría parte de un conjunto de edificios hoy desaparecido, suntuosa posesión de Maione da Bari, Almirante y después Gran Canciller del rey. Ciertas analogías formales con ejemplos del románico de Apulia, sobre todo con la Catedral Antigua de Molfetta, han inducido a algunos estudiosos a reconocer en Maione a la persona que encargó su construcción durante el periodo en que ocupó el cargo de Gran Almirante (1154-1160), quizá movido por el espíritu de emular a su predecesor Giorgio de Antioquía, que había erigido la vecina iglesia de Santa María del Almirante.  
En el exterior, el edificio se presenta como un volumen puro escuadrado, cuyas paredes están animadas por los arcos ciegos que enmarcan las tres ventanas abiertas en cada fachada. Una arcada ciega de menores dimensiones marca, en los laterales, la zona de paso entre las naves y el altar. Corona la iglesia, construida con pequeños sillares de piedra cortada bien escuadrada, un almenaje restaurado en muchas de sus partes, por encima del cual sobresalen los rojos volúmenes hemisféricos de las tres cupulitas que cubren la nave central, sustentadas por un bajo tambor continuo donde se abren pequeñas ventanas. En el interior, las cúpulas marcan las tres crujías cuadradas de la nave central, cerrada por dos breves naves laterales con crujías cubiertas por bóvedas de crucería. Los arcos sobre columnas que en sentido longitudinal delimitan las naves son apuntados; algunos capiteles son de expolio, reutilizados de edificios más antiguos. El paso del cuadrado de base a la circunferencia de la imposta de las cúpulas se hace mediante enlaces angulares de nichos reentrantes. La planta se cierra con tres ábsides; los dos menores practicados en el espesor del muro, mientras que del central, mayor, sobresale en el exterior la pared semicilíndrica, única concesión en la pureza del volumen paralelepípedo.  
A la riqueza del original pavimento de incrustaciones en mármol y pórfido, con un mosaico cuyo dibujo subraya las principales líneas estructurales del edificio, se contrapone la sencillez de las paredes desnudas, pautadas por una serie de ventanas de arco apuntado abiertas a lo largo de todo el perímetro, en correspondencia con las crujías de los tres ábsides y del portal de entrada. De los ornamentos internos se conservan solamente el altar y una losa de mármol blanco adornada con una cruz griega con los símbolos de los evangelistas. En 1877 empezaron los trabajos de restauración, dirigidos en los años 1882-1885 por Giuseppe Patricolo: se liberó el edificio de los volúmenes añadidos y se reconfiguró el exterior según los criterios de la restauración estilística. Hoy la iglesia pertenece a la Orden Ecuestre del Santo Sepulcro de Jerusalén.
