en.name: Goblet
description:
At the end of the 17th century a conscious effort was made by English glass-sellers to end their dependence on import products from Venice. In 1673 the Glass-Sellers’ Company engaged the glass-maker George Ravenscroft to carry out research into creating a recipe to rival Venetian crystal glass. Ravenscroft was official glass-maker to the Company from 1674, and strove to not merely imitate Venetian imports but create something to better them. He operated two furnaces in London, the Savoy furnace, which was run by Venetian glass-workers, and another at Henley-on-Thames run by glass-workers from Altare. Here, Ravenscroft perfected a recipe for 'flint glass', which used large amounts of lead-oxide in order to stabilise the recipe and produce a glass which resembled rock crystal.  
  
Large goblets such as this one are representative of the austere shapes of glass items that proliferated in England at the end of the 17th century, and the thick and heavy proportions that was well suited to this new type of glass.

en.name: Palace of Alin Aq Al-Husami
description: What remains of this palace, built by Alin Aq al-Husami one of Sultan Qalawun’s *amirs*, tells us that it was a residential palace with two floors and one of the noblest examples of the architecture of the *Bahri* Mamluk era. On passing through a curved passageway the visitor reaches the ground floor which once contained storerooms, stables, a bakery, courtyard and *takhtabush*. The upper floor has a balcony overlooking the courtyard and small rooms covered by barrel or cross vaults.

es.name: Palacio de Alin Aq al-Husami (opción)
description: Alin Aq al-Husami, uno de los emires del sultán Qalawun, indican que se trataba de un palacio residencial con dos plantas, de los más nobles de la época de los mamelucos *bahri*es. En la planta baja, a la cual se accede por una entrada en codo, se encontraban almacenes, establos, una tahona, un patio y un *tajtabuch*. La planta superior tiene un mirador que da al patio y consiste en pequeñas habitaciones cubiertas por bóvedas de cañón o de arista.

fr.name: Palais de Alin Aq al-Hussami (option)
description: Les vestiges de ce palais construit par Alin Aq al-Hussami, un des émirs du sultan Qalawun, indiquent qu’il s’agissait d’un palais résidentiel à deux étages, parmi les plus nobles de l’époque des Mamelouks *bahrides*. Au niveau inférieur, auquel on accède par une entrée coudée, se trouvaient des magasins, les écuries, un moulin, une cour et un *takhtabuch*. L’étage supérieur comporte un belvédère qui donne sur la cour et qui consiste en petites pièces surmontées de voûtes en berceau ou d’arêtes.

en.name: Cathedral
description:
"The Cathedral, begun about 1493 and still fortunately surviving almost intact, was the most important building erected during the Manueline era.  
D. Manuel I proposed it himself, and appointed João Gomes to oversee the work. However, due to constant misunderstandings and unforeseeable delays, work only began definitively in 1502, largely as a result of the king’s personal commitment. The Cathedral was completed in 1517 under the Master Mason, Pêro Anes, assisted by Gil Eanes. The role of the latter artist has been the subject of much discussion, so that he has to be understood as acting as the Master of Works, in other words: number two in the hierarchy on the building site.  
The fact that the Cathedral’s construction took many years is verified by the king’s financial contributions, as noted in documents from 1517 and 1521. Although a project that was developed much later, the wide church was similar to the model that had been used for the most important churches in mainland Portugal since the 13th century. It has three aisles with five bays, a projecting transept and apse, with three parallel rib-vaulted chapels. The carved bosses of the chancel vaulting, bear the royal coat of arms, an armillary sphere and the Cross of Christ. The *Mudejar* ceiling with its stylistic geometric designs, and roses in inlaid cedar wood, is particularly fine, although the pictorial decoration is in the Central European Renaissance style.  
The volumetric interior structure is reflected in the exterior scheme: the central part of the façade is higher than the sides. At the east end there is an elegant tower with a *spire* that was used as a belltower and probably as a watchtower too. A flamboyant garland completes the roof, covering of the apse chapels. The main portal is in the typical Late Gothic style: a pointed arch set on seven parallel *colonnettes* that extend to the capitals of the same number of *archivolts* Only the penultimate one is decorated.  
The Manueline retable with its three tiers of panels, joined by delicate wood carving and some important figures, is the only one of its kind to have remained intact in its place of origin amongst the many that were made at that time in Portugal. Although various alterations were introduced over the years, including a Baroque statue in the central niche, it is only the poor state of conservation of the retable that impedes a full appreciation of its original sumptuousness. Little is known of the painter, the “Master of Lourinhã”, who is said to have been from the Low Countries, but he and his team certainly demonstrate the stylistic processes of painters from this part of Europe. Be that as it might, Portuguese painters who were famous at that time, and particularly those working within the Court, were greatly influenced by imported Flemish painting, appreciating the mimetic expression of reality. The work can therefore be dated to around 1515, painted by an unknown artist, but directly linked to painters from the Lisbon circle.  
The magnificent choir stalls in the chancel probably date from between 1508 and 1512, and are still located in their original position in a remarkably good state of conservation. Similarly the choir stalls must be considered the work of an unknown Flemish master, consisting of two rows of seats, the higher one having canopies and backs, whilst the second row has just a carved frieze, already displaying Renaissance taste.  
The retable here also displays remarkable woodwork, revealing the influence of Olivier of Ghent, although a Flemish master working in Madeira probably produced them.  
The relief sculptures are of the highest quality, as can be seen in the beautifully carved figures of the apostles, in the niches that separate these figures, and in the decorative friezes. According to tradition, the quality of the carving was such that they were not originally gilded so as to highlight the sculpted lines. The gilding was added in 1755."

en.name: Folio with two miniatures from Persian translation of 'The Wonders of Creation and the Oddities of Existence' by Zakaria Qazwini
description: A folio from Persian translation of a popular cosmography treatise "The Wonders of Creation and the Oddities of Existence" by Zakaria bin Muhammad al-Qazwini. The book, written in AD 13th century, covers the fields of geography, astronomy, astrology and natural history, in a mixture of science and superstition. Both sides of the folio are embellished with miniatures featuring fruit-bearing trees.
keywords: Miniature; Manuscript; Iran; Safavid; Calligraphy
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

en.name: Messageries Maritimes's Istanbul-themed posters
short_description: *Messageries maritimes* was a French merchant shipping company. When it began, it operated on routes to the Middle East. Its ships were used as troop transports during the Crimean War, and were so helpful for the army that the Emperor gave the company the right to operate on the Bordeaux-Brazil route as thanks. This was the first French transatlantic line equipped with steamers. The following year, the *Société générale maritime* (later called *Compagnie générale transatlantique*) received the North Atlantic lines. From 1871 to 1914 the shipping company, now called *Compagnie des messageries maritimes*, saw its Golden Age.
keywords: travelling; orientalism; İstanbul; maritime travelling
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

en.name: Mosque
description:
With its imposing minaret of long curved lines topped by four rounded spires forming a crown (possibly to remind the faithful of their religious obligations), the mosque was also used as a city hall, arsenal or grain silo. The minaret was also an impregnable watchtower. The mosque had a courtyard that opened onto various spaces: the prayer room, the study rooms, the area with a boiler room reserved for ablutions, and a bathing pool.  
  
The long square prayer hall has arches that rise two metres above the ground and are parallel to the *qibla* wall, as in the original plan of the Mosque of Medina. Along the walls, tiny windows allow faint light to enter. The pillars are made of smooth black stone. The *mihrab* is small and whitewashed. The mosque is devoid of tiles and carpets.

fr.name: Mosquée
description:
Avec son imposant minaret aux longues lignes légèrement courbes sommées par quatre flèches qui forment une couronne et semblent rappeler sans cesse aux fidèles leur ardente obligation, le temple religieux est aussi hôtel de ville et arsenal ou silo à grain. La mosquée, dont le minaret constitue aussi une imprenable tour de guet, possède une cour qui s’ouvre sur plusieurs espaces : la salle de prière, les salles d’étude, le *takerboust* réservé aux ablutions et pourvu d’une chaufferie et d’une piscine. La longue salle de prière en forme d’équerre est dotée d’arcs qui s’élèvent à deux mètres à peine au-dessus du sol et qui sont parallèles au mur de la *qibla*, selon le premier plan de la mosquée de Médine. Tout au long des murs, de petites fenêtres étroites laissent passer une faible lumière. Les piliers sont en pierre noire lisse. Le *mihrab* est petit, blanchi à la chaux. La mosquée est dépourvue de  
carreaux de faïence et de tapis.

en.name: Old Cathedral
description:
The date of its foundation is uncertain. Rocco Pirri (1735) attributed its construction to Matteo Chiaramonte, but some documents testify to its existence already to the Norman period, where it is presumed a mosque already existed. It is known, in fact, that in 1174, after the Greek Church of San Nicol was abandoned, it was raised to the Mother Church. Later, during the Angevin period, the church was enriched and enlarged and was consecrated on the second Sunday in May 1266.  
The role of Mother Church for the foundation of the new Church of the Annunziata having been lost in 1619, the Old Cathedral (Duomo Vecchio) became the subject of a major transformation, changing its appearance according to the baroque style.  
It retains the general structure of the Norman period, in the form of a Latin cross with a single nave, preceded by a vestibule of lesser height in which there is a 14th-century niche to the right side of the entrance. The area of the *santuario* is flanked by the *prothesis* and by the *diaconicon*; emerging in relation to the perimetrical walls of the aula, constitute the transversal arm of the cross. Scenographically placed at the top of a flight of steps, the building shows the main front, facing the present-day Piazza Duomo, characterised by a rich portal, already restored in 1818, and with a rose window above that is at present closed up. The pointed arched entrance dating back to the era of the Chiaramonte family, is underlined by several lintels a rincasso, with zig-zag patterns, with pleated bands and leaves, connected by sculptured coved cornices, by listels and rods; the piers are combined with small columns. A barrel vault, no longer in existence, originally covered the nave; the hemispherical cupola at the crossing with the transept is also in poor condition. Today, the absence of the wall opposite the presbyteral area characterises the north side of the church.

es.name: Catedral Vieja
description:
Resulta incierta la fecha de su fundación. Rocco Pirri (1735) atribuye su construcción a Matteo Chiaramonte, pero algunos documentos prueban su existencia ya en época normanda, en el lugar donde se supone que había una mezquita. Se sabe, de hecho, que en 1174, abandonada la iglesia griega de San Nicolás, fue elevada a iglesia mayor. Más tarde, en el periodo angevino, la iglesia se enriqueció y agrandó, y fue consagrada el segundo domingo de mayo de 1266.  
Perdida su función de iglesia mayor con la fundación de la nueva iglesia de la Anunciada (1619), la Catedral Vieja fue objeto de trabajos de restauración (1771-1788) que cambiaron su aspecto según el gusto barroco.  
Conserva la planta general del periodo normando, de cruz latina con nave única, precedida por un vestíbulo de menor altura en cuya pared a la derecha de la entrada hay una hornacina del siglo XIV. El volumen del presbiterio está flanqueado por la *prótesis* y el *diacónicon*, que, sobresalientes exteriormente respecto a los muros del perímetro de la sala, constituyen el brazo transversal de la cruz. Escenográficamente situada en lo alto de una escalinata, la fachada principal —vuelta hacia la actual Piazza Duomo— se caracteriza por su fastuosa puerta, restaurada ya en 1818, y por un rosetón actualmente ocluido. La entrada de perfil apuntado de la época chiaramontana está remarcada por varios arcos rehundidos, con motivos en zigzag en franjas tableadas y con follaje, encuadrados por marcos escultóricos en bovedilla, baquetones y boceles; los *pies derechos* se combinan con columnitas. La nave estaba cubierta originalmente por una bóveda de cañón hoy perdida; en pésimo estado está también la cúpula hemisférica de la intersección con el transepto. La ausencia del paramento mural en el área del presbiterio caracteriza el lado norte de la iglesia.

en.name: Ewer
short_description: It is known that there were workshops producing glass vessels around Beykoz in Istanbul in the 19th century. The first glass workshop was founded by Mevlevi Dervish Mehmed Dede during the reign of Selim III (1789-1807). There were European glass craftsmen working in those workshops as well. Cups, bottles, jugs etc. made of colourful, colourless and opal glass were among Beykoz' productions. This is an ewer made of dark blue opaline with a water-drop-shaped lid. On its body there are raised flower patterns and *kabaras*.
keywords: Beykoz ceramic; Turkish decorative arts

en.name: *Housing in the Pierrefitte Chateau and Gardens* \[…\] *Payable in installments* \[…\] *\[Epargne Foncière Immobilière des Quinze - Vingts\]: open to visitors every day.*
short_description: Pierrefitte-sur-Seine was still a farming village in the mid 19th century. The construction of the Paris-Lille railway line in 1859 brought in rich Parisians in search of country air. The town was transformed again in the 20th century, thanks to the construction of factories in the Saint-Demis plains and the arrival of people looking for cheaper housing. The first tramway was also built in 1901. This poster advertises housing in an area outside the tramway's reach, which had remained wooded and rural, and was equipped with the most modern technologies available, such as gas and telephone.
keywords: Urbanisation; housing; France

fr.name: *Lotissement du parc et du chateau de Pierrefitte* \[...\], *grandes facilités de paiement* \[... \]. *\[Epargne Foncière et Immobilière des Quinze - Vingts\]: s'adresser pour visiter tous les jours sur place*
short_description: Au milieu du XIXe siècle, Pierrefitte-sur-Seine est encore un bourg agricole. La création de la ligne de chemin de fer Paris-Lille en 1859 attire de riches Parisiens en quête de villégiatures. La ville se transforme au XXe siècle avec des populations à la recherche de logements moins chers et la création d’usines dans la plaine de Saint-Denis. La première ligne de tramway est créée en 1901. Cette affiche de 1908 vante les mérites d’un lotissement dans une zone encore boisée et rurale mais desservie par le tramway, et bénéficiant des commodités les plus modernes alors (gaz, téléphone).
keywords: Urbanisation; lotissements; France

ar.name: تزويق قرآن.
description:
الصفحة الأولى مزخرفة بتزويق محاط بمستطيل مذهب. رصعت الزخرفة المركزية بمعينين مقعرين، أرضيتهما مذهبة وموشاة بخطوط كستنائية اللون، تحيط بزخارف زهرية الشكل ومنمنمة متعددة الفصوص. التزاويق مؤطرة من كلتا الجهتين بستة مثلثات مرصعة بزخرفة زهرية من نفس الطراز. المجموعة مفصولة بعدة أشرطة مقسمة إلى فصوص ذهبية أرضيتها بيضاء اللون، ومبرقشة بنقاط كستنائية. تبرز سعيفة نخل نحو الهامش الأيمن، مكونة من زخرفة زهرية خلفيتها مطلية بصباغة بيضاء وخضراء، وموشاة بنقاط كستنائية اللون، ومحاطة بنقاط مذهبة.  
كتبت الصفحة اليسرى بالخط الكوفي الأسود، وتمت الإشارة للحروف الصوتية بنقاط حمراء، وأشير للهمزة بنقطة خضراء تبعاً لنظام أبي الأسود. نهاية الآية مشار إليها بمثلث مكون من نقاط مذهبة، وقد أشير لنهاية الآية الخامسة برصيعة مذهبة. أما عنوان السورة وعدد آياتها، فتمت الإشارة إليهم دون تغيير السطر، بنقش كتابي كوفي مذهب محيطه مطلي بلون كستنائي، وينتهي بزخرفة سعيفة نخل بارزة نحو الهامش الأيسر.

يزخرف التزويقُ المؤطرُ بمستطيلٍ مذهبٍ الصفحةَ اليمنى؛ وأثِّث الزخرفُ المركزي بمعينين مقعرين لهما خلفية مذهبة مرصعة بخطوط بنية.  
كتبت الصفحة اليسرى بالخط الكوفي وباللون الأسود؛ بينما تمت الإشارة إلى عنوان السورة وعدد آياتها بنقيشة كتابية مذهبة.
keywords: فن الكتابة ؛ زخرفة زهرية ؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ رق؛ تذهيب؛ خطاطة.

en.name: Qur’anic illumination.
description:
The right-hand page has the illumination, which is framed inside a gilt rectangle. The central decoration has two concave diamond shapes with a gilt background marked with brown lines framing stylised multi-lobed fleurons. The decoration is surrounded on each side by six triangles containing similar floral motifs. The whole illumination is separated by strips on a white background dotted with brown markings and divided by gilt segments.  
The left-hand page contains black *kufic* script. Vowels are marked by red dots and the *hamza* is shown with a green dot, as in the Abi al-Aswad system. The end of the verse is indicated by a triangle of three gilt dots. The end of the fifth verse is marked by a gilt medallion.  
The title of the *sura*, with the number of its verses, is indicated on the same line by a gilt *kufic* inscription with brown edges which terminates in a palm-leaf motif pointing towards the left-hand margin.

The illumination, in a gold rectangular frame on the right-hand page, has two concave lozenges in its centre, gilded at the bottom and peppered with brown lines.  
The left-hand page is written in black *kufic* script with the title of the *sura* and the number of verses given in golden *kufic* script.
keywords: Calligraphy; floral decoration; geometric decoration; religious manuscript

es.name: Iluminación de Corán.
description:
La iluminación que decora la página derecha está enmarcada por un rectángulo dorado. La ornamentación central se compone de dos rombos cóncavos sobre fondo dorado salpicado por trazos marrones, que contienen unos florones estilizados polilobulados. Seis triángulos, decorados con un diseño floral del mismo estilo, ribetean la iluminación. Dividen el conjunto dos franjas, sobre fondo blanco, punteadas con marcas marrones y separadas por segmentos dorados. Hacia el margen derecho se proyecta una palmeta rodeada de puntos dorados e integrada por una decoración floral salpicada de puntos marrones sobre fondo blanco y verde.  
La página izquierda presenta una inscripción en cúfico negro. Conforme al sistema de Abi al-Aswad, los puntos rojos marcan las vocales, mientras que un punto verde indica la *hamza*. Un triángulo formado por tres puntos dorados señala el final de la aleya. Un medallón dorado indica el fin de la quinta aleya.  
El título de la sura, con el número de versículos, está señalado en la misma línea por una inscripción, en cúfico dorado con contorno marrón, que termina en una palmeta proyectada hacia el margen izquierdo.

La iluminación que decora la página derecha está enmarcada por un rectángulo dorado. La ornamentación central se compone de dos rombos cóncavos sobre fondo dorado, salpicado por trazos marrones.  
La página izquierda presenta una inscripción en cúfico negro. El título de la sura y el número de versículos están indicados por una inscripción en cúfico dorado.
keywords: Caligrafía; decoración floral; decoración geométrica

fr.name: Enluminure d’un coran.
description: La page de droite est meublée par l'enluminure, qui est encadrée par un rectangle doré. Le décor central est meublé par deux losanges concaves à fond doré parsemé de traits marron qui encadrent des fleurons stylisés à plusieurs lobes. Le décor est encadré, de part et d'autre, par six triangles garnis d'un décor floral de même style. L'ensemble est séparé par des bandes à fond blanc tachetées de points marron et divisées par des segments dorés. Une palmette, se projetant vers la marge droite, est formée d'un décor floral dont le fond, blanc et vert, est parsemé de points marron. Elle est entourée de points dorés. La page de gauche est écrite en coufique noir. Les voyelles sont marquées par des points rouges, la hamza est indiquée par un point vert, conformément au système d'Abi al-Aswad. La fin du verset est signalée par un triangle formé par trois points dorés. La fin du cinquième verset est indiquée par un médaillon doré. Le titre de la sourate, avec le nombre de ses versets, est marqué, sans changement de ligne, par une inscription en coufique doré aux pourtours marron et qui se termine par une palmette projetée vers la marge gauche.

L'enluminure, encadrée par un rectangle doré, orne la page de droite. Le décor central est meublé par deux losanges concaves à fond doré parsemé de traits marrons.  
La page de gauche est écrite en coufique noir. Le titre de la sourate et le nombre de ses versets sont marqués par une inscription coufique dorée.
keywords: Calligraphie; décoration florale; décoration géométrique
partner: Musée des arts islamiques de Kairouan

en.name: *The Port of Constanţa*
short_description: The Black Sea port of Constanța underwent its first modernization while Dobruja, the province where it is situated, was under Ottoman control. In 1857, when the Ottoman government hired a British company to build a railway in Dobruja, the concluded contract also stipulated the reconstruction of the Constanța port. Completed in 1864, it was still a small harbor with a wooden dock, a dam and one cereals depot. After Dobruja was annexed by Romania, a law was issued in 1885 for the “improvement and augmentation” of the port. In 1896 its modernization was leased to a French enterprise but due to some disagreements, three years later the state took over the works, which were led by architect Anghel Saligny. Inaugurated in 1909, the new port had 3 dams, several docks, depots, silos, an oil basin, an electric plant.

ar.name: وعاء / زبدية عليه أرنب بري
description: بحلول القرن العاشر فإن العاصمة الفاطمية القاهرة أصبحت مركز إنتاج الخزف المزين بطلاء معدني بواسطة طلاء براق ذهبي (يعرف بطلاء الخزف البراق ). والتشكيلات البصرية المدهشة على هذا الخزف يصور رجالا و نساء ولاعبي خفة وحيوانات – مثل هذا الأرنب البري المرح ذو الآذان الطويلة المرسوم بخطوط مائعة وطبيعة حيوية.وإن موضوعها العادي نسبيا والشدة اللونية الذهبية للطلاء البراق تضعها بعيدا عن الخزف الأقدم المطلي بطلاء براق في العراق والأمثلة اللاحقة  من إيران. وهذا النوع من الزبدية المزججة المطلية بطلاء براق الفاطمية كانت محط تقدير كبير في كل منطقة المتوسط والعديد من الزبديات المشابهة ما تزال ترى وهي تزين الجدران الخارجية للكنائس في بيزا ، إيطاليا من أواخر القرن الحادي عشر وبداية القرن الثاني عشر.
keywords: خزف ، طلاء براق ، خزف مطلي بطلاء براق ، زبدية
tags: خزف ، طلاء براق ، خزف مطلي بطلاء براق ، زبدية

en.name: Bowl with a hare
description: By the 10th century, the Fatimid capital of Cairo had become the centre of production for ceramics decorated in a metallic paint with a golden lustrous sheen (known as lustre ceramics). The striking visual compositions on these ceramics portray men and women, acrobats, and animals—such as this jovial long-eared hare—painted in fluid lines and lively naturalism. Their relatively “ordinary” subject matter and the golden tone of the lustre sheen set them apart from the earlier lustre ceramics in Iraq and later examples from Iran. This type of Fatimid lustre-glazed bowl was highly appreciated as an export product throughout the Mediterranean, and several similar bowls can still be seen adorning the exterior walls of churches in Pisa, Italy, from the late 11th and early 12th centuries.
keywords: Ceramics; lustre; lustre-ceramics; bowl

ar.name: سجادة صلاة
description: سجادة الصلاة هذه منسوجة بثلاثة ممرات مقنطرة ومصابيح معلقة وزهريات تحتوي حزم من الأزهار ولفات أزهار كبيرة. وألوان الباستيل الزهرية والعصابة المنسوجة بلفة أزهار هي نموذجية في حرير الشيان Chian . والنوع الشهير منه يعود لعام 1742 وقد تم الاحتفاظ به في دير في مون في كيوس. وتصدير حرير الشيان مسجل من القرن الخامس عشر عندما كانت الجزيرة تحت الحكم الجنوي واستمر حتى عندما انتقلت الجزيرة لأيدي العثمانيين في عام 1566.

el.name: Επίτοιχο ύφασμα
description: To μεταξωτό είναι υφασμένο με τριπλή τοξοστοιχία, κρεμαστές καντήλες, βάζα με μπουκέτα λουλουδιών και ελισσόμενους βλαστούς με μεγάλα άνθη. Τα παστέλ ρόδινα χρώματα και η ταινία με τον άνθινο βλαστό χαρακτηρίζουν τα μεταξωτά της Χίου. Το γνωστότερο δείγμα φυλάσσεται στη Νέα Μονή Χίου και χρονολογείται 1742. Η εξαγωγή χιώτικων μεταξωτών τεκμηριώνεται  από τον 15ο αιώνα όταν το νησί ήταν υπό τους Γενουάτες και συνεχίστηκε όταν πέρασε στα χέρια των Οθωμανών το 1566.

en.name: Hanging
description: This prayer rug is woven with a triple arcade, hanging lamps, vases with bunches of flowers and large flower scrolls. The pastel pinkish colours and the band woven with a flower scroll are typical of Chian silks. A famous one dated 1742 is kept in the monastery of Nea Mone on Chios. The export of Chian silks is recorded from the 15th century when the island was under Genoese rule and continued when the island passed into Ottoman hands in 1566.
keywords: Ottoman textile; Floral motifs; Hanging Lamp motifs; Chian Silks; floral decoration; textile

en.name: Theodor Aman – *Ottoman messengers at the court of Vlad the Impaler* (photo)

ar.name: مخمل
description: إن الحجم والنموذح غير المتكرر لهذا التصوير الأثري لامرأة تقف في قوس مفصص يجعله فريدا. وقد كانت هذه الأنسجة قد حيكت لأول مرة وبداية من قبل النساجين الصفويين في إيران والذين كانوا معروفين بصنع هذه الأقمشة التي لانظير لها تقنيا ولكننا نعلم من سيرة أكبر عظيم المغول أنه في حوالي 1600 وصل الهنود لنفس القدر من المهارة التقنية.
type: حرير وطبقات رقيقة من الفضة مغزولة حول الحرير

en.name: Velvet
description: The size and non-repetitive pattern of this monumental depiction of a woman standing in a lobed arch make it unique. It was first and foremost weavers from Safavid Iran who were known for making these technically unparalleled textiles, but we know from the biography of the Great Mughal Akbar that in around 1600, the Indians had come equally far in technical skill.
keywords: Velvet; Iran; India; Silk; textile; human representation; figural decoration; women; bird; floral decoration; animal decoration
materials: Silk and silver lamella spun around silk
tags: Silk and silver lamella spun around silk

en.name: Traditional peasant attire
names: Villager from the Beqaa Valley in traditional dress
short_description: Peasants and ordinary people's clothes did not change much over the centuries. It generally consisted of a shorter, narrower and darker coloured pair of baggy *shirwal* trousers for winter, and another pair in a lighter beige or khaki colour for the summer. This was paired with a cotton shirt or vest, called a *sudriye*, and a short embroidered *abaya*. A *keffiye*, a large scarf made of white cotton, was worn on the head with a *lebbede* or *'agal* on top.
keywords: Shirwal; Clothes; Traditions; Keffiye; Colour
materials: The costumes were made of cotton and silk

ar.name: قرآن.
description:
ضم هذا القرآن عدة مجلدات لاتحتفظ المكتبة الوطنية إلا بجزأين منهم، نقدم منهم الصفحتين 100 و101 من الجزء الثاني. قياسات الجزأين قريبة من المربع، وقد كتب كلاهما على رق، وبالخط الكوفي *المغربي* بالحبر البني. وبالرغم من أن الكتابة تتسم بنفس الطراز، فلم يكن لها نفس المظهر في الجزأين معا، مما يوحي بأن العمل قد أنجز من طرف ناسخين اثنين. ويبين الرسم العريض للخطوط وتدوير زوايا الحروف وتجويف الانحناءات، أن الخطين يرجعان لنفس الفترة، وينتميان لنفس القرآن. في الواقع واعتباراً من النصف الثاني من القرن 3 الهجري/ القرن 9 الميلادي يبدأ الخط الكوفي بالتمايز في الغرب الإسلامي عن الخط الشرقي، ليتطور نحو أسلوب، يسمى *المغربي،* سوف يبلغ ذروة كماله بعد قرنين. إن هذا الأسلوب في الكتابة والذي مازال يتبع نظام التصويت القديم لأبي الأسود، مجردٌ من نقاط تهجئة الحروف، ويقتصر على رسم الحروف الصوتية المختصرة مثل الفتحة والضمة اللتين يشار إليهما بنقطتين حمر فوق السطر، والكسرة بنقطة حمراء تحت السطر وإلى مضاعفة الحرف بالشدة كما هو الحال في الحاضر والتي تشبه حرف W اللاتيني مصغرا. وتشير النقاط المدورة باللون الأصفر والأخضر إلى الهمزة.  
تنعدم الزخرفة في هذا القرآن خاصة بالنسبة لعناوين السور، ووحدها الزخارف التي لها شكل وريدات صغيرة محاطة بنقاط متناوبة من اللونين الأزرق والأحمر تدل على الفصل بين الآيات، بينما استعملت زخارف على شكل وريدات كبيرة مزينة برقة لتقسيم الآيات إلى مجموعات مكونة من عشر آيات. ويمكن لهذه النسخة أن تشبه من حيث الخط المصاحف الزيرية. وأخيراً، تحوي ورقات المخطوط ثقبا صغيرة منتظمة جداً ضمن الهامش العلوي من كل ورقة حيث تظهر كلمة *حبوس*، التي تؤكد أن المصحف قدم كعطية دينية لمكان مقدس، يرجح أن يتواجد في مدينة فاس.

اثنان من هذا القرءان الذي كان يتألف من العديد من الأجزاء والذي يقدم منه هنا الجزء الثاني في الصفحتين 100 و 101 هما الوحيدين اللذين تم الحفاظ عليهما بالخزانة العامة بالرباط. قياساتهما قريبة من المربع؛ واستنسخا معا على الرق وبحبر بني وبخط كوفي.
keywords: قطعة دينية؛ كتابات قديمة؛ خط مغربي؛ قرآن.

en.name: Qur’an.
description:
Two books of this multi-volume Qur'an, of which pages 100 and 101 of book II are shown here, are the only ones kept in the Rabat National Library. On almost square pages, they are both in Maghrebi *kufic* script in brown ink on parchment. Although in the same style, the calligraphy in the two volumes is not the same, suggesting the work of two copyists. However, judging from the thickness of the lines, the roundness in the angles of the letters and the depth of the curves, the two styles belong to the same period and to the same Qur'an. *Kufic* script in the West started to differ from the oriental style in the second half of the AH 3rd / AD 9th century, evolving towards a style known as Maghrebi, which reached maturity two centuries later. This type of writing, which continued to obey Abu al-Aswad's archaic system of vocalisation, has no diacritical marks. Only the short vowels are represented (*fatha*, the letter A ; *damma*, the letter O, red dots over the line), *kasra* (the letter I, red dot under the line), and *shedda* (indicating the duplication of the letter) which today is written like a lower case *w*. The yellow and green round dots denote the vocal attack.  
In this Qur'an, the titles of the suras lack any specific decoration. Only small golden rosettes framed by little dots, alternately blue and red, mark the separation between the verses, whereas the big rosettes, delicately adorned, embellish the verses in groups of ten. The written forms found in this specimen could link it to Zirid Qur'ans. Some very regular small punched holes in the upper margin of every page, where the word *habus* appears, prove that this book was brought as a pious offering to a shrine, probably in Fez.

This Qur'an transcribed on parchment was offered as a pious gift to a shrine. The square format and the archaic *kufic* script with its rounded angles are characteristic of the Maghrebi calligraphy of the period. The red dots and golden rosettes mark the vowels and the separation of the verses.
keywords: religious object; calligraphy; religious manuscript

es.name: Corán.
description:
Páginas 100 y 101 del tomo II de este Corán de varios volúmenes, conservado, junto con el tomo I, en la Biblioteca Nacional de Rabat. Ambos pergaminos tienen formato casi cuadrado y están transcritos con tinta marrón en cúfico magrebí. A pesar de presentar el mismo estilo, la escritura difiere en los dos tomos, lo que sugiere el trabajo de dos copistas.  
No obstante, el grosor del trazado, la redondez de los ángulos de las letras y la profundidad de las curvas revela que las dos grafías son contemporáneas y pertenecen al mismo Corán. En efecto, en Occidente, a partir de la segunda mitad del siglo III/IX, la grafía cúfica comenzaba a distinguirse de la oriental, evolucionando hacia el estilo denominado magrebí, que alcanzaría su plenitud dos siglos más tarde.  
Este estilo gráfico, que mantiene el sistema arcaico de vocalización de Abu al-Aswad, carece de puntos diacríticos. Sólo se marcan las vocales breves (la *fatha* y la *damma* con puntos rojos sobre la línea y la *kasra* con un punto rojo bajo la línea) y la *shadda* (duplicación de letra), que se transcribe con una minúscula uve doble, como en la actualidad.  
Los puntos redondos amarillos y verdes señalan los ataques vocales. Los títulos de las suras no están decorados de manera especial. Las pequeñas rosetas doradas rodeadas de puntitos alternos en azul y rojo indican la separación de los versos, mientras que las grandes, adornadas delicadamente, marcan las series de diez versículos. La grafía de este ejemplar se asemeja a la de los coranes ziríes. Por último, las diminutas perforaciones regulares del margen superior de cada folio, donde figura la palabra *habus*, evidencian que este libro fue donado en ofrenda devota a un santuario, probablemente de Fez.

Este Corán sobre pergamino fue donado como ofrenda piadosa a un santuario. Su formato y la letra cúfica arcaica con ángulos redondeados son característicos de la caligrafía magrebí de la época. Los puntos rojos y las rosetas doradas marcan, respectivamente, las vocales y la separación entre versículos.
dates: Siglos III-IV de la Hégira/IX-X d. C.

fr.name: Coran.
description: Deux tomes de ce coran qui comportait plusieurs volumes, dont le tome II est présenté ici aux pages 100 et 101, sont les seuls qui soient conservés à la Bibliothèque générale de Rabat. De format presque carré, ils sont tous deux transcrits à l'encre brune sur parchemin en coufique *maghribi*. Mais, bien que du même style, l'écriture n'a pas la même allure dans les deux tomes, ce qui suggère le travail de deux copistes. Cependant, par le caractère épais des tracés, l'arrondi des angles des lettres et l'approfondissement des courbes, les deux graphies sont de la même époque et appartiennent au même coran. C'est en effet à partir de la seconde moitié du IIIe siècle H (IXe siècle J.-C.) que, en Occident, la graphie coufiquecommence à se différencier de la graphie orientale pour évoluer vers un style dit *maghribi* et atteindre sa maturité deux siècles plus tard. Ce style d'écriture, qui suit encore le système de vocalisation archaïque d'Abou el-Assouad, est dépourvu de points diacritiques. Seules sont représentées les voyelles brèves (la *fatha*, voyelle A, la *damma*,voyelle O : points rouges au-dessus de la ligne) ; la *kasra* (voyelle I) : point rouge au-dessous de la ligne) ; et la *chedda* (indiquant le redoublement de la lettre), transcrite comme de nos jours sous la forme d'un petit *w*.Les points ronds de couleur jaune et verte indiquent les attaques vocales. Ce coran ne porte aucun décor particulier pour les titres des sourates. Seules de petites rosaces dorées entourées de petits points alternativement bleus et rouges marquent la séparation entre les versets, tandis que les grandes rosaces délicatement ornées scandent les versets par groupes de dix. Par sa graphie, cet exemplaire peut être rapproché des corans zirides. Enfin, de petites perforations très régulières dans la marge supérieure de chaque folio, où figure le mot *habous*, prouvent que ce livre a été alloué en offrande pieuse à un sanctuaire, probablement de Fès.
dates: IIIe-IVe siècle de l’Hégire (IXe-Xe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: objet religieux ; calligraphie

en.name: An Entertainment Scene (The third day of entertainment) from *Surname-i Vehbi*
short_description: These images show events that took place on the Golden Horn on the evening of the third day. In them, we see the sultan seated in a tent on the Arsenal Palace quay surrounded by attendants. Two rafts are floating by. The one at the right, of which we can only see a part but appears to be a platform mounted on a pair of caiques, was donated by Yeğen Mehmed Pasha, Superintendent of the Customs Office. The figures of two rams suspended on gears and pulleys from the roof butt one another. This is following a real raft on which are set two gigantic dummies that face backwards and are dressed in Persian garb. At the front of the raft is a huge wheel of fireworks that one of the pyrotechnicists is causing to revolve. Its supporting frame is surmounted by a fire-spewing bird and rockets hurtle this way and that.
keywords: Levni; miniature; entertainment; Dance

en.name: Castle
description:
The Castle, like the town, was founded at the beginning of the 12th century, but all that remains today dates from Manueline improvements and consolidation built on structures of the 14th and 15th centuries.  
The solid, square keep has a high entrance door on the first floor, which was reached by a set of retractable steps, and one of the finest Manueline windows in the Beira region, with a balcony and a double span with 15th-century columns in foliate *archivolts*. There is a cross-shaped embrasure, more ornamental than functional. The uppermost part of the castle, of which only traces are now visible, had other towers besides the two that remain, and communicated with the *enceinte* below.

en.name: São Miguel (Parish Church)
names: São Miguel (Freixo de Espada à Cinta Parish Church)
description:
"This Late Gothic Parish Church was begun in the reign of D. Manuel I, and, therefore, some time before 1521. It took a while to complete, the vault dating from the time of D. João III.  
Its plan is, however, homogeneous and may have possibly been by a Biscayan architect or master builder, perhaps even João Castilho, who married a young woman from the neighbouring Spanish town of Quintanilla.  
It is a *hall-church*, with depressed vaulting supported by elongated piers, which demonstrate the great technical skill of those responsible. The portal and decorative elements are more vernacular and rude, built by less erudite men.  
The interior of the church is divided into three aisles and five bays, the vaulting being linked to the outside buttresses. The apse has three parallel chapels with simple angled vaulting, whilst the vault in the chancel is more developed with the royal coat of arms on the central boss, and the armillary sphere on the intermediate ribs.  
In the chancel, 16 panels have been preserved amongst the Baroque carvedgilded woodwork. These belonged to the 16th-century retable, which was located in this chapel until the early 18th century. They are currently distributed in a random fashion, bearing no relationship to the organisation that they would have had in the original retable. Because of their narrative sequence and their unequal sizes, the scenes from the *Life of the Virgin* and the *Childhood and Passion of Christ* were placed in rows and had an essentially pedagogical and decorative function.  
There is no historical information available as to the date and author of this work. However, its visual language and the figurative models used, allow us to place it amidst the production of Vasco Fernandes’s workshop in Viseu, and to propose a date somewhere around 1535. Despite the poor state of conservation of these panels and some already irrecoverable losses, as is the case with the *Assumption of the Virgin*, they reveal a remarkable sensitivity to the effects of light, which is used with great mastery to create space between the figures. This effect can be seen, for example, in the *Presentation at the Temple* and *Calvary*.  
The fragment of carved gilded woodwork, depicting the four writers of the Gospels, which currently stands on the altar of the right-hand chapel, might have been part of the structure of the original retable. It was probably the work of the Flemish sculptor and wood carver, Arnau de Carvalho, who worked with the painters from Viseu and made a series of retables for various churches in the region."

en.name: Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) / Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen
short_description: Portrait of Carol I, King of Romania (1839–1914) on horseback/ Karl von Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen. He was elected Prince of Romania on the recommendation of Napoleon III in 1866. In 1881, after achieving formal independence from the Ottoman Empire, Carol declared himself King of Romania.

ar.name: قطع من الجبس.
description:
تتكون هذه اللوحة من قطعتين من الجبس المنحوت بعناصر زخرفيّة مكونة من شرائط متشابكة، ومنقّطة بلآلئ (حبيبات) مطليّة باللون الأزرق على خلفيّة حمراء. تشكّل هذه الشرائط نجوماً مثمنة الرؤوس رسمت بداخلها زهور ذات ثلاث بتلات.  
كان هذا النوع من الزخارف شائعا في قصور قلعة بني حمّاد؛ وقد انمحى طلاء أغلب القطع بفعل مرور الزمن.

كسرتان من الجبس المنقوش بأشكال مكونة من شرائط مجدولة ومنقطة بلآلئ مصبوغة بالأزرق فوق خلفية حمراء، وتشكل نجوما مثمنة الرؤوس، رسمت بداخلها أزهار مؤلفة من ثلاث بتلات. وقد كان هذا الصنف من التلبيس يستعمل في زخرفة قبة دار البحر.
keywords: جبس؛ زخرفة زهريّة؛ زخرفة هندسيّة؛ طلاء؛ قصر.

en.name: Fragments of plaster.
description:
This panel is composed of two plaster fragments that have been sculpted with decorative motifs consisting of interweaving bands punctuated by blue painted pearls against a red background. These bands form eight-cornered stars, inside which appear flowers that feature three petals.  
This type of decoration is quite common in the palaces of the Qal'at Bani Hammad. The paintwork on the majority of fragments has worn off through time.

Two plaster fragments sculpted with motifs consisting of interlaced bands punctuated by blue painted pearls on a red background. The bands form eight-pointed stars containing three-petal flowers. This type of covering was used to decorate the dome at the Palace of the Sea (Dar al-Bahr).
holder: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Arts
place: Dar al-Bahr, Qal’at Bani Hammad, Algeria.
keywords: Palace; plaster; painting; geometric decoration; floral decoration; palatial architecture; architectural decoration
partner: National Museum of Antiquities and Islamic Art

es.name: Fragmentos de yesería.
description:
Este panel comprende dos fragmentos de yeso esculpidos con motivos decorativos compuestos de lacería realzada por perlas pintadas de azul sobre fondo rojo. La lacería forma estrellas de ocho puntas, en cuyo interior se distingue una flor de tres pétalos.  
Este tipo de decoración es bastante frecuente en los palacios de la Qalaa de los Banu Hammad. Por efecto del tiempo, la pintura se ha borrado en la mayoría de los fragmentos.

Dos fragmentos en yeso esculpido con lacería realzada por una línea de cuentas pintadas de azul sobre fondo rojo. La lacería forma estrellas de ocho puntas, en el interior de las cuales se distingue una flor de tres pétalos. Este tipo de revestimiento fue utilizado en la decoración de la cúpula de Dar al-Bahr (Palacio del Mar).
holder: Museo Nacional de Antigüedades y Arte Islámico
place: Dar al-Bahr de la Qalaa de los Banu Hammad (Argelia).
keywords: Palacio; yeso; pintura; decoración geométrica; decoración floral
partner: Museo Nacional de Antigüedades y de Arte Islámico

fr.name: Fragments de plâtre.
description:
Ce panneau comprend deux fragments en plâtre sculpté de motifs décoratifs composés de bandeaux entrelacés, ponctués de perles (grènetis) peintes en bleu sur fond rouge. Ces bandeaux forment des étoiles à huit pointes, à l'intérieur desquelles se dessinent des fleurs à trois pétales.  
  
Ce genre de décoration est assez fréquent dans les palais de la Qalaa des Beni Hammad. La plupart des fragments ont vu leur peinture effacée par les effets du temps.

Deux fragments en plâtre sculpté de motifs composés de bandeaux entrelacés et ponctués de perles peintes en bleu sur fond rouge qui forment des étoiles à huit pointes, à l'intérieur desquelles se dessinent des fleurs à trois pétales. Ce genre de revêtement a été utilisé dans la décoration de la coupole de Dar al-Bahr.
holder: Musée national des antiquités et des arts islamiques
place: Dar al-Bahr, Qalaa des Beni Hammad.
keywords: Palais ; plâtre ; peinture ; décoration géométrique ; décoration florale
partner: Le Musée national des antiquités et d’art musulman

en.name: Church and Convent of Jesus
names: Church of the Monastery of Jesus; Aveiro Museum
description:
The Church and Convent of Jesus date to the 15th century, though its simple architectonic plan is from the 16th century. Composed of one main chapel, it has a small rectangular nave with three secondary altars: Our Lady of the Rosary, Princess Santa Joana and St Dominic.  
The main chapel, with the royal Portuguese coat of arms, dates from the beginning of the 18th century. The gilt wood carvings were made by Portuguese carvers, António Gomes and José Correia. The Life of Princess Santa Joana cycle, painted on the side walls, is signed by the Portuguese artist Emanuel Ferreira e Sousa.  
The main altarpiece is furnished with sculptures of St. Vincent Ferrer and St. Thomas Aquinas, St. Francis of Assisi, and St. Dominic. The altarpiece throne is surmounted by a 19th-century Christ Crucified.  
The walls and panel ceiling (1685), in both the main chapel and nave, are covered with gilt wood carvings; the inferior parts with blue and white *azulejos* (tile panels), making for a very Portuguese Baroque setting.  
On the left, near the high choir, there is an 18th-century organ of polychrome wood supported by three male figures. The monumental marble tomb of Princess Santa Joana in the Low Choir was designed by the Baroque architect João Antunes.

The Church and Convent of Jesus in Aveiro were built in 1460. The single-nave church dates back to the 16th century, but its interior was redecorated during the reigns of Pedro II and João V.  
The main and secondary altars, as well as the panel ceiling with paintings from the Life of St. Dominic, are masterpieces of 17th- and 18th-century gilt wood carving. In the monastery's low-choir stands the tomb of the Princess Santa Joana. In the main chapel her life is depicted in paintings by Ferreira e Sousa.
artist: Founders: Brites Leitão, Mécia Pereira and Catarina de Ataíde; other patrons: King Afonso V, Francisco Tavares and Joana de Távora; the nobility of Aveiro, King Pedro II, King João V

Architect: João Antunes (1642–1712) – Tomb of Princess Santa Joana; main altarpiece carving: António Gomes [n.d.], José Correia (active 1725–1728/29); painter of main chapel: (Life of Princess Santa Joana cycle) Emanuel Ferreira e Sousa [n.d.]
history:
The Church and Convent of Jesus in Aveiro, which belonged to the Dominican Order, was founded in 1461 during the reign of King Afonso V, whose daughter Princess Santa Joana, lived there up until her death in 1490.  
The plan of the church dates to the 16th century, under the patronage of Francisco Tavares and Joana de Távora.  
The church underwent complete redecoration in the Baroque style in the 17th and 18th centuries. Gilt wood carvings cover the major part of the church, nave and ceiling as well as the main and side altars, thus it is a true Golden Church.  
From 1876 the Church and Convent of Jesus became redundant. In 1911, in the aftermath of the proclamation of the Portuguese Republic, the Museum of Aveiro was established in the Church and Convent.
keywords: Gilt carved wood, Golden Church, inlaid marble sculpture, Princess Santa Joana, Aveiro, *azulejos.*
tags: Gilt carved wood, Golden Church, inlaid marble sculpture, Princess Santa Joana, Aveiro, azulejos.
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: *Igreja e Convento de Jesus*
names: Igreja do Convento de Jesus de Aveiro; Museu de Aveiro
description:
A Igreja e o Convento de Jesus remontam ao século XV, embora o seu traçado arquitectónico simples seja do século XVI. Composta por uma capela principal, a Igreja tem uma pequena nave rectangular com três altares secundários: de Nossa Senhora do Rosário, da princesa Santa Joana e de São Domingos.  
A capela-mor, com as armas reais de Portugal, data do início do século XVIII. A talha dourada foi executada pelos entalhadores António Gomes e José Correia. O *Ciclo da Vida da Princesa Santa Joana*, pintado nas paredes laterais, está assinado pelo artista português Emanuel Ferreira e Sousa.  
O altar principal é enriquecido com as esculturas de São Vicente Ferrer e de São Tomás d' Aquino, de São Francisco de Assis e de São Domingos. O trono do altar é encimado por um *Cristo Crucificado* do século XIX.  
As paredes e os painéis do tecto (1685), tanto na capela-mor como na nave, são revestidos de talha dourada; as partes inferiores, com painéis de azulejos azuis e brancos, tornam a composição num verdadeiro exemplar do Barroco português.  
À esquerda, junto ao coro alto, encontra-se um órgão do século XVIII em madeira policromada, suportado por três figuras. O monumental túmulo em mármore da princesa Santa Joana, no coro baixo, foi desenhado pelo arquitecto barroco João Antunes.

A Igreja e o Convento de Jesus de Aveiro remontam a 1460. A nave central e única data do século XVI, mas o seu interior foi redecorado durante os reinados de D. Pedro II e de D. João V.  
O altar-mor e os altares secundários, bem como o tecto apainelado com pinturas sobre a vida de São Domingos, são obras-primas em talha dourada dos séculos XVII e XVIII. No coro baixo do convento, eleva-se o túmulo da princesa Santa Joana. Na capela-mor, a sua vida é relatada em pinturas de Ferreira e Sousa.
artist: Fundadoras: D. Brites Leitão, D. Mécia Pereira, D. Catarina de Ataíde; rei D. Afonso V; D. Francisco Tavares e D. Joana Távora; nobreza de Aveiro; reis D. Pedro II e D. João V.

Túmulo da princesa Santa Joana – Arquitecto: João Antunes (1642-1712); talha do altar-mor - António Gomes \[n.d.\], José Correia (activo 1725–1728/29); pinturas da capela-mor (*Ciclo da Vida da Princesa Santa Joana*) - pintor Emanuel Ferreira e Sousa \[n.d.\].
history:
A Igreja e o Convento de Jesus de Aveiro pertenceram à Ordem Dominicana e foram fundados em 1461, no reinado de D. Afonso V. A princesa Santa Joana, filha de D. Afonso V, aí viveu até à sua morte, em 1490.  
O traçado da igreja data do século XVI, sob o padroado de D. Francisco Tavares e de sua mulher, D. Joana Távora.  
A igreja foi completamente redecorada no período barroco, nos séculos XVII e XVIII. O trabalho de talha dourada cobre a maior parte da igreja, a nave central e a cobertura do tecto, bem como os altares laterais, pelo que se trata de uma verdadeira Igreja de Ouro.  
Em 1876, a igreja e o convento foram extintos. Em 1911, após a proclamação da República em Portugal, o Museu de Aveiro foi instalado na igreja e no convento.
keywords: Talha dourada, Igreja de Ouro, escultura de mármore embutido, princesa Santa Joana, Aveiro, azulejos.
tags: Talha dourada, Igreja de Ouro, escultura de mármore embutido, princesa Santa Joana, Aveiro, azulejos.

en.name: Suspended Together
description: Manal Al Dowayan’s Suspended Together can be used to question the assumption that the existence of roads, routes, and transport systems automatically means freedom of movement. Created in 2011, the installation refers to a period when Saudi women needed permission from a male guardian in order to travel. The suspended white doves suggest flight, mobility, and freedom, yet their stillness reveals a condition of restriction. In this sense, the work is especially relevant for discussing travel and infrastructure from a gendered perspective: even when roads exist, not everyone has equal access to movement. The piece reminds viewers that mobility is not only a matter of physical routes, but also of law, social permission, gender, and power. For this reason, the work can be used to expand a discussion of travel in the region beyond railways and roads, toward the unequal social conditions that determine who is allowed to move.
holder: Qatar Museums, Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
keywords: transport systems; freedom of movement; women; Saudi Arabia

en.name: Lustre-painted ewer, rooster-shaped
description:
The ewer features a sparkling play of golden lustre arabesque of curls and dots painted over opaque white glaze. The design is on the brink of perfection: along with strokes a Persian ceramist left some elements of decor in white and filled up the surrounding surface. This "reserve" technique required a particular skill and carefulness from the master. The rooster was regarded by Iranians as a ritually pure and auspicious being since pre-Islamic times.  
The art of lustre painting on ceramics was mastered by Iranian potters of Kashan in late 12th century. The technique involved application of metal-based pigment over already glazed and fired vessel.
keywords: Ewer; ceramics; lustre; Ilkhanid; Iran
materials: Stonepaste; painted in lustre over opaque glaze

en.name: National Museum of Archaeology
short_description: The Jerónimos Monastery is one of the most important examples of Manueline architecture. Its church, built in a lengthwise plan to the design of Boitaca, is divided into three naves topped by a flattened vault supported by eight towering octagonal pillars. This system provides a unified and luminous space. The main portal, which also gives access to the cloister, boasts a statuary programme depicting the Nativity. The church’s side portal, by João de Castilho, features sculptural images of the Virgin, the Apostles, Prophets, Doctors of the Church and angels. The museum is located in the monastery’s west wing which held the monks’ dormitories in the past.
artist: Architects: Master Diogo Boitaca (c.1460–1527), João de Castilho (c.1470–1552), Jerónimo de Ruão (1530–1601)
history: The National Museum of Archaeology was founded in 1893 inside the Monastery of Jerónimos, which is one of the most important testimonies to Portugal’s Great Discoveries. With 120 years of existence, the museum became a reference institution of Portuguese Archaeology having regular contacts with museums, universities and research centers across the globe.
keywords: Archaeology; Museum; Rediscovry the past; National Identiity

de.name: Kath. Dekanatspfarrkirche Hl. Veit
description: Monumentale Oktogonanlage in kräftiger Wandpfeilerbauweise. In Tirol sehr seltenes Beispiel für das Arkadenoktogon, das ein vor allem im benachbarten Bayern häufigerer Bautypus ist. Die gegen die Mitte des überkuppelten Hauptraums ausgerichteten acht Pfeiler werden von Bögen in nur gering wechselndem Schnitt verbunden. Die Anräume sind in weitgehend symmetrischer Anlage hinzugefügt. Trotz der kraftvollen, klaren Formensprache ist der Bau nicht klassizistisch, eher hochbarock zu nennen. Dagegen ist die Ausstattung aus Altären, Stuck, Fresken etc. im zeitgemäßen Stil des ausgehenden Rokoko gehalten.

Der spätbarocke achteckige Zentralbau in kräftiger, klarer Formensprache erhält durch die Ausstattung im Stil des späten Rokoko heitere, ungezwungene Züge. Seltenes Beispiel eines ‚Arkadenoktogons’ in Tirol, an dessen monumentaler Raumwirkung insbesondere die qualitätvollen Deckenbilder mit ihrem vielfigurigen Heiligenhimmel wesentlich mitsprechen.
artist:
Architekt: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726-1801)  
Maurermeister: Andrä Hueber  
Stuck: Franz Graßmayr (Zuschreibung)  
Fresken und Altargemälde: Franz Anton Zeiller (1716-1794);  
Skulpturen u. a. von Joseph Götsch (1728-1793, Zuschreibung)
history: Erstellung von Bauplänen durch den Salzburger Hofbauverwalter Wolfgang Hagenauer 1766, von Andrä Hueber ab 1772 an Stelle eines gotischen Vorgängers leicht verändert ausgeführt (gotischer Turm mit Spitzhelm einbezogen). Vollendung der Ausstattung 1782, Weihe am 21. August 1808. Der selige Engelbert Kolland, der als Franziskanermissionar 1860 in Damaskus den Märtyrertod erlitt, war 1827 in der Pfarrkirche getauft worden und wird hier besonders verehrt.
keywords: Pfarrkirche, Zentralbau, Arkadenoktogon, Deckenfresko, Heiligenhimmel

en.name: Catholic Deanery Parish Church of St. Vitus
description: Monumental octagonal building of a bold pilaster-type construction. A rare example of an arcaded octagon in Tyrol, a building type more frequently found in neighbouring Bavaria. The eight columns aligned with the centre of the domed main space are connected by arches of slightly varying cross section. The side rooms are integrated into the largely symmetrical building. Despite the bold, clear formal language, the building is to be classified as High Baroque as opposed to Classicist. In contrast, the interior work composed of altars, stucco, frescos etc. is in the style of the Late Rococo.

Thanks to its décor in the style of the Late Rococo, the Late Baroque, octagonal central-plan building in bold, clear formal language, acquires a sanguine, effortless quality. It is a rare example of an arcaded octagon in Tyrol whose masterful ceiling paintings of a heaven populated with numerous figures are in large part responsible for its monumental impression.
artist: Architect: Wolfgang Hagenauer (1726–1801); master mason: Andrä Hueber [n.d.]; stuccowork, attributed to: Franz Graßmayr [n.d.]; frescos and altar paintings: Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–1794); sculptures, attributed to: Joseph Götsch (1728–1783), Franz Xaver Nißl (1731–1804), amongst others
history: Construction plans drawn up by Salzburg’s court building administrator, Wolfgang Hagenauer in 1766, were executed from 1772 onwards in slightly amended form on the site of its Gothic forerunner (Gothic tower with pointed helm roof retained) by Andrä Hueber. The interior was complete in 1782 and the church was consecrated on 21 August 1808.
keywords: Parish church; central-plan building; arcaded octagon; ceiling fresco; Heaven of the Saints

en.name: Water women 1/5
description: The photograph, entitled *Water Women* (2016), is a striking work from the Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts that fuses portraiture, landscape and cultural symbolism into a multilayered visual narrative. By employing the technique of double exposure, the artist superimposes an image of a smiling woman carrying a water container on her head upon the typically rugged sandstone terrain and ancient steps that are characteristic of Petra. This merging of human and environment transforms the subject into a living embodiment of endurance and heritage, connecting the labour of daily survival with the monumental legacy of Jordan's desert civilisation. The photograph is indicative of themes of resilience, gender and ecology. The subject's countenance, characterised by a poised yet radiant expression, serves to create a pronounced visual contrast with the arid landscape, thereby underscoring the pivotal role women play in the sustenance of life in such inhospitable environments. The water jug positioned on her head functions as both a literal vessel of survival and a metaphorical burden, thereby echoing the carved steps and eroded stone, which are symbols of persistence and continuity through time. From a visual perspective, the warm ochres of the sandstone blend harmoniously with the cool tones of her embroidered clothing. This creates a dialogue between tradition and adaptation. The presence of an additional veiled woman, walking in the background and carrying bottled water, serves to anchor the image in contemporary realities of scarcity and modernity. Collectively, these elements form a layered composition that evokes a poetic meditation on the intersection of nature, culture and feminine strength. This work is situated within a broader discourse of Middle Eastern identity and environmental consciousness in modern photographic art.
holder: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts
keywords: woman; water; photograph; print
partner: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts

en.name: Pashmina carpet
description:
Although this piece was purchased, and came to Portugal in the 20th century, Indian carpets began arriving in Portugal as the consequence of trade in Asia from the 16th century onwards. This influx occurred within a similar time frame, although on a smaller scale, as that of Persian carpets. This large fragment was produced in Kashmir or Lahore in the middle of the 17th century, during the reign of Shah Jahan (1592‒1666); a period that itself is associated with the use of floral designs. This emperor, like Akbar and Jahangir, stood out due to his having supported artistic development through the workshops of the royal court: a similar sort of workshop production was probably responsible for this piece, and the material used and the high quality of the design both attest to this. The use of pashmina-pile knots made from the fleece of the Himalayan mountain goat (*Capra hircus laniger*) onto a silk foundation allowed for a high knot-count and consequently a very detailed design.  
Although the earliest Mughal carpets from the 16th century reveal the direct influence of Persian archetypes, by the 17th century, Mughal carpet designs would be composed of a greater number of Indian motifs (local elements, such as exotic flora and fauna). The designs had also become more naturalistic due to the impact of European botanical albums, introduced to the court through missionaries and merchants. Such is the case with this piece, which represents the sub-category of North Indian knotted-pile carpets with all-over flower and lattice pattern. This style of carpet, with its rows of flowers framed by geometrical lattices, themselves displayed in bright lac-red fields, would reach its peak during the reign of Shah Jahan, he who ordered the construction of the Taj Mahal mausoleum.
keywords: India; Lahore; Kashmir; Mughal dynasty; carpet, knotted carpet; silk; floral decoration; floral motifs; pashmina; Persian knot
materials: Silk warp and weft; pashmina pile; knotted (Persian knot, open to the left)
tags: knotted (Persian knot, open to the left)

en.name: *Khabia*
names: Water storage jar; Large earthenware jar; clay cistern jar
description:
The *khabia* is a large earthenware jar traditionally used in Morocco for the storage and preservation of drinking water. Handcrafted by skilled potters from the Marrakech region, the *khabia* was an indispensable element of both domestic and communal life before the spread of modern water supply systems. Its substantial size, often exceeding two metres in height, allowed families, mosques, or fountains to store large quantities of water drawn from wells or *khettaras*.  
The process of making a *khabia* required specialised knowledge—shaping and assembling clay coils, smoothing the surface, and firing in traditional kilns — reflecting centuries of artisanal heritage. Beyond its utilitarian role, the khabia embodied the cultural significance of water conservation in Moroccan society.  
The *khabia* displayed at the Mohammed VI Museum of Water Civilisation offers insight into vernacular technologies of storage and sustainability, serving as a reminder of how communities safeguarded water in arid environments long before industrial systems.
holder: Mohammed VI Museum of Water Civilisation
place: Acquired as representative of domestic and communal water storage tradition
artist: Traditional pottery workshops of Marrakech region
keywords: khabia; water storage; pottery; Marrakech; domestic life; water conservation
materials: Terracotta clay, hand-shaped and fired; some glazed surfaces for waterproofing
partner: Mohammed VI Museum for the Civilisation of Water in Morocco

description: On the preserved Pirot kilims of earlier date mild and calm nuances of dark blue, red and green prevail. Besides, on this kilim also appear yellow and white colours. In the middle of the central field there is a rhomboid medallion filled with *čenđeli* ornament. Inside four smaller rhombi, placed in the corners, there are interesting stylisations of a human figure surrounded by the branches with *pomegranates* (*narovi*). The rest of the central field is filled with *bibice* ornament, while the wide border (*ploča*) is decorated with the *tree of life* motif. According to Milena Vitković Žikić, a similar kilim is preserved at the Osman Pazvantoglu mosque in Vidin.
