en.name: Qazwini, Zakariya Ibn-Muhammad al-, Tuhfatu i-Gharaʾib (ʿAjaʾibu i-Mahluqat wa Gharaʾibu i-Mawjudat) (The Gift of Oddities)
description: This manuscript is a Persian copy of Zakariya Ibn-Muhammad al-Qazwini’s (1203-1283) Arabic original “Tuhfatu i-Gharaʾib” (“The Gift of Oddities”) calligraphed by the scribe Pir Husain al-Katib. This copy can be localised in Shiraz and was inspired by the Herati style however it also reflects Turkmen and Safavid styles as well. The date 1492 is mentioned in the colophon and soon after its production, it is likely that it came into the collection of Shah Tahmasp (1514-1576), whose seal can be found within. The manuscript has richly embellished double opening pages situated within a decorative blue and gold colour scheme interspersed with floral scrolls and colourful buds and flowers. There are 204 illustrations scattered across various pages of the manuscript showing constellations, zodiacal signs, celestial symbols, animals, and fantastical creatures, among other depictions. These paintings mostly occupy a small section of the text area, and often protrude into the empty margins that surround the written text. There are occasional colour abrasions in the illustrations, as well as some miniatures having been painted over in the early Safavid period, but they are mostly well-preserved.
keywords: Creation; illumination; miniature; nasta’liq; wonders
materials: Ink, opaque watercolour and gold on paper. Calligraphic *nasta‘liq* in 16 lines per page. *Thuluth* headings in blue, red and gold (Persian).

en.name: Albarello
description: An albarello (plural: albarelli) is typically an earthenware jar originally designed for medicinal purposes and used to hold apothecaries' ointments and dry drugs. The origins of this type of pharmacy jar trace back to the Islamic world. Its craftsmanship and design influence spread to Europe through Muslim-European interaction. This particular albarello exemplifies 14th-century AD Valencian ware by Muslim potters. It has a cylindrical body, tall neck, and slanting shoulder on a short foot. It is decorated in blue and lustre glazes, with seven horizontal geometric bands that include many abstract motifs favoured for pharmacy jars, including two bands bearing *al-afiya*, a stylised inscription of the Arabic word for health and happiness. While the albarello was originally used for medicines, glazed jars like this one were used for storing and transporting items like wine, water, butter, honey and olives.
dates: Hegira second half of 8th century /AD second half of 14th century
materials: Tin-glazed earthenware with lustre and cobalt blue decoration

ar.name: جامع.
description:
إنه بقايا جامع، تبين لدارسي الآثارأنه البناء المقدس الإسلامي الوحيد الباقي في جزيرة صقلية. يقع جانب المسرح القديم لمدينة سيجيستا، خارج منطقة السور المسكونة في أواخر العصور الوسطى. يبدو أنه مستطيل الشكل، طوله 20،5 م، وعرضه 11،4 م. بني في مرحلة واحدة وبتقنية واحدة ( استعمل حجر الجير والتراب للصق الاحجار ببعضها بعضاً) بنيت أرضيته بالصخر الأصم.  
محرابه مائل متجه الى الجنوب ( القبلة ) عرضه الداخلي 2 م، وطوله 1،5 م ، له بروز الى الخارج، قدره متر واحد، وليس للمنبر أي أثر.  
يبدو أن الجامع كان مقسوماً الى قسمين؛ كل قسم له ثلاثة أعمدة، لم يبق منها سوى قواعدها. ومن المفترض أنه كان مسقوفاً بالفخار نصف الأسطواني، ولا نرى الآن رواقاً ولا مأذنةً، ولم تذكر الدراسات وجود مكان للوضوء.  
يعتقد أنه جامع قروي؛ ولمَّا جاء الاحتلال النورمندي وأخذ بالتوسع، هرب بعض السكان الذين يعتنقون الإسلام، وبنوا قرية لسكناهم ومسجداً جامعاً، وليس من المعروف أنه كان مخصصاً لأهل القرية أو أنه كان عاماً. وقد وجد في جوار هذه المنطقة مدافن إسلامية.  
تقرر استعمال المنطقة لإقامة أسرة إقطاعي مسيحي جاء في نهاية القرن (السادس/ السابع) وشيدت أبنية جديدة في القرية الإسلامية، وبنيت كنيسة، وهدم الجامع، واستعملت بعض أجزائه لبناء أبنية أخرى .  
ثم هجرت القرية مرة أخرى بشكل تدريجي، وأصبحت أطلالاً في نصف القرن الثالث عشر.

تتواجد آثار المسجد في الضواحي المجاورة للمسرح القديم ل"سيجيست"، خارج الفضاء المحصن للسكن الوسيطي. وعلى التصميم، يتخذ المسجدُ شكل مستطيل متفاوت المقاييس، مع مشكاة محراب مبني بالجانب الجنوبي، وموجه توجهاً دقيقا ببضع درجات في اتجاه الجنوب الشرقي.  
من المحتمل أن الأمر يتعلق بمسجد ريفي يرجع إلى الفترة النورمندية، بني في نفس الفترة التي شيد خلالها الجزء المحصن فوق فضاء تمت تعليته من قبل ساكنة مسلمة فرت المناطق التي كان النورمانديون في طور إعادة إخضاعها.
keywords: منشأة دينية.
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

en.name: Mosque.
description:
The remains of the mosque, which at the current stage of archaeological investigation appears to be the only surviving sacred Islamic building in Sicily, are located in the immediate vicinity of the ancient theatre of Segesta, outside the fortified area of the late medieval settlement. It is laid out over an irregular rectangle 20.5 m long and 11.4 m wide, and was constructed in a single phase using a uniform building technique (limestone blocks bound with mud). The floor is bare rock. The *mihrab* niche on the south side, correctly oriented to within a few degrees of southeast, is 2 m wide on the inside and 1.5 m deep. It is rectangular on the outside and protrudes from the wall by about a metre. There are no traces of a *minbar*.  
The mosque was split into two naves by a line of three columns, of which only the bases have survived. It would have been covered with a tiled roof and did not have a porticoed courtyard or a minaret nor even, at the current stage of excavation, did it appear to have a fountain for ablutions.

The remains of the mosque can be found in the immediate vicinity of the ancient theatre of Segesta, outside the fortified area of the late medieval settlement. It is laid out over an irregular rectangle with the *mihrab* niche on the south side, correctly oriented a few degrees to the southeast. It was probably a rural mosque from Norman times, which was built, along with the fortified settlement, on high ground by an Islamicised people fleeing the lands gradually being conquered by the Normans.
history:
It was probably a rural mosque from the Norman period that was built, along with the fortified settlement, on high ground by an Islamised population fleeing the lands that were being progressively conquered by the Normans. It is not clear whether it served just the village or the entire surrounding area. An Islamic necropolis has been discovered nearby.  
The arrival of a Christian feudal lord towards the end of the AH 6th / AD 12th century saw the area become a lordly residence, with new building work carried out within the Islamic settlement and a church erected. As a result, the mosque was demolished and the building materials reused.  
The settlement was slowly abandoned and even the lord’s residence fell into ruin during the second half of the 13th century.
keywords: religious architecture
partner: Regione Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

es.name: Mezquita.
description:
Los restos de la mezquita, que según los estudios arqueológicos en curso resulta ser el único edificio islámico sagrado que ha perdurado en Sicilia, están situados en las cercanías del teatro antiguo de Segesta, fuera del área fortificada del asentamiento altomedieval. La planta es un rectángulo irregular de 20,5 m de largo por 11,4 m de ancho, levantado en una única fase constructiva con una técnica uniforme (bloques de piedra caliza con tierra como argamasa). El suelo es de piedra lisa. El *mihrab*, en el muro meridional, orientado correctamente unos cuantos grados al sureste, es de dos metros de ancho en el interior y metro y medio de profundidad; es rectangular en el exterior y sobresale del muro alrededor de un metro. No se aprecian rastros del *minbar*.  
La mezquita estaba dividida en dos naves por una fila de tres columnas, de las que se conservan únicamente las basas. La cubierta debió de ser de tejas. Carecía de patio porticado y de alminar. En el estado actual de la excavación, parece ser que ni siquiera contaba con fuente para las abluciones.  
Probablemente se trata de una mezquita rural del periodo normando que fue construida, junto con el asentamiento fortificado, sobre un alto por una población islamizada que iba abandonando los territorios conquistados por los normandos. Queda por determinar si cumplió su función únicamente en el asentamiento o también en todo el territorio circundante. En las cercanías se ha descubierto, además, un cementerio musulmán.  
La llegada del feudatario cristiano a finales de siglo determinó el uso del área como residencia señorial, con nuevas edificaciones en el centro del asentamiento islámico y la construcción de una iglesia, con la consiguiente demolición de la mezquita y la reutilización de los materiales de expolio.  
El asentamiento se fue abandonando progresivamente e incluso la residencia señorial cayó en ruinas ya en la segunda mitad del siglo VII / XIII.

Los restos de la mezquita se encuentran en las cercanías del teatro antiguo de Segesta, fuera del área fortificada del pueblo altomedieval. El edificio era de planta casi rectangular, con el nicho del *mihrab*, situado en el muro meridional, correctamente orientado pocos grados hacia el sureste.  
Se trata probablemente de una mezquita rural de época normanda, construida en un alto, junto con una fortificación, por una población islamizada que huía de los territorios que los normandos iban conquistando.
dates: Siglo VI de la Hégira / XII d. C.
keywords: arquitectura religiosa
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

fr.name: Mosquée.
description:
Les restes de la mosquée, qui, en l'état actuel des recherches archéologiques, s'avère être le dernier édifice sacré islamique subsistant en Sicile, se trouve à proximité immédiate du théâtre antique de Ségeste, à l'extérieur de la zone fortifiée de l'habitat du haut Moyen Âge. Son plan se présente comme un rectangle irrégulier, d'une longueur de 20,5 m et d'une largeur de 11,4 m, construit en une seule phase et avec une technique uniforme (des blocs de calcaire et de la terre en guise de liant). Le pavement est constitué de roche vierge. La niche du *mirhab*, sur le mur méridional, correctement orientée de quelques degrés au sud-est, présente, à l'intérieur, une largeur de 2 m et une longueur de 1,5 m ; à l'extérieur, elle est rectangulaire et saillante de 1 m environ par rapport au mur. Il n'y a pas de traces de *minbar*.  
  
La mosquée était divisée en deux nefs par une rangée de trois colonnes, dont il ne reste que les bases. Elle devait être coiffée d'un toit recouvert de tuiles et ne comportait ni cour à portiques, ni minaret, ni, en l'état actuel des recherches, de fontaine aux ablutions.  
  
Il s'agit probablement d'une mosquée rurale d'époque normande qui fut construite sur une éminence en même temps que les fortifications, par une population islamisée fuyant les territoires que les Normands étaient en train de conquérir. On ignore si elle desservait seulement le village ou tout le territoire environnant. On a également découvert, dans les abords immédiats, une nécropole islamique.  
  
L'arrivée d'un feudataire chrétien, vers la fin du VIe siècle H (XIIe J.-C.), entraîna la transformation du lieu en demeure seigneuriale, avec de nouvelles constructions au centre de l'ensemble islamique, et l'édification d'une église ; ce qui provoqua la démolition de la mosquée et le remploi des matériaux.  
  
L'ensemble fut progressivement abandonné, et même la demeure seigneuriale tomba en ruine dès la seconde moitié du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).

Les vestiges de la mosquée se trouvent dans les environs immédiats du théâtre antique de Ségeste, à l'extérieur de la zone fortifiée de l'habitat médiéval. Sur plan, elle se présente comme un rectangle irrégulier avec la niche du *mihrab*, placée sur le côté sud, correctement orientée de quelques degrés au sud-est.  
Il s'agit probablement d'une mosquée rurale d'époque normande qui fut construite, en même temps que la partie fortifiée, sur une zone surélevée, par une population islamisée fuyant les territoires que les Normands étaient en train de conquérir.
dates: VIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: architecture religieuse
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

it.name: Moschea.
description: I resti della moschea, che allo stato attuale delle indagini archeologiche risulta essere l'unico edificio sacro islamico sopravvissuto in Sicilia, si trova nelle immediate vicinanze del teatro antico di Segesta, fuori dall'area fortificata dell'abitato altomedievale. In pianta si presenta come un rettangolo irregolare, lungo 20.5 m e largo 11,4 m, costruito in un'unica fase e con tecnica edilizia uniforme (blocchi di calcare e terra usata come legante). Il pavimento è costituito da roccia vergine. La nicchia del mihrâb, sul lato meridionale, correttamente orientata di pochi gradi verso sud-est, è larga all'interno 2 m e lunga 1,5 m: all'esterno è rettangolare e sporge dal muro di circa un metro. Non vi sono tracce di minbar. La moschea era divisa in due navate da una fila di tre colonne delle quali sono rimaste solo le basi. Doveva essere coperta da un tetto con coppi e non presentava né la corte porticata, né il minareto e, allo stato attuale delle ricerche, neanche la fontana per le abluzioni. Si tratta probabilmente di una moschea rurale di epoca normanna che venne costruita, insieme all'insediamento fortificato, in zona di sommità da una popolazione islamizzata in fuga dai territori che i normanni stavano progressivamente conquistando. Non è chiaro se servisse solo il villaggio o tutto il territorio circostante. Nei pressi è stata rinvenuta anche una necropoli islamica. L'arrivo di un feudatario cristiano, verso la fine del VI/XII secolo, determinò l'uso dell'area a dimora signorile, con nuove edificazioni al centro dell'insediamento islamico e la costruzione di una chiesa, con la conseguente demolizione della moschea ed il riutilizzo dei materiali di spoglio. L'insediamento venne progressivamente abbandonato, ed anche la dimora signorile cadde in rovina già nella seconda metà del XIII secolo.

I resti della moschea si trovano nelle immediate vicinanze del teatro antico di Segesta, fuori dall'area fortificata dell'abitato altomedievale. In pianta si presenta come un rettangolo irregolare con la nicchia del *mihrâb*, posta sul lato meridionale, correttamente orientata di pochi gradi verso sud-est.  
Si tratta probabilmente di una moschea rurale di epoca normanna che venne costruita, insieme all'insediamento fortificato, in zona di sommità da una popolazione islamizzata in fuga dai territori che i normanni stavano progressivamente conquistando.
keywords: architettura religiosa
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

ar.name: الأسوار الموحدية.
description:
اختار السلطان يعقوب المنصور، مدفوعاً برغبته في تشييد عاصمة موحدية جديدة على شاكلة فاس المرينية، ومراكش المرابطية، موقعاً على الضفة اليسرى لوادي سلا (نهر أبي رقراق الحالي)، وخطط بنفسه حدود المدينة المستقبلية، التي كانت ستحمل اسم رباط الفتح، وهو الاسم الذي أطلقه جده، السلطان عبد المومن سابقاً، على القلعة القديمة الدفاعية والدينية، المشيدة في المنطقة المجاورة. أحاط السلطانُ مساحة تبلغ 450 هكتارا بسياج من الأسوار الضخمة والقوية، المحصنة ب 74 برجاً مربعاً. تمتد هذه الأسوار على طول 5263 متر، بسماكة وسطية تصل إلى 2.40 متر، وبارتفاع يتراوح مابين 7.55 متر و 8.40 متر، وشكلت، من جهتي الغرب والجنوب، تحصيناً منيعاً للمدينة التي كانت محمية سلفا بواسطة المنحدر الصخري والنهر والمحيط. وبعد وفاة السلطان يعقوب المنصور، أُهمِلَ مشروعُه الحضري، ووجب الانتظار حتى عام 1912، لتصبح الرباط عاصمة للمغرب.  
قاومت الأسوار، بعد ثماني قرون على بنائها، بشكل مثير للإعجاب، التلف الحاصل مع مرور الزمن، والتقلبات الجوية، بفضل نوعية مادة البناء، المكونة من نوع من الطابية المركبة من خليط من آجر مسحوق وحصى صغيرة مبرومة ومن الجير، يضفي عليها صلابة الحجر المنحوت.  
كانت الأسوار الموحدية لرباط الفتح لاتحتوي في الأصل إلا على خمسة أبواب: باب "العْلو"،(باب المرتفع)، وباب "الحد" (باب يوم الأحد)، باب الرواح (باب الانصراف)، وباب الحديد، وباب زعير (باب يفضي على أراضي قبيلة زعير). وفي القرن العشرين، تم فتح عدة أبواب أخرى في الأسوار، استجابة لحاجات حركة السير. وبالرغم من ذلك، فإن الأسوار قد بقيت في مجملها مصانةً بعناية، تبعا للصيغة الأصلية للبناء.

كانت مدينة رباط الفتح، وعلى غرار فاس الإدريسية ومراكش المرابطية، عاصمة موحدية، إذ خطط يعقوب المنصور بنفسه محيط سور يصل طوله إلى 6263 متر فوق مساحة تناهز 450 هكتار. كانت هذه الأسوار التي يصل معدل سماكتها إلى 2.40 متر، ويتراوح ارتفاعها مابين 7.55 متر و 8.40 متر، تشكل تحصينا قويا للمدينة. لكن، وبعد وفاة السلطان، جرى التخلي عن مشروعه الحضري، ولم تصبح الرباط عاصمة إلا في عام 1912.  
أضيفت إلى الأبواب الخمسة الأصلية المتواجدة بالسياج الحائطي فتحات عديدة حُوفظ عليها وفقا للصيغة البنائية لتلك الفترة.
dates: انتهت أشغال البناء في عام 593 هجري / 1197 ميلادي.
artist: السلطان الموحدي، أبو يوسف يعقوب المنصور، (حكم في الفترة 580 – 595 هجري/ 1184 - 1199 ميلادي).
وضع تصميم الأسوار من طرف السلطان، أبي يوسف يعقوب المنصور نفسه.
keywords: أسوار؛ تحصين دفاعي؛ طابية؛ أبراج مربعة؛ أبواب؛ رباط.

en.name: Almohad ramparts.
description:
When he wanted to build a new Almohad capital in the image of Idrisid Fez and Almoravid Marrakesh, Ya'qub al-Mansur chose a site on the left bank of the Wadi Sala (present day Bou Regreg) and drew the contours of the new city himself, which was to be called Ribat al-Fath, a name already given by his grandfather 'Abd al-Mu'min to the old religious and defensive fortress erected in the area. He surrounded an area of 450 ha with a powerful enclosure wall flanked with 74 square towers. Stretching for 5,263 m, with an average thickness of 2.40 m and at a height varying between 7.55 m and 8.40 m, these ramparts constituted a powerful fortification on the west and south sides of the town, which was already protected by cliffs, the river and the ocean.  
After the death of Ya'qub al-Mansur, his town-planning project was abandoned and it was not until 1912 that Rabat became the capital of Morocco.  
After eight centuries in existence, the wall has resisted the passage of time and the elements admirably, thanks to the quality of its construction material: concrete made of crushed bricks, small round stones and lime, a mix which made it as hard as freestone.  
The Almohad wall of Ribat al-Fath originally had only five gateways: Bab al-'Alu (the Gateway of Height), Bab al-Had (the Sunday Gateway), Bab Rwah (the Gateway of Departure), Bab al-Hedid (the Iron Gateway) and Bab Zaers (the gateway that leads to the territory of the Zaers tribe). In the 20th century, a number of other apertures were opened in the wall to accommodate the traffic, but as a whole the wall has continued to be carefully maintained according to the original masonry design.

Like Idrisid Fez and Almoravid Marrakesh, Ribat al-Fath was intended to be the Almohad capital, with Ya'qub al-Mansur himself draughting the line of a 5,263 m wall surrounding an area covering 450 ha. With an average thickness of 2.4 m and a height of between 7.55 m and 8.4 m, these ramparts constituted a formidable fortification for the town. After the king's death, his project was abandoned, and Rabat did not become the capital of Morocco until 1912. A number of openings have been added to the original five gateways in the wall, all carefully maintained using the masonry design of the time.
artist: King Abu Yusuf Ya’qub al-Mansur (r. AH 580–95 / AD 1184–99).
Ya’qub al-Mansur drew the contours of the city himself.
keywords: Enclosure wall; defensive fortification; crushed-brick mortar
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate of Cultural Heritage

es.name: Murallas almohades.
description:
Con la intención de construir una nueva capital almohade, a imagen de la Fez idrisí y la Marrakech almorávide, Yaqub al-Mansur eligió un emplazamiento en la orilla izquierda del río Sala (el actual Bou Ragrag) y delineó el perímetro de la futura ciudad, que se llamaría Ribat al-Fath, nombre dado por su abuelo Abd al-Mumin al antiguo bastión defensivo y religioso levantado en aquellos parajes. Acotó una superficie de 450 hectáreas con una espectacular muralla flanqueada por 74 torres cuadradas. De 5.263 m de longitud, la muralla tenía un grosor medio de 2,40 m y una altura entre 7,55 m y 8,40 m, constituyendo un imponente conjunto defensivo al oeste y sur de la ciudad, ya protegida los acantilados, el río y el océano.  
Tras el fallecimiento de Yaqub al-Mansur, se abandonó su proyecto urbanístico, que no fue retomado hasta 1912, cuando Rabat se convirtió en la capital de Marruecos.  
Esta muralla, en pie desde hace ocho siglos, ha resistido admirablemente el paso y las inclemencias del tiempo gracias a la calidad de sus materiales de construcción, una mampostería de ladrillo prensado, arena de grava y cal, mezcla que le confiere la dureza de la sillería. La muralla almohade de Ribat al-Fath contaba originariamente con sólo cinco puertas: Bab al-Alu (puerta de la Altura), Bab al-Had (puerta del Domingo), Bab Ruah (puerta de la Salida), Bab al-Hadid (puerta de Hierro) y Bab Zaers (puerta orientada al territorio de la tribu de los Zaers). En el siglo XX se abrieron algunas puertas adicionales para facilitar la circulación. No obstante, no han alterado el conjunto, mantenido escrupulosamente al respetarse la mampostería original.

Siguiendo el ejemplo de la Fez idrisí y la Marrakech almorávide, Ribat al-Fath iba a ser la capital almohade. Sobre una superficie de 450 hectáreas, Yaqub al-Mansur trazó él mismo el contorno de una muralla de 5.263 m. Con un grosor medio de 2,40 m y una altura entre 7,55 y 8,40 m, esta muralla constituía una poderosa fortificación para la ciudad.  
Tras la muerte del soberano, su proyecto urbanístico se abandonó; Rabat no se convertiría en capital de Marruecos hasta 1912. Varias puertas se añadieron a las cinco originales de la muralla, aunque en mampostería idéntica a la original.
dates: Terminadas en el año 593 de la Hégira / 1197 d. C.
artist: El soberano almohade Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur (r. 580-595 / 1184-1199).
Se cree que el propio Yaqub al-Mansur decidió el trazado de las murallas.
keywords: Muralla exterior; fortaleza defensiva; argamasa de ladrillo prensado.
partner: Ministry of Culture,Directorate of Cultural Heritage

fr.name: Remparts almohades.
description:
Désireux d'édifier une nouvelle capitale almohade, à l'image de Fès l'Idrisside et de Marrakech l'Almoravide, Yacoub al-Mansour choisit un site sur la rive gauche de l'oued Sala (l'actuel Bouregreg) et traça lui-même les contours de la future cité, qui devait porter le nom de Ribat al-Fath, nom déjà donné par son grand-père Abdelmoumen à la vieille forteresse défensive et religieuse érigée dans les parages. Il entoura ainsi une superficie de 450 ha d'une puissante muraille d'enceinte flanquée de 74 tours carrées. S'étendant sur 5 263 m, avec une épaisseur moyenne de 2,40 m et une hauteur variant entre 7,55 m et 8,40 m, ces remparts constituaient, à l'ouest et au sud, une puissante fortification pour la ville, déjà protégée par la falaise, le fleuve et l'océan.  
  
Après la mort de Yacoub al-Mansour, son projet urbanistique fut abandonné et il fallut attendre 1912 pour que Rabat devienne capitale du Maroc.  
  
Après huit siècles d'existence, la muraille a admirablement résisté à l'usure du temps et aux intempéries, grâce à la qualité du matériau de construction, un béton composé de briques pilées, de petits cailloux roulés et de chaux, mélange qui lui confère la dureté de la pierre de taille.  
  
L'enceinte almohade de Ribat al-Fath ne comportait à l'origine que cinq portes : Bab al-Alou (porte de la Hauteur), Bab al-Had (porte du Dimanche), Bab Rouah (porte du Départ), Bab al-Hadid (porte de Fer) et Bab Zaers (porte donnant sur le territoire de la tribu des Zaers). Au XXe siècle, plusieurs autres ouvertures ont été percées dans la muraille pour les besoins de la circulation, mais l'enceinte reste, dans son ensemble, soigneusement entretenue selon la formule de maçonnerie originelle.

à l'instar de Fès l'Idrisside et de Marrakech l'Almoravide, “Ribat al-Fath” devait être la capitale almohade.  
Sur une superficie de 450 ha, Yacoub al-Mansour traça lui-même les contours d'une muraille de 5 263 m.  
Avec une épaisseur moyenne de 2,40 m et une hauteur de 7,55 à 8,40 m, ces remparts constituaient une puissante fortification pour la ville.  
Après la mort du souverain, son projet urbanistique fut abandonné, et Rabat ne devint capitale du Maroc qu'en 1912.  
Plusieurs ouvertures ont été ajoutées aux cinq portes originelles de l'enceinte, soigneusement entretenue selon la formule maçonnique de l'époque.
artist: Le souverain almohade Abou Youssef Yacoub al-Mansour (580-595 H / 1184-1199 J.-C.).
keywords: muraille d’enceinte ; fortification défensive ; mortier à base de brique pilée

en.name: *Bust of the Cardinal Scipione Borghese*
description:
In 1605 when Paul V became Pope, he immediately made his nephew Scipione a cardinal, despite his young age, quickly promoting him to a position comparable to secretary of state. This enormous power allowed the cardinal-nephew to create a splendid home and a marvellous art collection over a decade, in an unorthodox manner.  
The bust portrait of Scipione by Gian Lorenzo Bernini was sculpted for his first major patron in 1632, after a creative hiatus of nearly seven years as a sculptor, during which he developed a new concept in portraits, more representative of the vibrant Baroque style.  
The spontaneous and intense pose, the arrangement of the bust with the head turned in a slight movement, the attentive gaze and the mouth open in an expression of vague wonderment combine to create a highly expressive, almost colloquial relation with the viewer.  
The cloth folds in the *mozzetta* (a short elbow length cape worn by Catholic clergy) and the detail of the small unfastened button showing us the live body beneath the clothes are an integral and involving part of the piece.  
The marked confidence displayed by this excellent example of a Baroque style of which Bernini was a master gives an intimate and human dimension to the sitter, despite his official status.  
With the bust almost finished, a hairline fracture opened up in the marble around the forehead, due to the stresses of the sculpting tools. The sculptor was forced to produce a second version of the bust at very short notice. This shows how little attention Bernini paid to his choice of marble, something that was of fundamental importance for other sculptors, such as Michelangelo. Despite the crack, the Cardinal requested that both works be delivered to him, keeping both in the Galleria Borghese.

Cardinal Borghese, the pope’s nephew, was a passionate collector and looked after the cultural policy of the papal court. He had a sensitive instinct for artistic quality and gave a boost to the birth of the Baroque. Bernini renders the Cardinal life-like; the transience of human feeling and the expression of inner emotions are part of the Baroque aesthetic.
keywords: Bust; portrait; marble; collection; collector; patronage; talking portrait

it.name: *Busto del cardinale Scipione Borghese*
description:
Quando Paolo V salì al soglio pontificio nel 1605 nominò subito cardinale, malgrado la giovane età, il nipote Scipione, conferendogli in brevissimo tempo una carica equiparabile a Segretario di Stato. Questo immenso potere permise al “cardinal nepote” di creare nell'arco di un decennio e in modo talvolta poco ortodosso, splendide dimore e una collezione d'arte meravigliosa.  
Il busto-ritratto di Scipione fu realizzato da Gian Lorenzo Bernini per il suo primo grande mecenate nel 1632, dopo una pausa creativa come scultore di circa 7 anni, durante i quali elaborò un nuovo concetto di ritrattistica, più rappresentativo del vibrante linguaggio barocco.  
La posa spontanea ed intensa, l'impostazione del busto con la testa girata in un leggero movimento, lo sguardo attento, le labbra dischiuse in una espressione di vago stupore, creano un rapporto quasi colloquiale con lo spettatore, di notevole forza espressiva.  
Le pieghe del tessuto della mozzetta e il dettaglio del piccolo bottone slacciato fanno percepire, al di sotto della veste, l'esistenza di un corpo vivo, sono parte integrante e partecipativa della rappresentazione.  
La vivace disinvoltura che deriva da questa alta prova di virtuosismo  tipicamente barocca di cui Bernini era eccezionale interprete rende, pur nella ufficialità del ritratto, quella dimensione intima e umana del personaggio.  
Il busto era quasi giunto a compimento quando durante la lavorazione, sotto la sollecitazione degli strumenti, si aprì un cosiddetto “pelo” del marmo, ovvero una lesione, all'altezza della fronte. Il problema costrinse lo scultore a realizzare una seconda versione del busto in tempi brevissimi. Questo dimostra come Bernini fosse noncurante nei confronti di una attenta scelta del marmo, questione invece fondamentale per scultori come Michelangelo. Malgrado la crepa il cardinale volle che gli fossero consegnate tutte e due le opere, conservate entrambe nella Galleria Borghese.

Il cardinale Borghese, nipote di Paolo V, era un appassionato collezionista e si occupò della politica culturale della corte papale. Aveva un sensibile istinto per l'arte e con le sue committenze diede un impulso importante alla nascita del Barocco. Attraverso la posa spontanea ed intensa, Bernini rende la scultura del cardinale come viva; la transitorietà del sentimento umano, l'espressione delle emozioni profonde fanno parte dell'estetica del Barocco.
keywords: Busto; ritratto; marmo; collezione; collezionista; mecenatismo; ritratto parlante

en.name: Wooden Sideboard with Mother of Pearl Inlay
short_description: This tall, intricately carved sideboard consists of two parts, the mirror section with intricately carved openwork and mashrabiya ornamentation enhanced with mother-of-pearl inlay, and the narrow table section decorated with similar elements and with its four front legs supporting an elaborate system of lobed arches. the sideboard is further enhanced by religious inscriptions, some of which seem to suggest a Christian context. Sideboards and other European-style furniture were unknown in the Middle East until the second half of the12th/ 18th century. By the 13th/ 19th century, the urban elites in Ottoman cities enthusiastically imported domestic furniture from Italy, France and England or bought locally-made hybrid pieces that combined European and traditional Islamic elements like the item shown here. Many European entrepreneurs like the Italian Furino Brothers, based in Cairo, set up shop in Ottoman cities and specialised in this so-called Arabesque style, especially fashionable for furniture.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
keywords: Furino Brothers

de.name: Stuckkartusche
description: Die Urheberschaft der exzellenten Stuckausstattung ist archivalisch nicht belegt, doch war der Meister mit Sicherheit ein Wessobrunner. Die Zuschreibung an Franz Xaver Feichtmayr, eventuell unter Beteiligung seines Bruders Johann Michael, gilt als gesichert. Es handelt sich um Rocaillenstuck von großer Feinheit, der teils auch freiplastisch und durchbrochen gearbeitet ist. Die im unteren Teil der Kartusche noch recht breiten und kräftigen Formen werden nach oben immer graziler und lösen sich gegen das Hauptfresko in zerbrechliche vegetabile C-Bögen auf, deren freies Spiel auch die Symmetrie der Kartusche aufbricht. Bei der Rückenfigur des Zwickelfreskos soll es sich um ein Selbstbildnis Matthäus Günthers handeln.
artist: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr (und sein Bruder Johann Michael, 1696-1772)

en.name: Stucco cartouche
description: The authorship of the excellent stuccowork has not been recorded although, undoubtedly, the master craftsman was a member of the Wessobrunn school. The attribution to Franz Xaver Feichtmayr, possibly with the involvement of his brother Johann Michael, is considered reliable. It is composed of rocaille stucco of the greatest refinement, which in parts has been executed in free sculptural forms and open work. As they ascend, the broad, bold forms in the lower section of the spandrel become increasingly delicate, and against the background of the main fresco dissolve into fragile vegetative tendrils, whose free play of forms also disrupts the symmetry of the cartouche. The rear-view figure in the spandrel fresco is reputedly a self-portrait of Matthäus Günther.
place: West nave bay, southeast vault spandrel
artist: Franz Xaver Feichtmayr the elder (1698–1763, attributed) and his brother Johann Michael Feichtmayr (1696–1772, attributed)

en.name: *View Looking across the Hall of Columns, Karnak*
short_description: Roberts' viewpoint across the Great Hypostyle Hall, in the Precinct of Amon-Re, at the Temple Complex at Karnak, captures in great detail the physical features of the monument as it appeared in his day. At the same time, he used exaggerated proportions to convey the structure’s imposing scale, which impressed him deeply. In his diary he writes: ’Karnak is even more astonishing than Luxor. Its magnificence is unimaginable. Trying to describe rationally what I have seen would be ridiculous’. In the 19th century,, the Karnak temple complex became one of the most famous ancient Egyptian sites visted by artists and archaeologists. During his travels up and down the Nile, Roberts captured over 300 monuments and ruins in his unprecedentedly detailed and precise works, many of them before excavation or restoration.  In his work, Roberts also drew on the pioneering scholarship of scholars like Champollion. The final depictions subtlely contributed to the Orientalist discourse on Ancient Egypt, which Europe increasingly saw as their right to appropriate.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority

en.name: Old Castle
description:
Roughly 1 km. to the north of Alcoutim, the old castle stands atop a small hill in a strategic position overlooking the River Guadiana. The surrounding area, which has not yet been completely studied, contains an important group of rural mining settlements from Islamic times, which suggest that they were to some extent dependent on the castle itself.  
The fortifications were probably built in the 3rd/9th century, since, according to archaeological data, this is the date of the castle walls (enclosing an area of little more than 700 sq. m.), as well as the cistern and the buildings that marked the first phase of settlement. The area was inhabited until the period of the *Taifa* Kingdoms in the mid-5th/11th century, and the old castle of Alcoutim was abandoned at the end of this century, with there being no evidence of its being inhabited during the Almoravid and Almohad periods.

es.name: Castelo Velho
description:
Situado a un kilómetro aproximadamente al norte de la villa de Alcoutim, el Castelo Velho (Castillo Antiguo) ocupa la cima de un cerro con buena posición estratégica sobre el Guadiana. En las inmediaciones, y aún no estudiados por completo, hay unos cuantos pueblos agrícolas y mineros de época islámica, que quizá tuvieran algún tipo de dependencia del castillo.  
La fortificación debió de edificarse en el siglo III/IX, pues de este periodo son, si atendemos a los datos arqueológicos, las murallas (que encierran un área poco mayor de 700 m2), la cisterna y los edificios de la primera fase de la ocupación. Habitado hasta las *taifas* de mediados del siglo V/m. XI, el Castelo Velho de Alcoutim fue abandonado probablemente a finales de esa centuria, y no se tienen pruebas de que estuviera poblado en tiempos de los almorávides y los almohades.

en.name: *Baliq*
description: The once black background is covered with richly stylised floral elements. The central part of the stylised flower motifs and branching patterns are reminiscent of the elements that combine to form the fish. The border consists of a wide and two narrow stripes.
dates: Date unknown, purchased by the Museum in the 19th century
keywords: Carpet; Azerbaijan; *Baliq*; stylised flower motif; fish motif
materials: Wool warp and weft; symmetrical knot

en.name: *Arab horseman*
names: 1846 sketch for the porait of Ali Ben Ahmed, the Bey of Constantine, on horseback. Currently held in the Musée de Versailles.
short_description: This piece, drawn in 1846, is a study for the portrait of 'Ali bin Ahmed, the Bey of Constantine, on horseback. The portrait is currently held in the Musée de Versailles. The artist has concentrated on his posture rather than his face, which is sparse on details. The artist came to Constantine in May 1846 and said: "This is the only truly Arab city left in this country". In 1844 he was summoned by the Bey Ahmed, who he met in France, and was commissioned to paint his portrait on horseback surrounded by his beylical guard. The prints cabinet at the Musée National des Beaux-Arts contains the final sketch for this painting, which was exhibited at the Louvre in 2003.

fr.name: *Cavalier arabe*
names: Etude pour le portrait d’Ali ben Ahmed, bey de Constantine, à cheval, peint en 1846, actuellement conservé par le musée de Versailles
short_description: Ce dessin est une autre étude pour le portrait d’Ali ben Ahmed, bey de Constantine, à cheval, peint en 1846, actuellement conservé par le musée de Versailles. Davantage d’importance est donnée à la posture du modèle, dont le visage est à peine esquissé. C’est en mai 1846 que l’artiste arrive à Constantine. Il note : « C’est la seule ville vraiment arabe qui reste dans ce pays. ». L’artiste avait été invité à s’y rendre en 1844 par le bey Ahmed de Constantine qu’il rencontre en France, ce dernier souhaitant servir de sujet à un portrait à cheval, en compagnie de sa garde rapprochée. Le cabinet des estampes du Musée national des Beaux-Arts renferme une étude au crayon montrant la composition finale de ce tableau, dessin qui fut exposé au musée du Louvre en 2003.

en.name: Game Piece
description: Chess and game pieces of the Islamic periods vary in shape and material. They appear in the form of a complex figure or as a simple abstract in different materials such a glass, ivory or stone. As a strategic war game introduced into Iran potentially from India sometime during the beginning of the sixth century, chess remained a popular game in royal and aristocratic circles. Simple glass gaming pieces such as this green coloured piece – likely a pawn – were certainly not of a royal or courtly quality, given the simplicity of its shape. It has a circular, widened base for better balance, and a spherical knob on its top.
keywords: Glass; Game piece; Moulded; Abbasid

en.name: Constantine
description:
For more than 2,000 years, Constantine has been a continuous urban community on the same site. Human settlement dates back to the Palaeolithic era. Bones dating from the Neolithic period have been found there. In the 3rd century BC, the name Cirta was used for this city of Numidian Kings. In 203 BC, Massinissa made it the capital of his centralised state. Later it became part of the Cirtec confederation under Roman rule. Destroyed by Maxentius, it would be restored by Constantine and was given his name.  
  
It subsequently became one of the Muslim states. Governed by the Aghlabids of Kairouan, it fell to the Fatimids in 295 / 908, and then to the Zirids and Hammadids, who ensured a long prosperous period. The city suffered from waves of nomadic Arab invasions, which it survived by negotiating truces and tributes.  
  
Meanwhile, it managed to sustain urban activity in a largely rural region. Upon the establishment of the Turkish Regency in Algiers it was chosen as capital of the Beylik of the East, the most populated of the three Beyliks of Algeria. Its most famous beys were Salah Bey (1184–1206 / 1770–92) and Ahmed Bey (1241–52 / 1826–37).  
  
The former distinguished himself, in 1188 / 1774, by repelling the Spaniards at Algiers, thanks to his cavalry and camel riders. He succeeded as an administrator by identifying all the oases in his territory in order to distribute water equitably. He organised and encouraged teaching in the mosques, and distinguished himself by rebuilding the Bridge of el-Kantara. Soon he came into conflict with the dey of Algiers, who strangled him. It is said that the women of Constantine wear their black veils even today as a sign of mourning.  
  
Ahmed Bey was the last bey of the city. Authoritarian and judicious at the same time, he could also be cruel. A hero of the resistance against France, he continued the struggle while preparing his state to succeed the dey of Algiers. Popular support enabled him to lead the resistance in his capital until 1252 / 1837, and in the south until 1265 / 1849.  
  
History has tied the city to its rocky perch, like an eagle’s nest cut off from its surroundings. It has remained encased for 2,000 years. Successive invaders had to destroy it to make their own. The old town is surrounded on two sides by the Rhumel Canyon, and on the third side by a cliff. From the north, via the road from Skikda, you can appreciate the city’s precarious position at the edge of an immense rock wall along the Rhumel Gorge, 75 to 150 metres deep. Or you can cross one of the bridges (Sidi Rached or el-Kantara) that connect the ancient city to the rest of the urban area. Balconies have been set up for enjoyment of the panoramic views.  
  
The medina is enclosed by the most formidable rampart there is: cliffs on all sides. Built in tiers from its Casbah down to lower quarters, and covered with red-tiled roofs, unfortunately its urban fabric has suffered disfiguring destruction. In the Ottoman era it included the high part, to the north; the Casbah; and the district of el-Kantara to the southeast. The main gates opened to the south: Bab al-Oued, Bab al-Djadid, Bab al-Djabi. The streets were lined with shops (saddlers, shoemakers, blacksmiths) and a large market. The Casbah was a separate district with barracks and a mosque.  
  
In the southern part is the Bey Palace, built by Ahmed Bey at the beginning of the 13th / 19th century – a jewel of Muslim art. The protected entrance leads to a patio defined by galleries with marble columns. Several courtyards are distributed around small gardens. Tiles of glazed earthenware and wall paintings form the core of the decoration. Frescoes depict cities and ports of the Ottoman Mediterranean: Constantine, Tunis, Rhodes and Algiers repelling Spanish forces sent by Charles V.  
  
The city had many mosques and a *zawiyas* (religious buildings). The Great Mosque was built under the Hammadids and restored under the Ottomans. Its south wall and *mihrab* date to the Hammadid period. The fluted dome of the Fatimid *mihrab* and its finely executed screens should also be noted. In the modern Constantine of today don’t miss Martyrs Square, the heart of the city; the Baths of Sidi M’sid, a hot spring – vestiges of Roman baths having made possible the construction of Olympic-size swimming pools; and Constantine University, designed by architect Oscar Niemeyer in a futuristic style (1969–72) on the surrounding plateau.  
  
The University of Islamic Sciences in Constantine is among the largest of its kind in Algeria. It was inaugurated in 1984, at the same time as the Emir Abdelkader Mosque, also a magnificent architectural monument, whose site it shares. The university welcomes approximately 3,000 students into two departments: Sharia Law and Islamic Civilisation, and Literature and Human Sciences.  
  
Constantine is the birthplace of an important school of Andalusian music. It is also famous for its cuisine and craftsmanship: metalwork, embroidery and jewellery.

fr.name: Constantine
description:
Depuis plus de 2000 ans, la ville présente une continuité urbaine sur le même site. L’implantation humaine remonte au paléolithique. On a retrouvé des ossements datant du néolithique. C’est au IIIe siècle av. J.-C. que le nom de Cirta apparaît comme cité des rois numides. En 203 av. J.-C., Massinissa en fait la capitale de son État centralisé. Elle fait ensuite partie de la confédération cirtéenne sous l’égide romaine. Détruite par Maxence, elle est relevée par Constantin et prendra son nom.  
  
Elle fait ensuite partie des États musulmans. Gouvernée par les Aghlabides de Kairouan, elle tombe ensuite aux mains des Fatimides en 295/908, puis des Zirides et des Hammadides qui lui offrent une longue période de prospérité. Elle subit les vicissitudes de l’invasion des nomades arabes, aux côtés desquels elle survit en négociant trêves et tributs. Elle parvient cependant à maintenir une activité urbaine dans une région largement dominée par le pastoralisme. C’est donc tout naturellement que, avec l’avènement de la Régence turque à Alger, elle est choisie comme chef-lieu du beylik de l’Est, le plus peuplé des trois beyliks d’Algérie. Ses beys les plus célèbres furent Salah Bey (1184-1206/1770-1792) et Ahmed Bey (1241-1252/1826-1837).  
  
Le premier s’illustra, en 1188/1774, en repoussant les Espagnols devant Alger, grâce à ses cavaliers et ses chameliers. Il se montra bon administrateur en recensant les oasis de son territoire afin de répartir l’eau équitablement. Il organisa et encouragea l’enseignement dans les mosquées et s’illustra en reconstruisant le pont d’el-Kantara. Il ne tarda pas à entrer en conflit avec le dey d’Alger, qui le fit étrangler. On dit que c’est en signe de deuil que les femmes de Constantine portent, aujourd’hui encore, leur voile noir.  
  
Ahmed Bey fut le dernier bey de la ville. Autoritaire et juste à la fois, il était parfois cruel. Héros de la résistance contre la France, il continua la lutte tout en organisant son État pour prendre la succession du dey d’Alger. Le soutien des populations lui permit de mener la résistance dans sa capitale jusqu’en 1252/1837 et dans le sud jusqu’en 1265/1849.  
  
L’histoire a accroché la ville à son rocher, nid d’aigle perché, exigu, comme coupé du reste de l’environnement. Elle y est restée enfermée 2000 ans. Les différents envahisseurs durent souvent détruire pour se faire leur place.  
  
La vieille ville est ceinte, sur deux côtés, par le canyon du Rhumel, sur le troisième par un escarpement. En venant du nord par la route de Skikda, on en prend la mesure en découvrant la ville au bord d’une immense paroi rocheuse ou en longeant les gorges du Rhumel, profondes de 75 à 150 mètres, ou encore en empruntant un des ponts (Sidi Rached ou el-Kantara) les franchissant et reliant la vieille ville au reste de l’agglomération. Des balcons sont aménagés pour jouir du panorama.  
  
La médina est enfermée dans le plus formidable rempart qui soit : des à-pics sur tout son pourtour. Bâtie en dégradé depuis la Casbah jusqu’aux quartiers bas, drapée dans ses toitures de tuiles rouges, son tissu urbain a malheureusement subi des trouées qui l’ont défigurée.  
  
À l’époque ottomane, elle comprenait la partie haute, au nord, la Casbah, et le quartier d’el-Kantara au sud-est. Les portes principales s’ouvraient au sud : Bab al-Oued, Bab al-Djadid, Bab al-Djabi. Les rues étaient bordées de boutiques (selliers, cordonniers, forgerons) et d’un grand marché. La Casbah constituait un quartier à part avec sa caserne et sa mosquée.  
Dans la partie sud, se trouve le palais du Bey, construit par Ahmed Bey au début du XIIIe/XIXe siècle et joyau de l’art musulman. L’entrée en chicane débouche sur un patio délimité par des galeries à colonnettes de marbre. Plusieurs cours se succèdent et se distribuent autour de jardinets. Carreaux de faïence et peintures murales forment l’essentiel de la décoration. Des fresques représentent des villes et ports de la Méditerranée ottomane : Constantine, Tunis, Rhodes et Alger repoussant les Espagnols de Charles-Quint.  
  
La ville comptait de nombreuses mosquées et *zaouïas*. La Grande Mosquée fut construite sous les Hammadides et restaurée sous les Ottomans. Son mur sud et son *mihrab* sont d’époque hammadide. Il faut aussi y retenir la coupole cannelée de son *mihrab*, d’inspiration fatimide, ainsi que ses claustras finement exécutés. Aujourd’hui, dans la ville moderne, on ne peut ignorer la place des Martyrs, coeur de la ville, les Bains de Sidi M’sid, source chaude, vestiges des thermes romains ayant permis la réalisation de piscines olympiques, l’Université de style futuriste, conçue par l’architecte Niemeyer. L’Université des sciences islamiques de Constantine est, quant à elle, la plus importante d’Algérie. Elle a été inaugurée en 1984, en même temps que la Grande Mosquée Émir-Abdelkader, qui est aussi un magnifique monument architectural, dont elle partage les bâtiments. Elle accueille environ 3000 étudiants répartis dans deux facultés (Faculté de la charia et de la civilisation islamique et Faculté de littérature et des sciences humaines).  
  
Constantine est le berceau d’une grande école de musique andalouse. Elle est aussi célèbre pour sa cuisine et son artisanat : dinanderie, broderie, orfèvrerie.

en.name: *Letta Asım Baloya Giderken* (*Letta Asım was about to go to a ball*)
short_description: As a result of modernization efforts and the increase in relations with the West in the 19th century, there were significant changes in Ottoman social life. Instead of the traditional 18th-century entertainment which consisted of miniatures, in Tanzimat Period of the 19th century, theatre, opera, musical performances and ballrooms became popular in Istanbul. In public places, western-style dance and musical instruments began to be seen.

en.name: Pair of clogs
description:
The high heeled clogs (ar. *qabqab*, tr. *nalın* are an emblematic item of the hamam reflecting the atmosphere of such public baths. They were worn when entering the bath complex to protect the wearer from the dirty water as well as from the hot marble floor. Wearing these shoes meant that the wearer was obliged to walk slowly to avoid falling. This slower pace was in tune with the temporality dictated by the rhythms of the hamam and its cleansing rituals.  
  
This pair of clogs is attributed to Syria. They are made of wood inlaid with silver and multi-coloured triangular pieces of mother-of-pearl. The front and rear parts of the sole are incrusted with repoussé silver bands decorated with floral motifs encircled with two dotted lines. They are embellished with long silver chains ending in trinkets which must have created a gentle tinkling with each step highlighting the sound dimension of the hamam.  
  
The strap holding the foot is made of various layers of leather for comfort. It is topped with a large silver band intricately designed and solidly nailed to the sole.  
  
This pair of clogs is particularly high, suggesting that it might have been the property of the hamam owner who traditionally wore sophisticated clogs with heels higher than those of the clients. Often offered as part of the dowry of the bride in a toiletry trousseau providing her with all the hamam essentials, the clogs were a statement on the social status of their owner and could also bear many symbolic meanings through their decoration.  
  
Although strongly associated with femininity, hamam clogs, with lower heels and different ornamentation, were also worn by men in their own establishments.
keywords: Water; clogs ; Ottomans; hammam, ablutions; qabqab; nalın
materials: Wood with silver and mother-of-pearl overlay
tags: Wood with silver and mother-of-pearl overlay
partner: Museum of the Arab World Institute

en.name: *Kitarah* (Curved single-edged Sword with Kattara Hilt)
description: This curved, single-edged sword with Kattara hilt from the al-Busaid Dynasty demonstrates the use of Arabesque, a specific decorative element consisting of a continuous branching stem with split palmate leaves to decorate Islamic weaponry. In a larger sense, the word Arabesque is used to refer to an entire range of designs based on stylised floral, foliar and animal motifs, the aesthetics of which are derived from the imposition of order on the natural world. Arabesque patterns are used extensively in traditional Omani woodwork, plasterwork and metalwork as a means of covering entire surfaces or precise areas within a defined geometric framework.
keywords: Sword; Kattara; Arabesque; Weaponry

en.name: The Damascene Hall
short_description: In the eastern part of Wilhelma, towards the R. Neckar, is the Damascene Hall. It is the only one of the historical buildings that was not built by the royal architect Karl Ludwig von Zanth, but, after his death, by Professor Wilhelm Bäumer in 1864. It served Wilhelm I as a building for keeping pheasants and chickens. The name comes from that of the inhabitants of the town of Damascus, which used to be a centre of the Moorish style of building. The Damascene Hall was the only one of the historical buildings at Wilhelma to have survived the war undamaged. Despite this it was still very carefully restored in 1992. A small part of the old Moorish splendour of Wilhelma is to be seen here in the sumptuous ceiling painting, the stucco marble of the walls and the wonderful chandelier.
holder: Wilhelma, Zoological and Botanical Garden Stuttgart
history:
King Wilhelm I of Württemberg commissioned to Karl Ludwig von Zanth in 1837 the design of Moorish style buildings for his Wilhelma garden. The architect planned and built all the buildings with the exception of the Damascene Hall.  
The idea was not to reproduce faithfully the Islamic art but to lend an “oriental” flair to the garden. The mention of an “oriental garden” conjured up visions of elegance, luxury, colourful brilliance, seduction and eroticism.  
The Moorish style recalls the Islamic art of Spain and North Africa between the 12th and 15th centuries which reached its zenith in the Alhambra. It was fashionable in 19th century: Wilhelma is also known as the “Alhambra on the river Neckar” and other buildings – synagogues in Berlin and Vienna for example – were built in the Moorish style.
keywords: Moorish style; Alhambra; Romanticism; gardens

ar.name: برج الذهب (توري ديل أورو).
description:
ابتداءاً من عام 541 / 1147 ، وهي السنة التي فتح فيها الموحدون اشبيلية التي كانت تحت حكم المرابطين، ترك برنامج الأشغال العمومية للحكومة الجديدة بصمة قوية على المدينة.  
خلال الثلث الأول من القرن السابع / الثالث عشر، وعندما كانت السيطرة الموحدية في أدنى مستوياتها، تم تمديد سور القصر وأبراج مختلفة حتى النهر، حيث جرى تشييد بنية دفاعية قوية: برج الذهب (توري ديل أورو). لقد أتاح شكله المثمن مجالاً واسعاً للمراقبة وشكَّل الطرف الأكثر تقدماً لكل المركب الدفاعي للمدينة. وقد كان الهدف من هذا البرج حماية الميناء، وتأمين التجارة النهرية، وفي حالة الحصار، قطع الممر إلى المدينة عبر النهر.  
يرجع البدنان السفليان فقط، ضمن الأجزاء الثلاثة التي تشكل البرج، إلى الفترة الموحدية؛ في حين يعود العزري، الذي يتواجد فوق البدن العلوي، إلى بناء من القرن الثامن عشر. شُيِّدَ البدنُ السفلي من الطابية (التراب المدكوك) ودُعِّمَ في الزوايا بأحجار منجورة من الصلصال الرملي، ويصل ارتفاعه إلى 20.70 متراً. جرى تشكيل قاعدته من موشوري ذي اثنتي عشرة زاوية، يأوي بداخله بنية مسدسة الأضلاع حيث يتواجد الدرج المؤدي إلى الطوابق الثلاث وإلى السطح. وغُطيَ كل طابق بقبوات متقاطعة، مثلثة ومربعة بالتناوب. وعند مستوى السطح، يتحول الموشوري الداخلي إلى شكل ذي اثنتي عشرة زاوية ليُشكل البدنَ الثاني، الذي يبلغ ارتفاعه إلى 8.15 أمتار. شُيِّد هذا الأخير من الآجر، ومُلئَ داخلُه، الذي لم يترك إلا فراغاً أسطوانياً حيث يتواجد الدرج الحلزوني الذي يتم الولوج عبره إلى السطح الثاني؛ وكُلِّلَ السطحان معاً بحواجز متدرجة.  
يقدم البرج لشبه الجزيرة الإيبيرية شكلاً جديداً، يتمثل في استعمال الفخار المبرنق من أجل الزخرفة الخارجية. فقد غُطيت ركنيات العقود المصمتة بتلبيسات من الخزف المبرنق الأبيض والأخضر (الزليج) الذي يشكل معينات، وهي التركيبة الزخرفية التي سوف تصبح مألوفة فيما بعد. وبحسب مصدر يرجع لمنتصف القرن السابع عشر، فإن اسم البرج يأتي من الزليج المذهب الذي كان يغطيه.

من أجل حماية الميناء النهري، وتأمين حركة السير، وقطع المرور إلى المدينة في حالة الحصار عبر الوادي الكبير، مدد الموحدون سور القصبة الإشبيلية حتى النهر وشيدوا هذا البرج البراني المدمج إلى هذه الأخيرة والمسمى برج الذهب بسبب الزليج المذهب المنقرض حاليا والذي كان يغطي واجهاته. كان شكله المثمن الفريد والذي يبقى مصدرا لشهرته ملائما لفتح مرامي تسهل المراقبة. أما الجسم الذي يعلو البرج فهو إضافة ترجع إلى القرن 12 الهجري / القرن 18 الميلادي.
keywords: آجر؛ اشبيلية؛ برج الذهب؛ تحصين؛ حجارة منجورة؛ خزف / فخار مبرنق؛ دفاع؛ زليج؛ صلصال رملي؛ طابية / تراب مدكوك؛ موحدون.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

en.name: Golden Tower (Torre del Oro).
description:
The new government's programme of public works, commencing after the Almohads captured the city of Seville from the Almoravids in AH 541 / AD 1147, left a great impression on the city.  
In the first third of the AH 7th / AD 13th century, with the Almohads already in decline, the wall of the citadel, with a number of intermediary towers, was extended to the river, where a great defensive structure was erected: the Golden Tower. Its polygonal shape afforded a wide view and it was the most advanced part of the defensive system intended to protect the port, ensure river traffic and prevent access to the city from the river in the event of a siege.  
Only the lower two of the three parts that make up the tower are from the Almohad period. The lantern on top of the higher part was built in the 18th century.  
The lower part, with its adobe construction reinforced with sandstone ashlars in the corners, is 20.70 m high. The base is a 12-sided volume containing a hexagon that houses the staircase providing access to the three upper floors and the terrace. Each of the floors is covered with alternating triangular and square arris vaults. At the height of the terrace, the inner volume changes into a dodecagon to shape the subsequent part, 8.15 m high. Made of brick, it was solid, leaving only a cylindrical space to contain the spiral staircase that leads to the second terrace. Both terraces are finished with crenellated parapets.  
The tower was unique in the peninsula in its use of glazed clay to decorate the outside surfaces. The spandrels of the blind arches are covered with ceramic tiles glazed white and green to form rhomboids, a theme that would later become widespread. According to a chronicle from the 17th century, the name of the tower derives from the golden tiles that covered it.  
The vaults and the second part of the tower were seriously affected by an earthquake in 1755. In 1760, this part and the first floor of the lower part were filled in, and a third part was built: a lantern crowned by a semi-hemispheric cupola.

In order to protect the river port, and its traffic and to prevent access to the city via the Guadalquivir at times of siege, the Almohads extended the wall of the Seville citadel to the river and built a flanking tower into it. This tower was known as the ‘golden tower’ because of its covering of golden tiles, now lost. The unique 12-sided shape for which it is famous allowed for openings that facilitated its use as a watchtower. The uppermost part of the tower was added in the AH 12th / AD 18th century.
keywords: Golden Tower; Seville; Almohads, fortification; defence; flanking tower; adobe; ashlars, sandstone; brick; glazed clay
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

es.name: Torre del Oro.
description:
A partir de 541 H. / 1147 d. C., año en que los almohades conquistaron la ciudad de Sevilla, entonces en poder de los almorávides, el programa de obras públicas del nuevo gobierno dejó en la ciudad una fuerte impronta.  
  
En el primer tercio del siglo VII H. / XIII d. C., ya en el periodo de decadencia almohade, la muralla del alcázar, con varias torres intermedias, fue prolongada hasta el río, y allí se alzó una gran defensa: la Torre del Oro. Su forma poligonal permitía un amplio campo de observación y constituía el extremo más avanzado del conjunto defensivo, cuyo fin era proteger el puerto, asegurar el tráfico fluvial y, en caso de asedio, cortar el acceso a la ciudad por el río.  
  
De los tres cuerpos que componen la torre, sólo los dos inferiores son de época almohade. La linterna que remata el cuerpo superior es obra del siglo XVIII.  
  
El cuerpo inferior, construido en tapial y reforzado en las esquinas por sillares de piedra arenisca, tiene 20,70 m de altura. Su base está formada por un prisma dodecagonal que aloja en su interior otro hexagonal, donde se encuentra la escalera para acceder a las tres plantas y terraza. Cada uno de los pisos se cubre con bóvedas de arista, triangulares y cuadradas alternativamente. A la altura de la terraza, el prisma interior se convierte en dodecagonal para formar el siguiente cuerpo, de 8,15 m de altura. Construido en ladrillo, su interior está macizado y deja solamente un hueco cilíndrico en el que se sitúa la escalera de caracol por la que se accede a la segunda terraza. Ambas terrazas se rematan con parapetos almenados.  
  
La torre ofrece la novedad, en la Península, de emplear barro vidriado en la decoración de exteriores. Las albanegas de los arcos ciegos se cubren con placas de cerámica vidriada en blanco y verde formando rombos, tema que luego se hará frecuente. Según una crónica de mediados del siglo XVII, el nombre de la torre proviene de los azulejos dorados que la cubrían.  
  
Como consecuencia del terremoto de 1755, las bóvedas y el segundo cuerpo de la torre quedaron gravemente afectados. En 1760 se macizaron ese cuerpo y la primera planta del inferior, y se construyó un tercer cuerpo, una linterna de remate coronada por una cúpula semiesférica.

Para proteger el puerto fluvial, asegurar el tráfico y cortar el acceso a la ciudad por el Guadalquivir en caso de asedio, los almohades prolongaron la muralla del alcázar sevillano hasta el río y construyeron, unida a ella, esta torre albarrana, llamada del Oro por los azulejos dorados que la recubrían, hoy perdidos. Su forma dodecagonal, única y fundamento de su fama, propició la abertura de vanos, que facilitaron la vigilancia. El cuerpo que remata la torre es un añadido del siglo XII H. / XVIII d.C.

fr.name: Torre del Oro (tour de l’or).
description:
À partir de 541 H / 1147 J.-C., année où les Almohades conquirent Séville alors au pouvoir des Almoravides, le programme de travaux publics du nouveau gouvernement laissa une puissante empreinte dans la ville.  
Au cours du premier tiers du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J. C.), alors que la suprématie almohade était déjà déclinante, la muraille de l'alcazar, avec diverses tours intermédiaires, fut prolongée jusqu'au fleuve, où l'on érigea une puissante structure défensive : la Torre del Oro (la tour de l'or). Sa forme polygonale permettait un large champ d'observation et constituait l'extrémité la plus avancée du complexe défensif de la ville. Elle avait pour finalité de protéger le port, d'assurer le trafic fluvial et, en cas de siège, de couper l'accès à la cité par le fleuve.  
Des trois parties qui composent la tour, seuls les deux corps inférieurs sont d'époque almohade. La lanterne qui surmonte le corps supérieur est un ouvrage du XVIIIe siècle. Le corps inférieur, construit en pisé et renforcé aux angles par des pierres de taille en grès, s'élève à 20,70 mètres de hauteur. Sa base est formée par un prisme dodécagonal qui loge dans son intérieur un corps hexagonal où se trouve l'escalier conduisant aux trois étages et à la terrasse. Chaque étage est couvert par des voûtes d'arêtes, alternativement triangulaires et carrées. À hauteur de la terrasse, le prisme intérieur devient dodécagonal pour former le second corps, de 8,15 mètres de hauteur. Construit en briques, son intérieur est massifié et ne laisse qu'un creux cylindrique où se trouve l'escalier en colimaçon par lequel on accède à la seconde terrasse. Les deux terrasses sont couronnées de parapets crénelés.  
La tour offre la nouveauté, pour la péninsule Ibérique, d'utiliser l'argile vernissée pour la décoration extérieure. Les écoinçons des arcs aveugles sont couverts de placages de céramique vernissée en blanc et vert formant des losanges, thème qui deviendra fréquent par la suite. Selon une chronique du milieu du XVIIe siècle, le nom de la tour provient des *azulejos* dorés qui la couvraient.  
Conséquence du tremblement de terre de 1755, les voûtes et le deuxième corps de la tour restèrent gravement endommagés. En 1760, cette partie et le premier étage du niveau inférieur furent massifiés et l'on construisit un troisième corps, surmonté d'une lanterne sommée d'une coupole hémisphérique.

Afin de protéger le port fluvial, sécuriser le trafic et, en cas de siège, couper l'accès à la cité par le Guadalquivir, les Almohades prolongèrent la muraille de la forteresse sévillane jusqu'au fleuve et construisirent, intégrée à celle-ci, cette tour *albarrana*, appelée Tour de l'or en raison des azulejos dorés, aujourd'hui disparus, qui la recouvraient. Sa forme dodécagonale, unique, et qui est à l'origine de sa renommée, était propice à l'ouverture d'embrasures qui facilitaient la surveillance. Le corps qui surmonte la tour est une adjonction du XIIe siècle H (XVIIIe siècle J.-C).
artist: Abou l-Oula, gouverneur almohade de Séville.

partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Fine Arts

en.name: *Convoy of pilgrims*
short_description: The Hijaz Railway was a narrow-gauge railway (1,050mm/​3ft, 5 11⁄32 in track gauge) that ran from Damascus to Medina, through the Hijaz region of Saudi Arabia, with a branch line to Haifa on the Mediterranean Sea. It was a part of the Ottoman railway network and was built to extend the line from the Haydarpaşa Terminal in Istanbul beyond Damascus to the holy city of Mecca. It got no further than Medina, 400 kilometres (250mi) short of Mecca, due to the construction interruption caused by the outbreak of World War I. The main purpose of the railway was to establish a connection between Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire and the seat of the Islamic Caliphate, and Hijaz in Arabia, the site of the holiest shrines of Islam and the holy city of Mecca, the destination of the Hajj (annual pilgrimage).
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
keywords: Yıldız Album; II. Abdulhamid Han; Photograph pilgrims; pilgrimage; travelling
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

de.name: Mariae-Himmelfahrts-Altar (Hochaltar)
description: Der pompöse, 14 x 20 Meter messende Hochaltar zeigt mittels Malerei und Skulptur die Himmelfahrt Mariens. Das Altarblatt ist versenkbar und gibt dann auswechselbare Kulissenszenerien preis, mit deren Hilfe noch heute an den Hochfesten theaterhaft die Heilsgeschichte dargestellt wird. Beidseitig flankieren den Hochaltar vier überlebensgroße Figuren der Kirchenväter – ihres gemessenen Pathos wegen Hauptwerke der bayerischen Barockskulptur.
artist: Vorentwurf zu Altararchitektur und Skulpturen: Egid Quirin Asam (1692-1750); Ausführungsentwurf zur Altararchitektur: François de Cuvilliés (1695-1786); Skulpturen: Johann Joachim Dietrich (1690-1735); Altarblatt: Balthasar Augustin Albrecht (1687-1765)

en.name: The Altar of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary (high altar)
description: The grandiose high altar, measuring 14 x 20 metres, depicts the Assumption of the Virgin Mary into Heaven through the media of painting and sculpture. The altarpiece can be retracted, revealing interchangeable backdrops which are used to assist with the theatrical displaying of salvation history on different feast days. Four larger-than-life statues of the Church Fathers flank the high altar on both sides – truly they are crowning achievements of Bavarian Baroque sculpture on account of their solemn expressionalism.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: سيرة حياة النبي.
description:
تمَّ تدوين العمل باللغة التركية على ورق (أحارلي) أنيق مصقول، بمعدَّل 13 سطراً للصفحة، كتبت بخط نسخي كبير. كتب النص بحبر أسود ضمن حواشٍ مذهَّبة، وكتبت أسماء الأعلام بالحبر الأحمر. أما الفراغات بين أسطر النص فقد وُشِّيت بطلاء ذهبي ذي حواف سوداء. تروي المجلدات الستة لسيرة النبي قصة حياة النبي محمد وتاريخ الإسلام حتى وفاته. والمجلد الموجود في متحف الفنون التركية والإسلامية هو نسخة عن المجلد الرابع ويضم 545 ورقة. وثمة 193 منمنمة بالإجمال تصوِّر المواضيع المتضمَّنة. الصفحة الأولى، وهي صفحة عنوان الكتاب، نفذت بالألوان الساطعة ووشَّت بالذهب. الرسوم الواردة في صفحات المنمنمات واقعة بين سطرين من النص في أعلى الصفحة وسطرين في أسفلها. تمَّ تزيين الغلاف الجلدي البني للمجلد برصيعة بيضوية الشكل ذات دلايات سعفية وحليات للزوايا.  
  
يُستهل المجلد الرابع بولادة ابنة النبي، فاطمة، ويتابع قصة زواجها من علي، ثم معجزات محمد، وحبه لطلحة وحمزة، وقصص النساء المسلمات البطلات، والاستعداد لمعركة بدر، ووصف المعركة نفسها، وجَرح محمد في معركة أحد، ومقتل عم النبي حمزة، وتوزيع غنائم الحرب، وقصة كعب وابنته، ومقتل عدو المسلمين، سفيان بن خالد.  
  
أُعدَّت سيرة النبي في ستة مجلدات، في مشغل القصر، بأمر من السلطان مراد الثاني في القرن 10 / 16. وقد فُقد مجلد منها، بينما باقي المجلدات موزعة حالياً في مكتبات حول العالم. أما المخطوطة الموجودة في متحف الفنون التركية والإسلامية فهي نسخة (أنجزت في القرن 11 / 17) عن مخطوطة المجلد الرابع لسيرة النبي الموجودة في مكتبة تشيستر بيتي في دبلن في أيرلندا (T. 419). وتعتبر المنمنمات نموذجاً نمطياً لأسلوب تلك الفترة.

نسخة "سيرة النبي" هذه، العائدة إلى القرن الحادي عشر الهجري/ السابع عشر الميلادي، تتمتَّع بمكانة مهمة في الفن العثماني، ليس بسبب الكتاب وحسب، بل ونتيجة تجليده، والأسلوب التصويري لنمنماته، وتشكيلاته المعمارية.
artist: الخطاط الذي دوّن هذا العمل غير معروف؛ أما الرسام الذي نفذ رسوماته فهو سيِّد سليمان قاسم باشا.
keywords: تلوين مائي؛ توشية بالذهب؛ حبر؛ رسم الغلاف الجلدي؛ ورق؛ ورنيش.

en.name: *Siyer-i Nebi* (‘Biography of the Prophet’).
description:
The work is written in Turkish on delicate finished (*aharlı*) paper using 13 lines per page of large *naskhi* script. The text is written within gilded margins in black ink; proper names are written in red ink. The areas between the lines of text are filled with gilding whose edges are traced in black. The six-volume *Siyer-i Nebi* or 'Biography of the Prophet' tells of the life of the Prophet Muhammad and of the history of Islam up until his death. The volume in the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts is a copy of the fourth volume and has 545 folios. A total of 193 miniatures depict the subjects within. The first page, an illuminated title page, is decorated with gilding. On those pages with miniatures, the painting is situated between the top and bottom two lines of text. The volume's brown leather binding is adorned with an oval medallion with palmette pendants and corner-pieces.  
  
The fourth volume begins with the birth of the Prophet's daughter, Fatima, and goes on to describe her marriage to 'Ali; the miracles of Muhammad; the love of Talha and Gamza; tales of heroic Muslim women; the preparation for the battle of Badr and the battle itself; Muhammad's wounding at the battle of Uhud; the death of the Prophet's uncle Hamza; the distribution of the spoils of war; the story of Ka'b and his daughter; and the killing of the Muslims' enemy, Sufyan ibn Khalid.  
  
*Siyer-i Nebi* was prepared in six volumes by the palace atelier at the behest of Sultan Murad III in the AH 10th / AD 16th century. Today one volume is lost, while the others are dispersed in libraries around the world. The manuscript in the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts is a copy (made in the AH 11th- / AD 17th-century) of a manuscript of the fourth volume of *Siyer-i Nebi* in the Chester Beatty Library in Dublin, (T. 419). The miniatures are stylistically typical of the period.

This AH 11th- / AD 17th-century copy of *Siyer-i Nebi*, literally 'Life of the Prophet', has an important place in Ottoman art not only because of subject but also because of its binding, the figurative style of its miniatures, and its architectural compositions.

es.name: Biografía del Profeta *(Siyer-i Nebi)*.
description:
La obra está escrita en turco en grandes letras *nasji* sobre un delicado papel trabajado *(aharlı)* con trece líneas por página. El texto está escrito en tinta negra dentro de márgenes dorados. Los nombres propios aparecen en rojo. Las zonas que quedan entre los renglones están decoradas con un fondo dorado perfilado en negro. Los seis volúmenes de la *Siyer-i Nebi* o biografía del Profeta relatan la vida de Muhammad (Mahoma) y la historia del Islam hasta la muerte de él. El ejemplar que se conserva en el Museo de Arte Turco e Islámico es una copia del cuarto volumen y tiene 545 folios. Un total de 193 miniaturas ilustran los temas. La primera página, una portada ilustrada, está decorada en dorado. En las páginas con miniaturas, las iluminaciones están situadas entre dos renglones, uno por encima y otro por debajo. El cuero marrón de la encuadernación está adornado con un medallón ovalado con arracadas de palmetas y piezas esquineras.  
El cuarto volumen comienza con el nacimiento de la hija del Profeta, Fátima, y continúa con la descripción de su boda con Ali; los milagros de Muhammad; el amor de Talha y Gamza; los relatos de heroicas mujeres musulmanas; la batalla de Badr y sus preparativos; la herida de Muhammad en la batalla de Uhud; la muerte de Hamza, tío del Profeta; la distribución de los botines de guerra; la historia de Kaab y su hija; y el asesinato de Sufyan ibn Jalid, enemigo de los musulmanes.  
La biografía se redactó en el taller de palacio, en el siglo X / XVI, a petición del sultán Murad III. Uno de los volúmenes se ha perdido y los demás están repartidos por bibliotecas de diversas partes del mundo. El manuscrito del Museo de las Artes Turcas e Islámicas es una copia (realizada en el siglo XI / XVII) de un manuscrito del cuarto volumen que está en la biblioteca Chester Beatty de Dublín (Irlanda) (T.419). Desde el punto de vista estilístico, las miniaturas son típicas del periodo.

Esta copia del siglo XI / XVII de *Siyer-I Nebi*, literalmente "Vida del Profeta", es importante en el arte otomano no sólo por el tema que trata, sino también por su encuadernación, por el estilo figurativo de sus miniaturas y por sus composiciones arquitectónicas.

fr.name: *Siyer-i Nebi* (Biographie du Prophète).
description:
Ouvrage copié en turc sur un délicat papier préparé. Chaque page contient 13 lignes de texte rédigées en grande écriture *naskhi*, comprises entre des marges tracées à l'encre noire et à l'or. Les noms propres sont mentionnés à l'encre rouge. Les espaces entre les lignes sont occupés par une dorure à contours noirs. En six volumes, cet ouvrage raconte la vie de Mahomet et l'histoire de l'islam jusqu'à la mort du Prophète. Le manuscrit du musée d'Istanbul, copie du quatrième volume, compte 545 folios illustrés de 193 miniatures. La première page est la page de titre, ornée d'enluminures et de dorures. Les peintures sont chaque fois insérées entre deux lignes de texte. La reliure en cuir brun est ornée d'un médaillon ovale à lambrequins en palmette et coins ornés.  
Ce quatrième tome commence par la naissance de la fille du prophète, Fatima, décrit son mariage avec Ali, les miracles de Mahomet, l'amour de Talha et de Gamza, des récits de la vie d'héroïnes musulmanes, les préparatifs de la bataille de Badr et la bataille elle-même, la blessure de Mahomet à la bataille de Uhud, la mort de l'oncle du prophète Hamzah, la distribution des butins, l'histoire de Ka'b et de sa fille et l'assassinat de l'ennemi des musulmans Sufyan ibn Khalid.  
Les six volumes du *Siyer-i Nebi* ont été réalisés par l'atelier du palais à la demande du sultan Mourad III au Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.). Un volume a été perdu et les quatre autres sont dispersés dans divers musées dans le monde. Le manuscrit du Musée des arts turcs et islamiques est une copie du XIe siècle H (XVIIe siècle J.-C.) d'un manuscrit du quatrième volume actuellement à la Chester Beatty Library de Dublin, en Irlande (T. 419). Le style de ses miniatures est caractéristique du XIe/XVIIe siècle.

Cette copie du *Siyer-i Nebi* (littéralement “vie du Prophète”) du XIe siècle H (XVIIe siècle J.-C.) occupe une place importante dans l’art ottoman, non seulement du fait de son sujet mais aussi en raison de sa reliure, du style figuratif de ses miniatures et de ses compositions architecturales.

tr.name: Siyer-i Nebi.
description:
Eser, ince aharlı kağıt üzerine iri nesih hat, 13 satır olarak Türkçe olarak yazılmıştır. Metin altın yaldızla çekilmiş cetveller içine siyah mürekkeple, metinde geçen özel isimler ise kırmızı mürekkeple yazılmıştır. Satır araları altın yaldızla doldurulmuş ve doldurulan bölümlerin etrafı siyah renkle konturlanmıştır. Siyer-i Nebi, Hz. Muhammed'in hayatı ve ölümüne kadar İslam tarihini anlatan altı ciltlik bir eserdir. 545 varaktan oluşan TİEM nüshası ise bu eserin, dördüncü cildinin kopyasıdır. İçinde konuyla ilgili 193 adet minyatür yer alır. Eserin ilk sayfası tek sayfa serlevha şeklinde düzenlenmiş ve tezhiplerle süslenmiştir. Minyatürlü sayfalarda ise minyatür, altta ve üstte iki satırlık metin arasında yer almaktadır. Eserin kahverengi deri cildi, palmet salbekli oval şemse ve köşebentlerle süslüdür.  
  
Hz. Muhammed'in kızı Fatma'nın doğumu ile başlayan eserde, Hz. Ali ile Fatma'nın evlenmesi, Hz. Muhammed'in mucizeleri, Talha ve Gamze'nin aşkları, kahraman müslüman kadınların öyküleri, Bedir savaşına hazırlık ve savaş, Uhud savaşı sırasında Hz. Muhammed'in yaralanması, Peygamber'in amcası Hz. Hamza'nın ölümü, savaş ganimetlerinin paylaşılması, Kaa'b ve kızının öyküsü ile Müslümanların düşmanı Süfyan bin Halid'in öldürülmesi konuları anlatılmaktadır.  
  
Siyer-i Nebi 16. yüzyılda Sultan III. Murad'ın isteği üzerine Saray nakkaşhanesinde altı cilt olarak hazırlanır. Bugün bir cildi kayıptır, diğerleri ise dünya kütüphanelerine dağılmıştır. İstanbul Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi'nde bulunan bu yazma, adı geçen eserin Dublin Chester Beatty Kütüphanesi'nde (T.419) bulunan dördüncü cildinin 17. yüzyılda yapılmış bir kopyasıdır. Eser minyatür üslubu açısından 17. yüzyıl özelliklerini taşımaktadır.

Hz. Muhammed'in hayatını konu alan 'Siyer-i Nebi'nin 17. yüzyılda kopya edilen bu cildi, konusu, minyatürlerindeki figür üslubu, doğa ve mekân kompozisyonları ile Osmanlı Resim Sanatı içinde önemli bir yere sahiptir.

en.name: Aqueduct across the Wady en-Nawaimeh
description: A bridge with three arches supporting an aqueduct. The pointed style of the arches indicates their construction in the Medieval, probably Mamluk era, in support of sugar cane cultivation, a major activity in this period requiring an irrigation system.
